chapters.name: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter

questions.q: The time period of a simple harmonic oscillator is \(T = 2\pi\sqrt{\frac mk}\). Measured value of mass (\(m\)) of the object is 10 g with an accuracy of 10 mg and time for 50 oscillations of the spring is found to be 60 s using a watch of 2 s resolution. Percentage error in determination of spring constant (\(k\)) is ____ %.
questions.sol: \(k = \dfrac{4\pi^2m}{T^2}\), so \(\dfrac{\Delta k}{k} = \dfrac{\Delta m}{m} + 2\dfrac{\Delta T}{T} = \dfrac{10}{10000} + 2\times\dfrac{2}{60} = 0.1\% + 6.67\% \approx 6.76\%\).

questions.q: The speed of a longitudinal wave in a metallic bar is 400 m/s. If the density and Young's modulus of the bar material are increased by 0.5% and 1%, respectively then the speed of the wave is changed approximately to ____ m/s.
questions.sol: \(v = \sqrt{\dfrac Y\rho}\): \(\dfrac{\Delta v}{v} = \dfrac12(1\% - 0.5\%) = 0.25\%\). \(v \approx 400\times1.0025 = 401\) m/s.

questions.q:
Match List - I with List - II.
List-IList-II
A.Coefficient of viscosityI.\([ML^{-1}T^{-2}]\)
B.Surface tensionII.\([ML^2T^{-2}]\)
C.PressureIII.\([ML^0T^{-2}]\)
D.Surface energyIV.\([ML^{-1}T^{-1}]\)
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.sol: Viscosity \([ML^{-1}T^{-1}]\) (IV); surface tension, force per length, \([MT^{-2}]\) (III); pressure \([ML^{-1}T^{-2}]\) (I); surface energy, an energy, \([ML^2T^{-2}]\) (II).

questions.q: In an experiment, a set of readings are obtained as follows: 1.24 mm, 1.25 mm, 1.23 mm, 1.21 mm. The expected least count of the instrument used in recording these readings is ____ mm.
questions.sol: The readings differ in the second decimal place of a millimetre, so the least count is 0.01 mm.

questions.q:
A particle starts moving from time \(t = 0\) and its coordinate is given as \(x(t) = 4t^3 - 3t\)
A. The particle returns to its original position (origin) 0.866 units later
B. The particle is 1 unit away from origin at its turning point
C. Acceleration of the particle is non-negative
D. The particle is 0.5 units away from origin at its turning point
E. Particle never turns back as acceleration is non-negative
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.sol: \(x = 0\) again at \(t = \dfrac{\sqrt3}{2} = 0.866\) (A true). \(v = 12t^2 - 3 = 0\) at \(t = 0.5\), where \(x = -1\) (B true, D false). \(a = 24t \ge 0\) (C true), yet the particle does turn back (E false).

questions.q: A small block of mass \(m\) slides down from the top of a frictionless inclined surface, while the inclined plane is moving towards left with constant acceleration \(a_0\). The angle between the inclined plane and ground is \(\theta\) and its base length is \(L\). Assuming that initially the small block is at the top of the inclined plane, the time it takes to reach the lowest point of the inclined plane is ____ .
questions.sol: In the wedge frame, a pseudo force \(ma_0\) acts to the right, up the slope. Along the incline: \(a = g\sin\theta - a_0\cos\theta\), over a length \(\dfrac{L}{\cos\theta}\). \(t^2 = \dfrac{2L}{\cos\theta(g\sin\theta - a_0\cos\theta)} = \dfrac{4L}{g\sin2\theta - a_0(1 + \cos2\theta)}\).

questions.q: When the position vector \(\vec r = x\hat i + y\hat j + z\hat k\) changes sign as \(-\vec r\), which one of the following vector will not flip under sign change?
questions.sol: Velocity, momentum and acceleration all flip with \(\vec r\). \(\vec L = \vec r\times\vec p\) has two flipped factors, so it does not change.

questions.q: The mean free path of a molecule of diameter \(5\times10^{-10}\) m at the temperature 41°C and pressure \(1.38\times10^5\) Pa, is given as ____ m. (Given \(k_B = 1.38\times10^{-23}\) J/K).
questions.sol: \(\lambda = \dfrac{k_BT}{\sqrt2\pi d^2P} = \dfrac{1.38\times10^{-23}\times314}{1.414\times3.14\times25\times10^{-20}\times1.38\times10^5} \approx 2.83\times10^{-8} = 2\sqrt2\times10^{-8}\) m.

questions.q: As shown in the figure, a spring is kept in a stretched position with some extension by holding the masses 1 kg and 0.2 kg with a separation more than spring natural length and are released. Assuming the horizontal surface to be frictionless, the angular frequency (in SI unit) of the system is :
questions.sol: Reduced mass \(\mu = \dfrac{1\times0.2}{1.2} = \dfrac16\) kg. \(\omega = \sqrt{\dfrac k\mu} = \sqrt{150\times6} = 30\) rad/s.

questions.q:
Identify the correct statements :
A. Electrostatic field lines form closed loops.
B. The electric field lines point radially outward when charge is greater than zero.
C. The Gauss - Law is valid only for inverse-square force.
D. The work done in moving a charged particle in a static electric field around a closed path is zero.
E. The motion of a particle under Coulomb's force must take place in a plane.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.sol: Electrostatic field lines never form closed loops, so A is false. B, C, D and E are true: the field is conservative, Gauss's law needs an inverse-square force, and a central force keeps motion in one plane.

questions.q: Which one of the following is not a measurable quantity?
questions.sol: Only potential differences can be measured; the absolute potential (voltage) of a point depends on the chosen zero.

questions.q: A Wheatstone bridge is initially at room temperature and all arms of the bridge have same value of resistances (\(R_1 = R_2 = R_3 = R_4\)). When \(R_3\) resistance is heated to some temperature, its resistance value has gone up by 10%. The potential difference (\(V_a - V_b\)) (after \(R_3\) is heated) is ____ V.
questions.sol: Each side branch takes 40 V. \(V_a = 20\) V. With \(R_3 = 1.1R\): \(V_b = 40\times\dfrac{R}{2.1R} \approx 19.05\) V. \(V_a - V_b \approx 0.95\) V.

questions.q:
Identify the correct statements :
A. Effective capacitance of a series combination of capacitors is always smaller than the smallest capacitance of the capacitor in the combination.
B. When a dielectric medium is placed between the charged plates of a capacitor, displacement of charges cannot occur due to insulation property of dielectric.
C. Increasing of area of capacitor plate or decreasing of thickness of dielectric is an alternate method to increase the capacitance.
D. For a point charge, concentric spherical shells centered at the location of the charge are equipotential surfaces.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.sol: A, C and D are true. B is false: a dielectric does get polarised, so its charges are displaced slightly.

questions.q:
A long cylindrical conductor with large cross section carries an electric current distributed uniformly over its cross-section. Magnetic field due to this current is:
A. maximum at either ends of the conductor and minimum at the midpoint
B. maximum at the axis of the conductor
C. minimum at the surface of the conductor
D. minimum at the axis of the conductor
E. same at all points in the cross-section of the conductor
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.sol: Inside, \(B = \dfrac{\mu_0Ir}{2\pi R^2}\): zero on the axis and largest at the surface. Only D is correct.

questions.q: A plane electromagnetic wave is moving in free space with velocity \(c = 3\times10^8\) m/s and its electric field is given as \(\vec E = 54\sin(kz - \omega t)\hat j\) V/m, where \(\hat j\) is the unit vector along \(y\)-axis. The magnetic field vector \(\vec B\) of the wave is :
questions.sol: \(B_0 = \dfrac{E_0}{c} = 1.8\times10^{-7}\) T. The wave travels along \(+\hat k\) with \(\vec E\) along \(\hat j\); \(\hat j\times\vec B\) must point along \(\hat k\), so \(\vec B\) is along \(-\hat i\).

questions.q: A biconvex lens is formed by using two thin planoconvex lenses, as shown in the figure. The refractive index and radius of curved surfaces are also mentioned in figure. When an object is placed on the left side of lens at a distance of 30 cm from the biconvex lens, the magnification of the image will be :
questions.sol: \(\dfrac1f = \dfrac{0.5}{15} + \dfrac{0.2}{12} = \dfrac1{30} + \dfrac1{60} = \dfrac1{20}\). \(u = -30\) cm: \(\dfrac1v = \dfrac1{20} - \dfrac1{30} \Rightarrow v = 60\) cm. \(m = \dfrac vu = -2\).

questions.q: For a transparent prism, if the angle of minimum deviation is equal to its refracting angle, the refractive index \(n\) of the prism satisfies.
questions.sol: \(n = \dfrac{\sin A}{\sin(A/2)} = 2\cos\dfrac A2\). Since \(i = A\) must stay below 90°, \(\dfrac A2 < 45^\circ\): \(\sqrt2 < n < 2\).

questions.q: A nucleus has mass number \(\alpha\) and radius \(R_\alpha\). Another nucleus has mass number \(\beta\) and radius \(R_\beta\). If \(\beta = 8\alpha\) then \(R_\alpha/R_\beta\) is :
questions.sol: \(R \propto A^{1/3}\): \(\dfrac{R_\alpha}{R_\beta} = \left(\dfrac18\right)^{1/3} = 0.5\).

questions.q: Number of photons of equal energy emitted per second by a 6 mW laser source operating at 663 nm is ____ . (Given : \(h = 6.63\times10^{-34}\) J.s and \(c = 3\times10^8\) m/s)
questions.sol: \(E = \dfrac{hc}{\lambda} = \dfrac{6.63\times10^{-34}\times3\times10^8}{663\times10^{-9}} = 3\times10^{-19}\) J. \(N = \dfrac{6\times10^{-3}}{3\times10^{-19}} = 2\times10^{16}\) per second.

questions.q: Two p-n junction diodes \(D_1\) and \(D_2\) are connected as shown in figure. \(A\) and \(B\) are input signals and \(C\) is the output. The given circuit will function as a ____ .
questions.sol: The diodes point towards the inputs. If either input is low, its diode conducts and pulls C low; C is high only when both inputs are high: an AND gate.

questions.q: A fly wheel having mass 3 kg and radius 5 m is free to rotate about a horizontal axis. A string having negligible mass is wound around the wheel and the loose end of the string is connected to 3 kg mass. The mass is kept at rest initially and released. Kinetic energy of the wheel when the mass descends by 3 m is ____ J. (g = 10 m/s²)
questions.sol: Treating the wheel as a disc: \(mgh = \tfrac12mv^2 + \tfrac12\cdot\tfrac12MR^2\dfrac{v^2}{R^2}\): \(90 = 1.5v^2 + 0.75v^2 \Rightarrow v^2 = 40\). Wheel KE \(= 0.75\times40 = 30\) J.

questions.q: A thermodynamic system is taken through the cyclic process \(ABC\) as shown in the figure. The total work done by the system during the cycle \(ABC\) is ____ J.
questions.sol: Clockwise triangle: \(W = \tfrac12\times(5 - 2)\times(300 - 100) = 300\) J.

questions.q: Two tuning forks \(A\) and \(B\) are sounded together giving rise to 8 beats in 2 s. When fork \(A\) is loaded with wax, the beat frequency is reduced to 4 beats in 2 s. If the original frequency of tuning fork \(B\) is 380 Hz then original frequency of tuning fork \(A\) is ____ Hz.
questions.sol: Beats 4 Hz → 2 Hz: \(f_A = 380 \pm 4\). Wax lowers \(f_A\) and the beats fall, so \(f_A\) was above \(f_B\): 384 Hz.

questions.q: An inductor stores 16 J of magnetic field energy and dissipates 32 W of thermal energy due to its resistance when an a.c. current of 2 A (rms) and frequency 50 Hz flows through it. The ratio of inductive reactance to its resistance is ____ . (\(\pi = 3.14\))
questions.sol: \(\tfrac12L(2)^2 = 16 \Rightarrow L = 8\) H. \(R = \dfrac{32}{4} = 8\ \Omega\). \(\dfrac{X_L}{R} = \dfrac{2\times3.14\times50\times8}{8} = 314\).

questions.q: A beam of light consisting of wavelengths 650 nm and 550 nm illuminates the Young's double slits with separation of 2 mm such that the interference fringes are formed on a screen, placed at a distance of 1.2 m from the slits. The least distance of a point from the central maximum, where the bright fringes due to both the wavelengths coincide, is ____ \(\times10^{-5}\) m.

When both jaws of vernier callipers touch each other, zero mark of the vernier scale is right to zero mark of main scale, 4th mark on vernier scale coincides with certain mark on the main scale. While measuring the length of a cylinder, observer observes 15 divisions on main scale and 5th division of vernier scale coincides with a main scale division. Measured length of cylinder is ____ mm. (Least count of Vernier calliper = 0.1 mm)
questions.sol: Zero error \(= +4\times0.1 = +0.4\) mm. Reading \(= 15 + 5\times0.1 = 15.5\) mm. Corrected length \(= 15.5 - 0.4 = 15.1\) mm.

questions.q: Water drops fall from a tap on the floor, 5 m below, at regular intervals of time, the first drop strikes the floor when the sixth drop begins to fall. The height at which the fourth drop will be from ground, at the instant when the first drop strikes the ground is ____ m. (g = 10 m/s²)
questions.sol: Falling 5 m takes 1 s, split into 5 equal gaps of 0.2 s. The 4th drop has fallen for 0.4 s: \(\tfrac12\times10\times0.16 = 0.8\) m, so it is 4.2 m above the ground.

questions.q: A block of mass 5 kg is moving on an inclined plane which makes an angle of 30° with the horizontal. Friction coefficient between the block and inclined plane surface is \(\frac{\sqrt3}{2}\). The force to be applied on the block so that the block will move down without acceleration is ____ N. (g = 10 m/s²).
questions.sol: \(mg\sin30^\circ = 25\) N; maximum friction \(= \dfrac{\sqrt3}{2}\times50\times\dfrac{\sqrt3}{2} = 37.5\) N. Friction is larger, so a push of \(37.5 - 25 = 12.5\) N down the slope is needed.

questions.q: A particle of mass \(m\) falls from rest through a resistive medium having resistive force, \(F = -kv\), where \(v\) is the velocity of the particle and \(k\) is a constant. Which of the following graphs represents velocity (\(v\)) versus time (\(t\))?
questions.sol: \(m\dfrac{dv}{dt} = mg - kv \Rightarrow v = \dfrac{mg}{k}\left(1 - e^{-kt/m}\right)\): rises from zero and levels off at the terminal velocity.

questions.q: Two circular discs of radius each 10 cm are joined at their centres by a rod of length 30 cm and mass 600 gm as shown in figure. If the mass of each disc is 600 gm and applied torque between two discs is \(43\times10^5\) dyne.cm, the angular acceleration of the discs about the given axis \(AB\) is ____ rad/s².
questions.sol: The disc centres are 10 cm and 20 cm from AB. Each disc about a diameter: \(\dfrac{MR^2}{4} = 15000\) g cm². Discs: \(15000 + 600\times100 = 75000\) and \(15000 + 600\times400 = 255000\). Rod (−10 to 20 cm): \(\dfrac{600\times900}{12} + 600\times5^2 = 60000\). Total \(I = 390000\) g cm². \(\alpha = \dfrac{43\times10^5}{3.9\times10^5} \approx 11\) rad/s².

questions.q: Two wires \(A\) and \(B\) made of different materials of lengths 6.0 cm and 5.4 cm, respectively and area of cross sections \(3.0\times10^{-5}\) m² and \(4.5\times10^{-5}\) m², respectively are stretched by the same magnitude under a given load. The ratio of the Young's modulus of \(A\) to that of \(B\) is \(x : 3\). The value of \(x\) is ____
questions.sol: Same load and extension: \(Y \propto \dfrac LA\). \(\dfrac{Y_A}{Y_B} = \dfrac{6/3}{5.4/4.5} = \dfrac{2}{1.2} = \dfrac53\), so \(x = 5\).

questions.q: Which of the following best represents the temperature versus heat supplied graph for water, in the range of −20°C to 120°C?
questions.sol: Ice warms to 0°C, stays flat while melting, water warms to 100°C, stays flat while boiling, then steam warms: two flat parts, at 0°C and 100°C.

questions.q: 10 kg of ice at −10°C is added to 100 kg of water to lower its temperature from 25°C. Consider no heat exchange to surroundings. The decrement to the temperature of water is ____ °C. (specific heat of ice = 2100 J/Kg.°C, specific heat of water = 4200 J/Kg.°C, latent heat of fusion of ice = \(3.36\times10^5\) J/Kg)
questions.sol: Ice to water at 0°C: \(10\times2100\times10 + 10\times3.36\times10^5 = 3.57\times10^6\) J. \(100\times4200(25 - T) = 3.57\times10^6 + 10\times4200T \Rightarrow T = 15\)°C, a drop of 10°C.

questions.q: In the following \(p - V\) diagram the equation of state along the curved path is given by \((V - 2)^2 = 4ap\) where \(a\) is a constant. The total work done in the closed path is ____
questions.sol: Along the curve: \(\int_1^3\dfrac{(V - 2)^2}{4a}dV = \dfrac{1}{6a}\). Back along the top at \(p = \dfrac{1}{4a}\): \(-\dfrac{1}{4a}\times2 = -\dfrac{1}{2a}\). Net \(= -\dfrac{1}{3a}\) (anticlockwise cycle).

questions.q: Two point charges of 1 nC and 2 nC are placed at the two corners of equilateral triangle of side 3 cm. The work done in bringing a charge of 3 nC from infinity to the third corner of the triangle is ____ μJ. (\(\frac{1}{4\pi\epsilon_0} = 9\times10^9\) N·m²/C²)
questions.sol: \(W = \dfrac{kq(q_1 + q_2)}{r} = \dfrac{9\times10^9\times3\times10^{-9}\times3\times10^{-9}}{0.03} = 2.7\times10^{-6}\) J = 2.7 μJ.

questions.q: For the two cells having same EMF \(E\) and internal resistance \(r\), the current passing through the external resistor 6Ω is same when both the cells are connected either in parallel or in series. The value of internal resistance \(r\) is ____ Ω.
questions.sol: \(\dfrac{2E}{6 + 2r} = \dfrac{E}{6 + r/2} \Rightarrow 12 + r = 6 + 2r \Rightarrow r = 6\ \Omega\).

questions.q: In the potentiometer, when the cell in the secondary circuit is shunted with 4Ω resistance, the balance is obtained at the length 120 cm of wire. Now when the same cell is shunted with 12Ω resistance, the balance is shifted to a length of 180 cm. The internal resistance of cell is ____ Ω
questions.sol: Balance length \(\propto \dfrac{ER}{R + r}\). \(\dfrac{4/(4 + r)}{12/(12 + r)} = \dfrac{120}{180} \Rightarrow 12 + r = 8 + 2r \Rightarrow r = 4\ \Omega\).

questions.q: The magnetic field at the centre of a current carrying circular loop of radius \(R\) is 16 μT. The magnetic field at a distance \(x = \sqrt3R\) on its axis from the centre is ____ μT.
Three long straight wires carrying current are arranged mutually parallel as shown in the figure. The force experienced by 15 cm length of wire \(Q\) is ____ . (\(\mu_o = 4\pi\times10^{-7}\) T.m/A)
questions.sol: P (3 A, opposite to Q) repels Q towards R: \(\dfrac{2\times10^{-7}\times3}{0.03} = 2\times10^{-5}\) N/m. R (2 A, same as Q) attracts Q towards R: \(\dfrac{2\times10^{-7}\times2}{0.02} = 2\times10^{-5}\) N/m. Total on 0.15 m \(= 6\times10^{-6}\) N towards R.

questions.q: The electric current in the circuit is given as \(i = i_o(t/T)\). The r.m.s current for the period \(t = 0\) to \(t = T\) is ____ .
questions.sol: \(i_{rms}^2 = \dfrac1T\int_0^T\dfrac{i_o^2t^2}{T^2}dt = \dfrac{i_o^2}{3}\), so \(i_{rms} = \dfrac{i_o}{\sqrt3}\).

questions.q: The electric field of an electromagnetic wave travelling through a medium is given by \(\vec E(x, t) = 25\sin(2.0\times10^{15}t - 10^7x)\hat n\) then the refractive index of the medium is ____ . (All given measurement are in SI units)
questions.sol: \(v = \dfrac\omega k = \dfrac{2\times10^{15}}{10^7} = 2\times10^8\) m/s. \(n = \dfrac cv = 1.5\).

questions.q:
Given below are two statements :
Statement I : A plane wave after passing through prism remains as plane wave but passing through small pin hole may become spherical wave.
Statement II : The curvature of a spherical wave emerging from a slit will increase for increasing slit width.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
o: Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.sol: I is true: a prism keeps a plane wave plane, while a tiny hole acts as a point source. II is false: a wider slit diffracts less, so the curvature decreases.

questions.q: The magnitudes of power of a biconvex lens (refractive index 1.5) and that of a plano-concave lens (refractive index = 1.7) are same. If the curvature of planoconcave lens exactly matches with the curvature of back surface of the biconvex lens, then ratio of radius of curvature of front and back surface of the biconvex lens is
questions.sol: Biconvex: \(0.5\left(\dfrac{1}{R_1} + \dfrac{1}{R_2}\right)\); plano-concave: \(\dfrac{0.7}{R_2}\). Equal: \(\dfrac{0.5}{R_1} = \dfrac{0.2}{R_2} \Rightarrow R_1 : R_2 = 5 : 2\).

questions.q: An atom \({}^8_3X\) is bombarded by shower of fundamental particles and in 10 s this atom absorbed 10 electrons, 10 protons and 9 neutrons. The percentage growth in the surface area of the nucleons is recorded by :
questions.sol: Mass number goes from 8 to \(8 + 10 + 9 = 27\). \(R \propto A^{1/3}\): radius 2 → 3, area 4 → 9, a 125% increase.

questions.q: Assuming in forward bias condition there is a voltage drop of 0.7 V across a silicon diode, the current through diode \(D_1\) in the circuit is ____ mA. (Assume all diodes in the given circuit are identical)
questions.sol: D2 is reverse-biased, so D1 and D3 share the current. \(I = \dfrac{12 - 0.7}{300} = 37.7\) mA, so each carries about 18.8 mA.

questions.q: A solid sphere of radius 10 cm is rotating about an axis which is at a distance 15 cm from its centre. The radius of gyration about this axis is \(\sqrt n\) cm. The value of \(n\) is ____

The displacement of a particle, executing simple harmonic motion with time period \(T\), is expressed as \(x(t) = A\sin\omega t\), where \(A\) is the amplitude. The maximum value of potential energy of this oscillator is found at \(t = T/2\beta\). The value of \(\beta\) is ____ .
questions.sol: Potential energy is maximum at the extreme position, first at \(t = \dfrac T4 = \dfrac{T}{2\beta}\), so \(\beta = 2\).

questions.q: The equivalent resistance between the points \(A\) and \(B\) in the following circuit is \(\frac x5\) Ω. The value of \(x\) is ____ .
questions.sol: Nodes: A–M 6 Ω, M–B 3 Ω, A–N 3 Ω, N–B 6 Ω, M–N 3 Ω. With \(V_A = 1\), \(V_B = 0\): \(V_M = \dfrac37\), \(V_N = \dfrac47\). Current from A \(= \dfrac{4/7}{6} + \dfrac{3/7}{3} = \dfrac{5}{21}\), so \(R = \dfrac{21}{5}\ \Omega\) and \(x = 21\).

questions.q: A convex lens of refractive index 1.5 and focal length \(f = 18\) cm is immersed in water. The difference in focal lengths of the given lens when it is in water and in air is \(\alpha\times f\). The value of \(\alpha\) is ____ . (refractive index of water = 4/3)

The ratio of de Broglie wavelength of a deuteron with kinetic energy \(E\) to that of an alpha particle with kinetic energy \(2E\), is \(n : 1\). The value of \(n\) is ____ . (Assume mass of proton = mass of neutron)
questions.sol: \(\lambda = \dfrac{h}{\sqrt{2mK}}\). \(\dfrac{\lambda_d}{\lambda_\alpha} = \sqrt{\dfrac{4\times2E}{2\times E}} = 2\).

questions.q: In a vernier callipers, 50 vernier scale divisions are equal to 48 main scale divisions. If one main scale division = 0.05 mm, then the least count of the vernier callipers is ____ mm.
questions.sol: LC = 1 MSD − 1 VSD \(= 0.05\left(1 - \dfrac{48}{50}\right) = 0.002\) mm.

questions.q: The velocity (\(v\)) - Distance (\(x\)) graph is shown in figure. Which graph represents acceleration (\(a\)) versus distance (\(x\)) variation of this system?
questions.sol: The graph is \(v = v_0 - kx\). Then \(a = v\dfrac{dv}{dx} = -k(v_0 - kx) = -kv_0 + k^2x\): a straight line with a negative intercept and a positive slope.

questions.q: In case of vertical circular motion of a particle by a thread of length \(r\) if the tension in the thread is zero at an angle 30° shown in figure, the velocity at the bottom point (\(A\)) of the circular path is (\(g\) = gravitational acceleration)
questions.sol: The particle is \(\dfrac r2\) above the centre and the radial part of gravity is \(g\sin30^\circ\). With \(T = 0\): \(v^2 = \dfrac{gr}{2}\). From the bottom it rose \(\dfrac{3r}{2}\): \(u^2 = \dfrac{gr}{2} + 3gr = \dfrac72gr\).

questions.q: A flexible chain of mass \(m\) hangs between two fixed points at the same level. The inclination of the chain with the horizontal at the two points of support is 30°. Considering the equilibrium of each half of the chain, the tension of the chain at the lowest point is ____ .
questions.sol: Supports: \(2T\sin30^\circ = mg \Rightarrow T = mg\). At the lowest point the tension equals the horizontal component \(T\cos30^\circ = \dfrac{\sqrt3}{2}mg\).

questions.q: A thin uniform rod (\(X\)) of mass \(M\) and length \(L\) is pivoted at a height \(\left(\frac L3\right)\) as shown in the figure. The rod is allowed to fall from a vertical position and lie horizontally on the table. The angular velocity of this rod when it hits the table top, is ____ . (\(g\) = gravitational acceleration)
questions.sol: The centre of mass is \(\dfrac L6\) above the pivot and falls to the pivot level. \(I = \dfrac{ML^2}{12} + M\left(\dfrac L6\right)^2 = \dfrac{ML^2}{9}\). \(\dfrac12\cdot\dfrac{ML^2}{9}\omega^2 = Mg\dfrac L6 \Rightarrow \omega = \sqrt{\dfrac{3g}{L}}\).

questions.q: A cubical block of density \(\rho_b = 600\) kg/m³ floats in a liquid of density \(\rho_e = 900\) kg/m³. If the height of block is \(H = 8.0\) cm then height of the submerged part is ____ cm.
questions.sol: \(h = H\dfrac{\rho_b}{\rho_e} = 8\times\dfrac{600}{900} \approx 5.3\) cm.

questions.q: 10 mole of an ideal gas is undergoing the process shown in the figure. The heat involved in the process from \(P_1\) to \(P_2\) is \(\alpha\) Joule (\(P_1 = 21.7\) Pa and \(P_2 = 30\) Pa, \(C_v = 21\) J/K.mol, \(R = 8.3\) J/mol.K). The value of \(\alpha\) is ____ .
questions.sol: \(P_1 \to P_2\) is at constant volume (\(V = 1\) m³): \(Q = nC_v\Delta T = \dfrac{C_v}{R}V\Delta P = \dfrac{21}{8.3}\times1\times8.3 = 21\) J.

questions.q: The fifth harmonic of a closed organ pipe is found to be in unison with the first harmonic of an open pipe. The ratio of lengths of closed pipe to that of the open pipe is \(\frac5x\). The value of \(x\) is
questions.sol: \(\dfrac{5v}{4L_c} = \dfrac{v}{2L_o} \Rightarrow \dfrac{L_c}{L_o} = \dfrac52\), so \(x = 2\).

questions.q: A point source is kept at the center of a spherically enclosed detector. If the volume of the detector increased by 8 times, the intensity will
questions.sol: Volume ×8 means radius ×2. \(I \propto \dfrac{1}{r^2}\), so the intensity falls 4 times.

questions.q: The reading of the ammeter (\(A\)) in steady state in the following circuit (assuming negligible internal resistance of the ammeter) is ____ A.
questions.sol: No current flows through the capacitor branch. From the node after 1 Ω, current goes either through the left 8 Ω, or through 4 Ω and the two 8 Ω in parallel (4 + 4 = 8 Ω), returning via the ammeter. Total \(R = 1 + 4 = 5\ \Omega\), \(I = 2\) A, shared equally: the ammeter reads 1 A.

questions.q: A moving coil galvanometer of resistance 100Ω shows a full scale deflection for a current of 1 mA. The value of resistance required to convert this galvanometer into an ammeter, showing full scale deflection for a current of 5 mA, is ____ Ω
questions.sol: \(S = \dfrac{I_gG}{I - I_g} = \dfrac{1\times100}{4} = 25\ \Omega\).

questions.q: A regular hexagon is formed by six wires each of resistance \(r\) Ω and the corners are joined to the centre by wires of same resistance. If the current enters at one corner and leaves at the opposite corner, the equivalent resistance of the hexagon between the two opposite corners will be
questions.sol: By symmetry the centre is at half the potential. With \(V_0 = 1\), \(V_3 = 0\), node 1 gives \(3V_1 = 1 + V_2 + \tfrac12\) with \(V_2 = 1 - V_1\), so \(V_1 = 0.625\). Current from the input corner \(= \dfrac{2(0.375) + 0.5}{r} = \dfrac{1.25}{r}\), so \(R = \dfrac45r\).

questions.q: Three parallel plate capacitors each with area \(A\) and separation \(d\) are filled with two dielectrics (\(k_1\) and \(k_2\)) in the following fashion. Which of the following is true? (\(k_1 > k_2\))

Two identical circular loops \(P\) and \(Q\) each of radius \(r\) are lying in parallel planes such that they have common axis. The current through \(P\) and \(Q\) are \(I\) and \(4I\) respectively in clockwise direction as seen from \(O\). The net magnetic field at \(O\) is :
questions.sol: Each loop is \(r\) from O: \(B = \dfrac{\mu_0Ir^2}{2(2r^2)^{3/2}} = \dfrac{\mu_0I}{4\sqrt2r}\). Clockwise as seen from O, each field points away from O. They are opposite, so the net field is \(\dfrac{3\mu_0I}{4\sqrt2r}\), towards Q (the larger current).

questions.q: In the Young's double slit experiment the intensity produced by each one of the individual slits is \(I_o\). The distance between two slits is 2 mm. The distance of screen from slits is 10 m. The wavelength of light is 6000 Å. The intensity of light on the screen in front of one of the slits is ____
questions.sol: In front of a slit, \(y = \dfrac d2 = 1\) mm. \(\Delta = \dfrac{yd}{D} = 2\times10^{-7}\) m \(= \dfrac\lambda3\), so \(\phi = \dfrac{2\pi}{3}\). \(I = 4I_o\cos^2\dfrac\pi3 = I_o\).

questions.q: Distance between an object and three times magnified real image is 40 cm. The focal length of the mirror used is ____ cm.
questions.sol: Real image, \(v = 3u\), and \(|v| - |u| = 40\) cm, so \(u = -20\) cm and \(v = -60\) cm. \(\dfrac1f = -\dfrac1{60} - \dfrac1{20} \Rightarrow f = -15\) cm.

questions.q: Five persons \(P_1, P_2, P_3, P_4\) and \(P_5\) recorded object distance (\(u\)) and image distance (\(v\)) using same convex lens having power +5 D as (25, 96), (30, 62), (35, 37), (45, 35) and (50, 32) respectively. Identify correct statement
o: Readings recorded by \(P_3\) and \(P_2\) persons are incorrect
Readings recorded by all persons are correct
Readings recorded by \(P_3\) person are incorrect
Readings recorded by \(P_4\) and \(P_5\) persons are incorrect
questions.sol: \(f = 20\) cm. Expected \(v\): 100, 60, 46.7, 36, 33.3 cm. Only P3's reading (37 instead of about 47) is far off.

questions.q:
The binding energy for the following nuclear reactions are expressed in MeV.
\({}^3_2\text{He} + {}^1_0n \to {}^4_2\text{He} + 20\) MeV
\({}^4_2\text{He} + {}^1_0n \to {}^5_2\text{He} - 0.9\) MeV
If \(X_3, X_4, X_5\) denote the stability of \({}_2\text{He}^3, {}_2\text{He}^4\) and \({}_2\text{He}^5\), respectively, then the correct order is :
questions.sol: Adding a neutron to He-3 releases 20 MeV, so He-4 is much more stable than He-3. Forming He-5 needs 0.9 MeV, so He-5 is less stable than He-4, but its total binding energy is still far above He-3's: \(X_4 > X_5 > X_3\).

questions.q: When a light of a given wavelength falls on a metallic surface the stopping potential for photoelectrons is 3.2 V. If a second light having wavelength twice of first light is used, the stopping potential drops to 0.7 V. The wavelength of first light is ____ m. (\(h = 6.63\times10^{-34}\) J.s, \(e = 1.6\times10^{-19}\) C, \(c = 3\times10^8\) m/s)
questions.sol: \(e(3.2 - 0.7) = \dfrac{hc}{\lambda} - \dfrac{hc}{2\lambda} = \dfrac{hc}{2\lambda}\). \(\lambda = \dfrac{hc}{2\times2.5e} = \dfrac{1.243\times10^{-6}}{5} \approx 2.5\times10^{-7}\) m.

questions.q: Identify the correct truth table of the given logic circuit.
questions.sol: The top gate gives \(A\cdot A = A\); the lower path gives \(\overline{AB}\). Output \(Y = A\cdot\overline{AB} = A\bar B\): 1 only for \(A = 1\), \(B = 0\).

questions.q: A uniform solid cylinder of length \(L\) and radius \(R\) has moment of inertia about its axis equal to \(I_1\). A small co-centric cylinder of length \(L/2\) and radius \(R/3\) carved from this cylinder has moment of inertia about its axis equals to \(I_2\). The ratio \(I_1/I_2\) is ____ .
questions.sol: \(I = \dfrac12MR^2\) with \(M \propto LR^2\). The small cylinder has \(\dfrac12\times\dfrac19 = \dfrac1{18}\) of the mass and \(\dfrac19\) of \(R^2\): \(\dfrac{I_1}{I_2} = 18\times9 = 162\).

questions.q: A soap bubble of surface tension 0.04 N/m is blown to a diameter of 7 cm. If \((15000 - x)\) μJ of work is done in blowing it further to make its diameter 14 cm, then the value of \(x\) is ____ . (\(\pi = 22/7\))

When 300 J of heat given to an ideal gas with \(C_p = \frac72R\) its temperature raises from 20°C to 50°C keeping its volume constant. The mass of the gas is (approximately) ____ g. (\(R = 8.314\) J/mol.K)
questions.sol: \(C_v = \dfrac52R\). \(n = \dfrac{Q}{C_v\Delta T} = \dfrac{300}{2.5\times8.314\times30} \approx 0.481\) mol. The key's answer, 481, is this number × 1000.
questions.note: Bonus question: it asks for a mass in grams but gives no molar mass, so it cannot be answered as printed. Full marks are given to everyone. The amount of gas works out to 0.481 mol.

questions.q: A point charge \(q = 1\) μC is located at a distance 2 cm from one end of a thin insulating wire of length 10 cm having a charge \(Q = 24\) μC, distributed uniformly along its length, as shown in figure. Force between \(q\) and wire is ____ N. (Use : \(\frac{1}{4\pi\epsilon_0} = 9\times10^9\) N·m²/C²)
questions.sol: Force between a point charge on the axis and a uniformly charged rod: \(F = \dfrac{kqQ}{a(a + L)} = \dfrac{9\times10^9\times10^{-6}\times24\times10^{-6}}{0.02\times0.12} = 90\) N.

questions.q: In a meter bridge experiment to determine the value of unknown resistance, first the resistances 2Ω and 3Ω are connected in the left and right gaps of the bridge and the null point is obtained at a distance \(l\) cm from the left. Now when an unknown resistance \(x\) Ω is connected in parallel to 3Ω resistance, the null point is shifted by 10 cm to the right of wire. The value of unknown resistance \(x\) is ____ Ω.
questions.sol: \(\dfrac23 = \dfrac{l}{100 - l} \Rightarrow l = 40\) cm. New null point 50 cm: \(\dfrac{2}{R'} = 1 \Rightarrow R' = 2 = \dfrac{3x}{3 + x} \Rightarrow x = 6\ \Omega\).

questions.q:
Match the LIST-I with LIST-II
List-IList-II
A.Magnetic inductionI.\(MLT^{-2}A^{-2}\)
B.Magnetic fluxII.\(ML^2T^{-2}A^{-2}\)
C.Magnetic permeabilityIII.\(ML^0T^{-2}A^{-1}\)
D.Self inductanceIV.\(ML^2T^{-2}A^{-1}\)
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.sol: B (tesla) \(= [MT^{-2}A^{-1}]\) (III); flux (weber) \(= [ML^2T^{-2}A^{-1}]\) (IV); permeability (H/m) \(= [MLT^{-2}A^{-2}]\) (I); inductance (henry) \(= [ML^2T^{-2}A^{-2}]\) (II).

questions.q: A boy throws a ball into air at 45° from the horizontal to land it on a roof of a building of height \(H\). If the ball attains maximum height in 2 s and lands on the building in 3 s after launch, then value of \(H\) is ____ m. (g = 10 m/s²)
questions.sol: Time to the top is 2 s, so \(u_y = 20\) m/s. At \(t = 3\) s: \(H = 20\times3 - 5\times9 = 15\) m.

questions.q: Two masses 400 g and 350 g are suspended from the ends of a light string passing over a heavy pulley of radius 2 cm. When released from rest the heavier mass is observed to fall 81 cm in 9 s. The rotational inertia of the pulley is ____ kg·m². (g = 9.8 m/s²)
questions.sol: \(s = \tfrac12at^2 \Rightarrow a = \dfrac{2\times0.81}{81} = 0.02\) m/s². \(a = \dfrac{(0.4 - 0.35)g}{0.75 + I/r^2} \Rightarrow 0.75 + \dfrac{I}{4\times10^{-4}} = 24.5 \Rightarrow I = 9.5\times10^{-3}\) kg m².

questions.q: A brass wire of length 2 m and radius 1 mm at 27°C is held taut between two rigid supports. Initially it was cooled to a temperature of −43°C creating a tension \(T\) in the wire. The temperature to which the wire has to be cooled in order to increase the tension in it to 1.4\(T\), is ____ °C.
questions.sol: Thermal tension is proportional to the temperature drop: 70°C gives \(T\), so \(1.4T\) needs 98°C. Final temperature \(= 27 - 98 = -71\)°C.

questions.q: Density of water at 4°C and 20°C are 1000 kg/m³ and 998 kg/m³ respectively. The increase in internal energy of 4 kg of water when it is heated from 4°C to 20°C is ____ J. (specific heat capacity of water = 4.2 kJ/kg K and 1 atmospheric pressure = 10⁵ Pa )
questions.sol: \(Q = 4\times4200\times16 = 268800\) J. \(W = P\Delta V = 10^5\left(\dfrac{4}{998} - \dfrac{4}{1000}\right) \approx 0.8\) J. \(\Delta U = Q - W = 268799.2\) J.

questions.q: A cylindrical block of mass \(M\) and area of cross section \(A\) is floating in a liquid of density \(\rho\) and with its axis vertical. When depressed a little and released the block starts oscillating. The period of oscillation is ____
questions.sol: Restoring force for a dip \(x\): \(\rho Agx\), so \(k = \rho Ag\) and \(T = 2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{M}{\rho Ag}}\).

questions.q: A spring of force constant 15 N/m is cut into two pieces. If the ratio of their length is 1 : 3, then the force constant of smaller piece is ____ N/m.
questions.sol: \(k \propto \dfrac1L\). The smaller piece is a quarter of the length: \(k = 4\times15 = 60\) N/m.

questions.q: Three masses 200 kg, 300 kg and 400 kg are placed at the vertices of an equilateral triangle with sides 20 m. They are rearranged on the vertices of a bigger triangle of side 25 m and with the same centre. The work done in this process ____ J. (Gravitational constant \(G = 6.7\times10^{-11}\) N m²/kg² )
questions.sol: \(U = -\dfrac{G\sum m_im_j}{a}\) with \(\sum m_im_j = 260000\) kg². \(W = G\times260000\left(\dfrac{1}{20} - \dfrac{1}{25}\right) = 6.7\times10^{-11}\times2600 \approx 1.74\times10^{-7}\) J.

questions.q: The electrostatic potential in a charged spherical region of radius \(r\) varies as \(V = ar^3 + b\), where \(a\) and \(b\) are constants. The total charge in the sphere of unit radius is \(\alpha\times\pi a\epsilon_0\). The value of \(\alpha\) is ____ . (permittivity of vacuum is \(\epsilon_0\) )
questions.sol: \(E = -\dfrac{dV}{dr} = -3ar^2\). Gauss's law at \(r = 1\): \(Q = 4\pi\epsilon_0r^2E = -12\pi a\epsilon_0\), so \(\alpha = -12\).

questions.q: There are three concentric conducting spherical shells \(A, B\) and \(C\) of radii \(a, b\) and \(c\) respectively ( \(c > b > a\) ) and they are charged with charge \(q_1, q_2\) and \(q_3\) respectively. The potentials of the spheres \(A, B\) and \(C\) respectively, are :
questions.sol: A shell's potential is \(k\dfrac{q}{R}\) at or inside it and \(k\dfrac qr\) outside. A: \(k\left(\dfrac{q_1}{a} + \dfrac{q_2}{b} + \dfrac{q_3}{c}\right)\); B: \(k\left(\dfrac{q_1 + q_2}{b} + \dfrac{q_3}{c}\right)\); C: \(k\dfrac{q_1 + q_2 + q_3}{c}\).

questions.q: Three charges \(+2q, +3q\) and \(-4q\) are situated at \((0, -3a), (2a, 0)\) and \((-2a, 0)\) respectively in the \(xy\) plane. The resultant dipole moment about origin is ____ .

Two resistors of 100Ω each are connected in series with a 9 V battery. A voltmeter of 400Ω resistance is connected to measure the voltage drop across one of the resistors. The voltmeter reading is ____ V.
questions.sol: \(100\,\|\,400 = 80\ \Omega\), total \(180\ \Omega\), current \(0.05\) A. Voltmeter reads \(0.05\times80 = 4\) V.

questions.q: Two resistors 2Ω and 3Ω are connected in the gaps of bridge as shown in figure. The null point is obtained with the contact of jockey at some point on wire \(XY\). When an unknown resistor is connected in parallel with 3Ω resistor, the null point is shifted by 22.5 cm toward \(Y\). The resistance of unknown resistor is ____ Ω.
questions.sol: Initially \(\dfrac23 = \dfrac{l}{100 - l} \Rightarrow l = 40\) cm. After shifting to 62.5 cm: \(\dfrac{2}{R'} = \dfrac{62.5}{37.5} \Rightarrow R' = 1.2\ \Omega = 3\,\|\,X \Rightarrow X = 2\ \Omega\).

questions.q: For the series LCR circuit connected with 220 V, 50 Hz a.c source as shown in the figure, the power factor is \(\frac{\alpha}{10}\). The value of \(\alpha\) is ____ .

Match the LIST-I with LIST-II
List-IList-II
A.Radio-waveI.is produced by Magnetron valve
B.Micro-waveII.due to change in the vibrational modes of atoms
C.Infrared-waveIII.due to inner shell electrons moving from higher energy level to lower energy level
D.X-rayIV.due to rapid acceleration of electrons
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.sol: Radio waves come from accelerating electrons in aerials (IV); microwaves from magnetrons (I); infrared from molecular vibrations (II); X-rays from inner-shell electron transitions (III).

questions.q: An unpolarised light is incident at an interface of two dielectric media having refractive indices of 2 (incident medium) and \(2\sqrt3\) (medium) respectively. To satisfy the condition that reflected and refracted rays are perpendicular to each other, the angle of incidence is ____
questions.sol: Brewster's law: \(\tan i = \dfrac{2\sqrt3}{2} = \sqrt3 \Rightarrow i = 60^\circ\).

questions.q: The exit surface of a prism with refractive index \(n\) is coated with a material having refractive index \(\frac n2\). When this prism is set for minimum angle of deviation, it exactly meets the condition of critical angle. The prism angle is ____ .
questions.sol: At minimum deviation \(r = \dfrac A2\) at each face. At the exit, \(\sin C = \dfrac{n/2}{n} = \dfrac12 \Rightarrow C = 30^\circ = \dfrac A2\), so \(A = 60^\circ\).

questions.q: In a microscope of tube length 10 cm two convex lenses are arranged with focal length of 2 cm and 5 cm. Total magnification obtained with this system for normal adjustment is \((5)^k\). The value of \(k\) is ____ .
questions.sol: \(M = \dfrac{L}{f_o}\cdot\dfrac{D}{f_e} = \dfrac{10}{2}\times\dfrac{25}{5} = 25 = 5^2\), so \(k = 2\).

questions.q: Two electrons are moving in orbits of two hydrogen like atoms with speeds \(3\times10^5\) m/s and \(2.5\times10^5\) m/s respectively. If the radii of these orbits are nearly same then the possible order of energy states are ____ respectively.
questions.sol: For hydrogen-like atoms \(r \propto \dfrac{n^2}{Z}\) and \(v \propto \dfrac Zn\). Equal radii mean \(Z \propto n^2\), so \(v \propto n\): \(\dfrac{n_1}{n_2} = \dfrac{3}{2.5} = \dfrac65\).

questions.q:
Given below are two statements :
Statement I : For all elements, greater the mass of the nucleus, greater is the binding energy per nucleon.
Statement II : For all elements, nuclei with less binding energy per nucleon transforms to nuclei with greater binding energy per nucleon.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below
o: Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
questions.sol: Binding energy per nucleon peaks near iron and falls for heavier nuclei, so I is false. Nuclei change (by fission or fusion) towards higher binding energy per nucleon, so II is true.

questions.q: In the given figure the blocks \(A, B\) and \(C\) weigh 4 kg, 6 kg and 8 kg respectively. The co-efficient of sliding friction between any two surfaces is 0.5. The force \(\vec F\) required to slide the block \(C\) with constant speed is ____ N. (Use \(g = 10\) m/s² )
questions.sol: Ground friction on C: \(0.5\times180 = 90\) N. B–C friction: \(0.5\times100 = 50\) N, acting on both B and C. The string tension equals the friction holding back B: 50 N if A moves with B, giving \(F = 90 + 50 + 50 = 190\) N; adding A–B friction (20 N) to B's side gives \(T = 70\) N and \(F = 210\) N.
questions.note: Two answers are accepted: 190 N (block A moves along with B) or 210 N (friction on A is also counted).

questions.q: Sixty four rain drops of radius 1 mm each falling down with a terminal velocity of 10 cm/s coalesce to form a bigger drop. The terminal velocity of bigger drop is ____ cm/s.
questions.sol: 64 drops make one drop of radius 4 mm. \(v_t \propto r^2\): \(10\times16 = 160\) cm/s.

questions.q: A gas of certain mass filled in a closed cylinder at a pressure of 3.23 kPa has temperature 50°C. The gas is now heated to double its temperature. The modified pressure is ____ Pa.
questions.sol: At constant volume \(P \propto T\). Doubling the Celsius temperature (323 K → 373 K): \(P = 3.23\times\dfrac{373}{323} = 3.73\) kPa = 3730 Pa. Doubling the absolute temperature: 6460 Pa.
questions.note: Two answers are accepted: 3730 Pa if the Celsius temperature is doubled (to 100°C), or 6460 Pa if the absolute temperature is doubled.

questions.q: A short bar magnet placed with its axis at 30° with an external field of 800 Gauss, experiences a torque of 0.016 N.m. The work done in moving it from most stable to most unstable position is \(\alpha\times10^{-3}\) J. The value of \(\alpha\) is ____ .
questions.sol: \(\tau = mB\sin30^\circ \Rightarrow m = \dfrac{0.016}{0.08\times0.5} = 0.4\) A m². Work from stable to unstable \(= 2mB = 2\times0.4\times0.08 = 64\times10^{-3}\) J.

questions.q: A voltage regulating circuit consisting of Zener diode, having break-down voltage of 10 V and maximum power dissipation of 0.4 W, is operated at 15 V. The approximate value of protective resistance in this circuit is ____ Ω.
questions.sol: Maximum Zener current \(= \dfrac{0.4}{10} = 0.04\) A. \(R = \dfrac{15 - 10}{0.04} = 125\ \Omega\).

questions.q: To compare EMF of two cells using potentiometer the balancing lengths obtained are 200 cm and 150 cm. The least count of scale is 1 cm. The percentage error in the ratio of EMFs is ____
questions.sol: \(\dfrac{E_1}{E_2} = \dfrac{l_1}{l_2}\), so the percentage error is \(\left(\dfrac{1}{200} + \dfrac{1}{150}\right)\times100 \approx 1.17\%\).

questions.q: A paratrooper jumps from an aeroplane and opens a parachute after 2 s of free fall and starts decelerating with 3 m/s². At 10 m height from ground, while descending with the help of parachute, the speed of paratrooper is 5 m/s. The initial height of the airplane is ____ m. (g = 10 m/s²)
questions.sol: Free fall for 2 s: \(v = 20\) m/s after falling 20 m. Then \(5^2 = 20^2 - 2\times3\times s \Rightarrow s = 62.5\) m, ending 10 m above the ground. Height \(= 20 + 62.5 + 10 = 92.5\) m.

questions.q: A block is sliding down with constant velocity on an inclined plane of slope \(\theta\) and at an instant \(t = 0\) this block is given an upward momentum so that it starts moving up on the inclined surface with velocity \(u\). The distance (\(S\)) travelled by the block before its velocity become zero, is ____ . (g = gravitational acceleration)
questions.sol: Sliding down at constant velocity means \(\mu = \tan\theta\). Going up, the deceleration is \(g\sin\theta + \mu g\cos\theta = 2g\sin\theta\), so \(S = \dfrac{u^2}{4g\sin\theta}\).

questions.q: A bead \(P\) sliding on a frictionless semi-circular string (\(ACB\)) and it is at point \(S\) at \(t = 0\) and at this instant the horizontal component of its velocity is \(v\). Another bead \(Q\) of the same mass as \(P\) is ejected from point \(A\) at \(t = 0\) along the horizontal string \(AB\), with the speed \(v\), friction between the beads and the respective strings may be neglected in both cases. Let \(t_P\) and \(t_Q\) be the respective times taken by beads \(P\) and \(Q\) to reach the point \(B\), then the relation between \(t_P\) and \(t_Q\) is
questions.sol: P starts at S, already ahead of A horizontally, and gravity speeds it up on the way down, so its horizontal progress outruns Q's steady \(v\) for most of the path: \(t_P < t_Q\).

questions.q: A body of mass 14 kg initially at rest explodes and breaks into three fragments of masses in the ratio 2 : 2 : 3. The two pieces of equal masses fly off perpendicular to each other with a speed of 18 m/s each. The velocity of the heavier fragment is ____ m/s.
questions.sol: Masses 4, 4 and 6 kg. The two 4 kg pieces carry \(4\times18\sqrt2 = 72\sqrt2\) kg m/s together; the 6 kg piece balances it: \(v = \dfrac{72\sqrt2}{6} = 12\sqrt2\) m/s.

questions.q: A small metallic sphere of diameter 2 mm and density 10.5 g/cm³ is dropped in glycerine having viscosity 10 Poise and density 1.5 g/cm³ respectively. The terminal velocity attained by the sphere is ____ cm/s. (\(\pi = \frac{22}{7}\) and \(g = 10\) m/s²)
questions.sol: In CGS: \(v = \dfrac{2r^2(\rho - \sigma)g}{9\eta} = \dfrac{2\times(0.1)^2\times9\times1000}{9\times10} = 2\) cm/s.

questions.q: An air bubble of volume 2.9 cm³ rises from the bottom of a swimming pool of 5 m deep. At the bottom of the pool water temperature is 17°C. The volume of the bubble when it reaches the surface, where the water temperature is 27°C, is ____ cm³. ( g = 10 m/s², density of water = 10³ kg/m³, and 1 atm pressure is 10⁵ Pa )
questions.sol: Pressure at the bottom \(= 10^5 + 5\times10^4 = 1.5\times10^5\) Pa. \(V_2 = 2.9\times\dfrac{1.5\times10^5}{10^5}\times\dfrac{300}{290} = 4.5\) cm³.

questions.q: One mole of an ideal diatomic gas expands from volume \(V\) to \(2V\) isothermally at a temperature 27°C and does \(W\) joule of work. If the gas undergoes same magnitude of expansion adiabatically from 27°C doing the same amount of work \(W\), then its final temperature will be (close to) ____ °C. (\(\log_e2 = 0.693\))
questions.sol: \(W = RT\ln2 = 8.314\times300\times0.693 \approx 1729\) J. Adiabatic: \(W = \tfrac52R\Delta T \Rightarrow \Delta T \approx 83\) K, so \(T = 300 - 83 = 217\) K \(\approx -56\)°C.

questions.q: The internal energy of a monoatomic gas is 3nRT. One mole of helium is kept in a cylinder having internal cross section area of 17 cm² and fitted with a light movable frictionless piston. The gas is heated slowly by suppling 126 J heat. If the temperature rises by 4°C, then the piston will move ____ cm. (atmospheric pressure = 10⁵ Pa )
questions.sol: With \(U = 3nRT\): \(\Delta U = 3\times8.3\times4 \approx 99.6\) J, so \(W = 126 - 99.6 = 26.4\) J \(= P A x\). \(x = \dfrac{26.4}{10^5\times17\times10^{-4}} \approx 0.155\) m = 15.5 cm.

questions.q: Two short dipoles \((A, B)\), \(A\) having charges ±2μC and length 1 cm and \(B\) having charges ±4μC and length 1 cm are placed with their centres 80 cm apart as shown in the figure. The electric field at a point \(P\), equi-distant from the centres of both dipoles is ____ N/C.
questions.sol: P is 40 cm from both centres: on the axis of A (\(p_A = 2\times10^{-8}\) C m) and on the equatorial line of B (\(p_B = 4\times10^{-8}\) C m). \(E_A = \dfrac{2kp_A}{r^3} = 5625\) N/C and \(E_B = \dfrac{kp_B}{r^3} = 5625\) N/C, at right angles: \(E = 5625\sqrt2 = \dfrac{9}{16}\sqrt2\times10^4\) N/C.

questions.q: Two charges 7μC and −2μC are placed at \((-9, 0, 0)\) cm and \((9, 0, 0)\) cm respectively in an external field \(E = \frac{A}{r^2}\hat r\), where \(A = 9\times10^5\) N/C.m². Considering the potential at infinity is 0, the electrostatic energy of the configuration is ____ J.
questions.sol: The external field has potential \(V = \dfrac Ar = 10^7\) V at \(r = 0.09\) m. Energy \(= (q_1 + q_2)V + \dfrac{kq_1q_2}{0.18} = 5\times10^{-6}\times10^7 - 0.7 = 49.3\) J.

questions.q: A parallel plate capacitor with plate separation 5 mm is charged by a battery. On introducing a mica sheet of 2 mm and maintaining the connections of the plates with the terminals of the battery, it is found that it draws 25% more charge from the battery. The dielectric constant of mica is ____
questions.sol: \(\dfrac{C'}{C} = \dfrac{5}{3 + 2/K} = 1.25 \Rightarrow 3 + \dfrac2K = 4 \Rightarrow K = 2\).

questions.q: The current passing through a conducting loop in the form of equilateral triangle of side \(4\sqrt3\) cm is 2 A. The magnetic field at its centroid is \(\alpha\times10^{-5}\) T. The value of \(\alpha\) is ____ . (Given : \(\mu_0 = 4\pi\times10^{-7}\) SI units)
questions.sol: The centroid is \(d = \dfrac{a}{2\sqrt3} = 2\) cm from each side. Each side: \(\dfrac{\mu_0I}{4\pi d}(2\sin60^\circ) = \sqrt3\times10^{-5}\) T. Three sides: \(3\sqrt3\times10^{-5}\) T.

questions.q: A circular loop of radius 7 cm is placed in uniform magnetic field of 0.2 T directed perpendicular to plane of loop. The loop is converted into a square loop in 0.5 s. The EMF induced in the loop is ____ mV.
questions.sol: Perimeter \(2\pi\times7 = 44\) cm, so the square has side 11 cm. Area change \(= 154 - 121 = 33\) cm². \(\varepsilon = \dfrac{0.2\times33\times10^{-4}}{0.5} = 1.32\) mV.

questions.q: Suppose a long solenoid of 100 cm length, radius 2 cm having 500 turns per unit length, carries a current \(I = 10\sin(\omega t)\) A, where \(\omega = 1000\) rad./s. A circular conducting loop (\(B\)) of radius 1 cm coaxially slided through the solenoid at a speed \(v = 1\) cm/s. The r.m.s. current through the loop when the coil \(B\) is inserted 10 cm inside the solenoid is \(\frac{\alpha}{\sqrt2}\)μA. The value of \(\alpha\) is ____ . [Resistance of the loop = 10Ω ]
questions.sol: \(\varepsilon_0 = \mu_0n\pi r^2\dfrac{dI}{dt} = 4\pi\times10^{-7}\times500\times\pi(0.01)^2\times10^4 \approx 1.97\times10^{-3}\) V. Peak current \(\approx 197\ \mu A\), rms \(= \dfrac{197}{\sqrt2}\ \mu A\).

questions.q: The ratio of speeds of electromagnetic waves in vacuum and a medium, having dielectric constant \(k = 3\) and permeability of \(\mu = 2\mu_0\), is ( \(\mu_0\) = permeability of vacuum)
questions.sol: \(v = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{\mu\epsilon}}\), so \(\dfrac cv = \sqrt{2\times3} = \sqrt6\).

questions.q: When an unpolarized light falls at a particular angle on a glass plate (placed in air), it is observed that the reflected beam is linearly polarized. The angle of refracted beam with respect to the normal is ____ . (\(\tan^{-1}(1.52) = 57.7°\), refractive indices of air and glass are 1.00 and 1.52, respectively.)
questions.sol: Brewster angle \(57.7^\circ\); the reflected and refracted rays are perpendicular, so the refraction angle is \(90^\circ - 57.7^\circ = 32.3^\circ\).

questions.q: (Multiple correct answers) A prism of angle 75° and refractive index \(\sqrt3\) is coated with thin film of refractive index 1.5 only at the back exit surface. To have total internal reflection at the back exit surface the incident angle must be ____ (\(\sin15° = 0.25\) and \(\sin25° = 0.43\))
questions.sol: TIR at the film needs \(\sqrt3\sin r_2 > 1.5 \Rightarrow r_2 > 60^\circ \Rightarrow r_1 < 15^\circ \Rightarrow \sin i < \sqrt3\sin15^\circ \approx 0.43 \Rightarrow i < 25^\circ\). Options (A), (B) and (C) all satisfy this.
questions.note: Bonus question: three options, (A), (B) and (C), are all correct, so full marks are given to everyone.

questions.q: Which of the following pair of nuclei are isobars of the element?
questions.sol: Isobars have the same mass number: \({}^3_1\)H and \({}^3_2\)He.

questions.q: For the given logic gate circuit, which of the following is the correct truth table?
questions.sol: \(z = \overline{n\cdot(n + m)} = \bar n\). So \(z = 1\) when \(n = 0\) and \(z = 0\) when \(n = 1\): table (A).

questions.q: A ball of radius \(r\) and density \(\rho\) dropped through a viscous liquid of density \(\sigma\) and viscosity \(\eta\) attains its terminal velocity at time \(t\), given by \(t = A\rho^ar^b\eta^c\sigma^d\), where \(A\) is a constant and \(a, b, c\) and \(d\) are integers. The value of \(\frac{b+c}{a+d}\) is ____ .
questions.sol: Matching dimensions of time: \(c = -1\), \(a + d = 1\), \(b = 3(a + d) + c = 2\). \(\dfrac{b + c}{a + d} = \dfrac11 = 1\).

questions.q: Suppose there is a uniform circular disc of mass \(M\) kg and radius \(r\) m shown in figure. The shaded regions are cut out from the disc. The moment of inertia of the remainder about the axis \(A\) of the disc is given by \(\frac{x}{256}Mr^2\). The value of \(x\) is ____ .
questions.sol: Each hole has mass \(\dfrac{M}{16}\) and its moment of inertia about A is \(\dfrac{M}{16}\left(\dfrac{r^2}{32} + \dfrac{9r^2}{16}\right) = \dfrac{19}{512}Mr^2\). Remainder \(= \dfrac{Mr^2}{2} - 2\times\dfrac{19}{512}Mr^2 = \dfrac{109}{256}Mr^2\).

questions.q: The velocity of sound in air is doubled when the temperature is raised from 0°C to \(\alpha\)°C. The value of \(\alpha\) is ____ .
questions.sol: \(v \propto \sqrt T\): doubling \(v\) needs \(T = 4\times273 = 1092\) K \(= 819\)°C.

questions.q: The size of the images of an object, formed by a thin lens are equal when the object is placed at two different positions 8 cm and 24 cm from the lens. The focal length of the lens is ____ cm.
questions.sol: Equal image sizes for \(u = 8\) and 24 cm (one real, one virtual): \(f = \dfrac{8 + 24}{2} = 16\) cm.

questions.q: The average energy released per fission for the nucleus of \({}^{235}_{92}\text{U}\) is 190 MeV. When all the atoms of 47 g pure \({}^{235}_{92}\text{U}\) undergo fission process, the energy released is \(\alpha\times10^{23}\) MeV. The value of \(\alpha\) is ____ . (Avogadro Number \(= 6\times10^{23}\) per mole)
questions.sol: 47 g is 0.2 mol \(= 1.2\times10^{23}\) atoms. Energy \(= 1.2\times10^{23}\times190 = 228\times10^{23}\) MeV.

questions.q: In a screw gauge, the zero of the circular scale lies 3 divisions above the horizontal pitch line when their metallic studs are brought in contact. Using this instrument thickness of a sheet is measured. If pitch scale reading is 1 mm and the circular scale reading is 51 then the correct thickness of the sheet is ____ mm. [Assume least count is 0.01 mm ]
questions.sol: Zero above the pitch line means a negative zero error of \(3\times0.01 = -0.03\) mm. Reading \(= 1 + 51\times0.01 = 1.51\) mm; corrected \(= 1.51 + 0.03 = 1.54\) mm.

questions.q: Four persons measure the length of a rod as 20.00 cm, 19.75 cm, 17.01 cm and 18.25 cm. The relative error in the measurement of average length of the rod is :
questions.sol: Mean \(= \dfrac{75.01}{4} = 18.75\) cm. Absolute deviations: 1.25, 1.00, 1.74, 0.50; mean deviation \(\approx 1.12\). Relative error \(= \dfrac{1.12}{18.75} \approx 0.06\).

questions.q: An object is projected with kinetic energy \(K\) from a point \(A\) at an angle 60° with the horizontal. The ratio of the difference in kinetic energies at points \(B\) and \(C\) to that at point \(A\) (see figure), in the absence of air friction is :
questions.sol: At B (top) only the horizontal velocity remains: \(K_B = K\cos^260^\circ = \dfrac K4\). At C (same level as A) \(K_C = K\). \(\dfrac{K_C - K_B}{K_A} = \dfrac{3K/4}{K} = 3 : 4\).

questions.q: Two blocks with masses 100 g and 200 g are attached to the ends of springs \(A\) and \(B\) as shown in figure. The energy stored in \(A\) is \(E\). The energy stored in \(B\), when spring constants \(k_A, k_B\) of \(A\) and \(B\), respectively satisfy the relation \(4k_A = 3k_B\), is :
questions.sol: Stored energy \(= \dfrac{(mg)^2}{2k}\). \(\dfrac{E_B}{E_A} = \left(\dfrac{200}{100}\right)^2\dfrac{k_A}{k_B} = 4\times\dfrac34 = 3\), so \(E_B = 3E\).

questions.q: In a perfectly inelastic collision, two spheres made of the same material with masses 15 kg and 25 kg, moving in opposite directions with speeds of 10 m/s and 30 m/s, respectively, strike each other and stick together. The rise in temperature (in °C ), if all the heat produced during the collision is retained by these spheres, is : (specific heat of sphere material 31 cal/kg·°C and 1 cal = 4.2 J )
questions.sol: KE lost \(= \tfrac12\dfrac{m_1m_2}{m_1 + m_2}(v_1 + v_2)^2 = \tfrac12\times\dfrac{375}{40}\times40^2 = 7500\) J. \(7500 = 40\times31\times4.2\,\Delta T \Rightarrow \Delta T \approx 1.44\)°C.

questions.q: A small bob \(A\) of mass \(m\) is attached to a massless rigid rod of length 1 m pivoted at point \(P\) and kept at an angle of 60° with vertical as shown in figure. At distance of 1 m below point \(P\), an identical bob \(B\) is kept at rest on a smooth horizontal surface that extends to a circular track of radius \(R\) as shown in figure. If bob \(B\) just manages to complete the circular path of radius \(R\) upto a point \(Q\) after being hit elastically by bob \(A\), then radius \(R\) is ____ m.
questions.sol: A falls through \(1 - \cos60^\circ = 0.5\) m: \(v = \sqrt{10}\) m/s. The elastic collision between equal masses passes this speed to B. Just completing the loop needs \(v^2 = 5gR\): \(R = \dfrac{10}{50} = \dfrac15\) m.

questions.q: Two small balls with masses \(m\) and 2 m are attached to both ends of a rigid rod of length \(d\) and negligible mass. If angular momentum of this system is \(L\) about an axis (A) passing through its centre of mass and perpendicular to the rod then angular velocity of the system about \(A\) is :
questions.sol: The CM is \(\tfrac{2d}{3}\) from \(m\) and \(\tfrac d3\) from \(2m\). \(I = m\left(\tfrac{2d}{3}\right)^2 + 2m\left(\tfrac d3\right)^2 = \tfrac23md^2\). \(\omega = \dfrac LI = \dfrac32\dfrac{L}{md^2}\).

questions.q: The moment of inertia of a square loop made of four uniform solid cylinders, each having radius \(R\) and length \(L (R < L)\) about an axis passing through the mid points of opposite sides, is (Take the mass of the entire loop as \(M\) ) :
questions.sol: Each cylinder has mass \(\tfrac M4\). The two sides crossed by the axis: \(\tfrac M4\left(\tfrac{R^2}{4} + \tfrac{L^2}{12}\right)\) each. The two sides parallel to the axis at \(\tfrac L2\): \(\tfrac M4\left(\tfrac{R^2}{2} + \tfrac{L^2}{4}\right)\) each. Sum \(= \tfrac38MR^2 + \tfrac16ML^2\).

questions.q: The strain-stress plot for materials \(A, B, C\) and \(D\) is shown in the figure. Which material has the largest Young's modulus ?
questions.sol: \(Y = \dfrac{\text{stress}}{\text{strain}}\). On a strain-vs-stress graph this is \(\dfrac{1}{\text{slope}}\), so the line with the smallest slope, C, has the largest Young's modulus.

questions.q: A simple pendulum of string length 30 cm performs 20 oscillations in 10 s. The length of the string required for the pendulum to perform 40 oscillations in the same time duration is ____ cm. [Assume that the mass of the pendulum remains same.]
questions.sol: Period goes from 0.5 s to 0.25 s. \(L \propto T^2\): \(L = 30\times\dfrac14 = 7.5\) cm.

questions.q: Two point charges \(2q\) and \(q\) are placed at vertex \(A\) and centre of face \(CDEF\) of the cube as shown in figure. The electric flux passing through the cube is:
questions.sol: A charge at a vertex is shared by 8 cubes: flux \(\dfrac{2q}{8\epsilon_0}\). A charge at a face centre is shared by 2 cubes: \(\dfrac{q}{2\epsilon_0}\). Total \(= \dfrac{q}{4\epsilon_0} + \dfrac{q}{2\epsilon_0} = \dfrac{3q}{4\epsilon_0}\).

questions.q: A wire of uniform resistance \(\lambda\ \Omega\)/m is bent into a circle of radius \(r\) and another piece of wire with length \(2r\) is connected between points \(A\) and \(B\) (AOB) as shown in figure. The equivalent resistance between points \(A\) and \(B\) is ____ Ω.
questions.sol: Three paths in parallel between A and B: the quarter arc \(\tfrac{\pi r}{2}\lambda\), the three-quarter arc \(\tfrac{3\pi r}{2}\lambda\), and the wire AOB \(2r\lambda\). \(\dfrac1R = \dfrac{2}{\pi r\lambda} + \dfrac{2}{3\pi r\lambda} + \dfrac{1}{2r\lambda} = \dfrac{16 + 3\pi}{6\pi r\lambda}\), so \(R = \dfrac{6\pi\lambda r}{3\pi + 16}\).

questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R). Consider a ferromagnetic material :
Assertion (A) : The individual atoms in a ferromagnetic material possess a magnetic dipole moment and interact with one another in such a way that they spontaneously align themselves forming domains.
Reason (R) : At high enough temperature, the domain structure of ferromagnetic material disintegrates. Thus, magnetization will disappear at high enough temperature known as Curie temperature.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
o: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
questions.sol: Both statements are correct facts about ferromagnets, but the loss of magnetisation above the Curie temperature does not explain why domains form.

questions.q: A 20 m long uniform copper wire held horizontally is allowed to fall under the gravity (\(g = 10\) m/s²) through a uniform horizontal magnetic field of 0.5 Gauss perpendicular to the length of the wire. The induced EMF across the wire when it travels a vertical distance of 200 m is ____ mV.
questions.sol: \(v = \sqrt{2gh} = \sqrt{4000} = 20\sqrt{10}\) m/s. \(\varepsilon = Blv = 0.5\times10^{-4}\times20\times20\sqrt{10} = 0.02\sqrt{10}\) V \(= 20\sqrt{10}\) mV.

questions.q:
Match List - I with List - II.
List - I RelationList - II Law
A.\(\oint\vec E\cdot d\vec l = -\frac{d}{dt}\oint\vec B\cdot d\vec a\)I.Ampere's circuital law
B.\(\oint\vec B\cdot d\vec l = \mu_0\left(I + \epsilon_0\frac{d\phi_E}{dt}\right)\)II.Faraday's laws of electromagnetic induction
C.\(\oint\vec E\cdot d\vec a = \frac{1}{\epsilon_0}\int_V\rho\,dv\)III.Ampere - Maxwell law
D.\(\oint\vec B\cdot d\vec l = \mu_0I\)IV.Gauss's law of electrostatics
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.sol: A is Faraday's law (II), B is the Ampere–Maxwell law (III), C is Gauss's law (IV), D is Ampere's circuital law (I).

questions.q: A thin prism with angle 5° of refractive index 1.72 is combined with another prism of refractive index 1.9 to produce dispersion without deviation. The angle of second prism is ____ .
questions.sol: No net deviation: \((1.72 - 1)\times5^\circ = (1.9 - 1)A' \Rightarrow A' = \dfrac{3.6}{0.9} = 4^\circ\).

questions.q: Consider light travelling from a medium \(A\) to medium \(B\) separated by a plane interface. If the light undergoes total internal reflection during its travel from medium \(A\) to \(B\) and the speed of light in media \(A\) and \(B\) are \(2.4\times10^8\) m/s and \(2.7\times10^8\) m/s, respectively, then the value of critical angle is :
questions.sol: \(\sin C = \dfrac{v_A}{v_B} = \dfrac{2.4}{2.7} = \dfrac89\). Then \(\cos C = \dfrac{\sqrt{17}}{9}\), so \(\tan C = \dfrac{8}{\sqrt{17}}\).

questions.q:
In hydrogen atom spectrum, ( \(R\) → Rydberg's constant)
A. the maximum wavelength of the radiation of Lyman series is \(\frac{4}{3R}\)
B. the Balmer series lies in the visible region of the spectrum
C. the minimum wavelength of the radiation of Paschen series is \(\frac9R\)
D. the minimum wavelength of Lyman series is \(\frac{5}{4R}\)
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.sol: Lyman longest \(= \dfrac{4}{3R}\) (A true); Balmer lines are in the visible (B true); Paschen shortest \(= \dfrac9R\) (C true); Lyman shortest is \(\dfrac1R\), not \(\dfrac{5}{4R}\) (D false).

questions.q: The de Broglie wavelength of an oxygen molecule at 27°C is \(x\times10^{-12}\) m. The value of \(x\) is (take Planck's constant \(= 6.63\times10^{-34}\) J.s, Boltzmann constant \(= 1.38\times10^{-23}\) J/K, mass of oxygen molecule \(= 5.31\times10^{-26}\) kg )
questions.sol: Using the rms momentum \(p = \sqrt{3mkT} = \sqrt{3\times5.31\times10^{-26}\times1.38\times10^{-23}\times300} \approx 2.57\times10^{-23}\): \(\lambda = \dfrac hp \approx 25.8\times10^{-12}\) m, so \(x \approx 26\).

questions.q: The following diagram shows a Zener diode as a voltage regulator. The Zener diode is rated at \(V_z = 5\) V and the desired current in load is 5 mA. The unregulated voltage source can supply upto 25 V. Considering the Zener diode can withstand four times of the load current, the value of resistor \(R_s\) (shown in circuit) should be ____ Ω.
questions.sol: The resistor must drop \(25 - 5 = 20\) V. Taking the largest allowed current as four times the load current, \(4\times5 = 20\) mA: \(R_s = \dfrac{20}{0.020} = 1000\ \Omega\).

questions.q: The space between the plates of a parallel plate capacitor of capacitance C (without any dielectric) is now filled with three dielectric slabs of dielectric constants \(K_1 = 2, K_2 = 3\) and \(K_3 = 5\) (as shown in figure). If new capacitance is \(\frac n3C\) then the value of \(n\) is ____ .
questions.sol: Bottom half: \(K_2\) and \(K_3\) side by side, each \(\tfrac A2\) over \(\tfrac d2\): \(3C + 5C = 8C\). Top half: \(K_1\) over \(\tfrac d2\): \(4C\). In series: \(\dfrac{4C\times8C}{12C} = \dfrac83C\), so \(n = 8\).

questions.q: A simple pendulum made of mass 10 g and a metallic wire of length 10 cm is suspended vertically in a uniform magnetic field of 2 T. The magnetic field direction is perpendicular to the plane of oscillations of the pendulum. If the pendulum is released from an angle of 60° with vertical, then maximum induced EMF between the point of suspension and point of oscillation is ____ mV. (Take g = 10 m/s² )
questions.sol: At the lowest point \(v = \sqrt{2gL(1 - \cos60^\circ)} = 1\) m/s, \(\omega = \dfrac vL = 10\) rad/s. \(\varepsilon = \tfrac12B\omega L^2 = \tfrac12\times2\times10\times0.01 = 0.1\) V = 100 mV.

questions.q: Using a variable frequency a.c. voltage source the maximum current measured in the given LCR circuit is 50 mA for \(V = 5\sin(100t)\). The values of \(L\) and \(R\) are shown in the figure. The capacitance of the capacitor ( C ) used is ____ μF.
questions.sol: The largest current means resonance at \(\omega = 100\) rad/s: \(I = \dfrac{5}{100} = 50\) mA. \(C = \dfrac{1}{\omega^2L} = \dfrac{1}{10^4\times2} = 50\ \mu F\).

questions.q: The equation of the electric field of an electromagnetic wave propagating through free space is given by : \(E = \sqrt{377}\sin(6.27\times10^3t - 2.09\times10^{-5}x)\) N/C. The average power of the electromagnetic wave is \(\left(\frac1\alpha\right)\) W/m². The value of \(\alpha\) is ____ . \(\left(\text{Take } \sqrt{\frac{\mu_0}{\epsilon_0}} = 377 \text{ in SI units}\right)\)
questions.sol: Average intensity \(= \dfrac{E_0^2}{2Z_0} = \dfrac{377}{2\times377} = \dfrac12\) W/m², so \(\alpha = 2\).

questions.q: In two separate Young's double-slit experimental set-ups and two monochromatic light sources of different wavelengths are used to get fringes of equal width. The ratios of the slits separations and that of the wavelengths of light used are 2 : 1 and 1 : 2 respectively. The corresponding ratio of the distances between the slits and the respective screens ( \(D_1/D_2\) ) is ____.
questions.sol: Equal fringe width: \(\dfrac{\lambda_1D_1}{d_1} = \dfrac{\lambda_2D_2}{d_2} \Rightarrow \dfrac{D_1}{D_2} = \dfrac{d_1}{d_2}\cdot\dfrac{\lambda_2}{\lambda_1} = 2\times2 = 4\).

questions.q: If \(\epsilon, E\) and \(t\) represent the free space permittivity, electric field and time respectively, then the unit of \(\frac{\epsilon E}{t}\) will be :
questions.sol: \(\epsilon E\) has the units of charge per area (C/m²). Dividing by time: (C/s)/m² = A/m².

questions.q:
Given below are two statements :
Statement I : An object moves from position \(r_1\) to position \(r_2\) under a conservative force field \(\vec F\). The work done by the force is \(W = -\int_{r_1}^{r_2}\vec F\cdot d\vec r\).
Statement II : Any object moving from one location to another location can follow infinite number of paths. Therefore, the amount of work done by the object changes with the path it follows for a conservative force.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
o: Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
questions.sol: The work done by the force is \(+\int\vec F\cdot d\vec r\) (the minus sign gives the change in potential energy), so I is false. For a conservative force the work does not depend on the path, so II is false.

questions.q:
Given below are two statements :
Statement I : For a mechanical system of many particles total kinetic energy is the sum of kinetic energies of all the particles.
Statement II : The total kinetic energy can be the sum of kinetic energy of the center of mass w.r.t. the origin and the kinetic energy of all the particles w.r.t. the center of mass as the reference.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
o: Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
questions.sol: Both are true: total KE is the sum over particles, and by König's theorem it also equals the KE of the centre of mass plus the KE of the particles relative to the centre of mass.

questions.q: A uniform bar of length 12 cm and mass 20 m lies on a smooth horizontal table. Two point masses \(m\) and \(2m\) are moving in opposite directions with same speed of \(v\) and in the same plane as the bar, as shown in figure. These masses strike the bar simultaneously and get stuck to it. After collision the entire system is rotating with angular frequency \(\omega\). The ratio of \(v\) and \(\omega\) is :
questions.sol: Both masses give angular momentum in the same sense about the centre: \(L = 2mv(0.02) + mv(0.04) = 0.08mv\). \(I = \dfrac{20m(0.12)^2}{12} + 2m(0.02)^2 + m(0.04)^2 = 0.0264m\). \(\dfrac v\omega = \dfrac{0.0264}{0.08} = 0.33\) m = 33 cm.

questions.q: When a part of a straight capillary tube is placed vertically in a liquid, the liquid raises upto certain height \(h\). If the inner radius of the capillary tube, density of the liquid and surface tension of the liquid decrease by 1% each, then the height of the liquid in the tube will change by ____ %.
questions.sol: \(h = \dfrac{2T\cos\theta}{r\rho g} \propto \dfrac{T}{r\rho}\): \(\dfrac{\Delta h}{h} = -1\% + 1\% + 1\% = +1\%\).

questions.q: Consider two boxes containing ideal gases \(A\) and \(B\) such that their temperatures, pressures and number densities are same. The molecular size of \(A\) is half of that of \(B\) and mass of molecule \(A\) is four times that of \(B\). If the collision frequency in gas \(B\) is \(32\times10^{18}\)/s then collision frequency in gas \(A\) is ____ /s.
questions.sol: Collision frequency \(\propto nd^2\bar v\), with \(\bar v \propto \sqrt{T/m}\). For A: \(d^2\) is \(\tfrac14\) and \(\bar v\) is \(\tfrac12\), so the frequency is \(\tfrac18\) of B's: \(\dfrac{32\times10^{18}}{8} = 4\times10^{18}\)/s.
questions.note: Bonus question: the correct value is \(4\times10^{18}\) per second, but every option is a multiple of \(10^8\), so full marks are given to everyone.

questions.q: Using a simple pendulum experiment \(g\) is determind by measuring its time period \(T\). Which of the following plots represent the correct relation between the pendulum length \(L\) and time period \(T\) ?
questions.sol: \(T^2 = \dfrac{4\pi^2L}{g} \Rightarrow \dfrac{1}{T^2} = \dfrac{g}{4\pi^2L}\): \(\dfrac{1}{T^2}\) is inversely proportional to \(L\), a falling hyperbola (A).
