questions.q:
Given below are two statements :
Statement I : A satellite is moving around earth in the orbit very close to the earth surface. The time period of revolution of satellite depends upon the density of earth.
Statement II : The time period of revolution of the satellite is \(T = 2\pi\sqrt{\frac{R_e}{g}}\) (for satellite very close to the earth surface), where \(R_e\) radius of earth and \(g\) acceleration due to gravity. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
o: Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
questions.sol: \(T = 2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{R}{g}}\) is correct (II), and with \(g = \tfrac43\pi G\rho R\) it becomes \(T = \sqrt{\dfrac{3\pi}{G\rho}}\), which depends on density (I).

questions.q: Five positive charges each having charge \(q\) are placed at the vertices of a pentagon as shown in the figure. The electric potential (\(V\)) and the electric field (\(\vec E\)) at the center \(O\) of the pentagon due to these five positive charges are :
questions.sol: Potential is a scalar: \(V = 5\times\dfrac{q}{4\pi\epsilon_0r}\). The five equal field vectors are symmetric around the centre and cancel: \(\vec E = 0\).

questions.q: Three small identical bubbles of water having same charge on each coalesce to form a bigger bubble. Then the ratio of the potentials on one initial bubble and that on the resultant bigger bubble is :
questions.sol: Three drops of radius \(r\) make one of radius \(3^{1/3}r\) with charge \(3q\). \(V \propto \dfrac qr\): \(V_{big} = \dfrac{3q}{3^{1/3}r} = 3^{2/3}V\). Ratio \(1 : 3^{2/3}\).

questions.q: An electric power line having total resistance of 2Ω, delivers 1 kW of power at 250 V. The percentage efficiency of transmission line is ____ .
questions.sol: \(I = \dfrac{1000}{250} = 4\) A, line loss \(= 4^2\times2 = 32\) W. Efficiency \(= \dfrac{1000}{1032} \approx 96.9\%\).

questions.q: Figure shows the circuit that contains three resistances (9Ω each) and two inductors (4 mH each). The reading of ammeter at the moment switch \(K\) is turned ON, is ____ A.
questions.sol: At the instant of switching on, the inductors block any sudden current, so only the middle 9Ω branch conducts: \(I = \dfrac99 = 1\) A.

questions.q: A laser beam has intensity of \(4.0\times10^{14}\) W/m². The amplitude of magnetic field associated with beam is ____ T. (Take \(\epsilon_0 = 8.85\times10^{-12}\) C²/Nm² and \(c = 3\times10^8\) m/s )
questions.sol: \(I = \dfrac{cB_0^2}{2\mu_0} \Rightarrow B_0 = \sqrt{\dfrac{2\mu_0I}{c}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{2\times4\pi\times10^{-7}\times4\times10^{14}}{3\times10^8}} \approx 1.83\) T.

questions.q: The wavelength of light, while it is passing through water is 540 nm. The refractive index of water is 4/3. The wavelength of the same light when it is passing through a transparent medium having refractive index of 3/2 is ____ nm.
questions.sol: \(\lambda\mu\) is constant: \(540\times\dfrac43 = \lambda\times\dfrac32 \Rightarrow \lambda = 480\) nm.

questions.q:
Which of the following are true for a single slit diffraction?
A. Width of central maxima increases with increase in wavelength keeping slit width constant.
B. Width of central maxima increases with decrease in wavelength keeping slit width constant.
C. Width of central maxima increases with decrease in slit width at constant wavelength.
D. Width of central maxima increases with increase in slit width at constant wavelength.
E. Brightness of central maxima increases for decrease in wavelength at constant slit width.
questions.sol: Central maximum width \(= \dfrac{2\lambda D}{a}\): it grows with \(\lambda\) (A) and as \(a\) decreases (C). A shorter wavelength squeezes the light into a narrower, brighter central maximum (E).

questions.q: In parallax method for the determination of focal length of a concave mirror, the object should always be placed:
o: between the focus (\(F\)) and the centre of curvature (\(C\)) of the mirror ONLY
between the pole (\(P\)) and the focus (\(F\)) of the concave mirror ONLY
at any point beyond the focus (\(F\)) of the mirror
beyond the centre of the curvature (\(C\)) of the mirror ONLY
questions.sol: The parallax method locates a real image, which a concave mirror forms only when the object is beyond its focus.

questions.q: The smallest wavelength of Lyman series is 91 nm. The difference between the largest wavelengths of Paschen and Balmer series is nearly ____ nm.
questions.sol: \(\dfrac1R = 91\) nm. Paschen longest (4→3): \(\dfrac{144}{7}\times91 \approx 1872\) nm. Balmer longest (3→2): \(\dfrac{36}{5}\times91 \approx 655\) nm. Difference \(\approx 1217\) nm.

questions.q: Light is incident on a metallic plate having work function \(110\times10^{-20}\) J. If the produced photoelectrons have zero kinetic energy then the angular frequency of the incident light is ____ rad/s. (\(h = 6.63\times10^{-34}\) J.s).
questions.sol: Zero kinetic energy: \(\hbar\omega = \phi\). \(\omega = \dfrac{2\pi\phi}{h} = \dfrac{2\pi\times1.1\times10^{-18}}{6.63\times10^{-34}} \approx 1.04\times10^{16}\) rad/s.

questions.q: The correct truth table for the given input data of the following logic gate is :
questions.sol: \(Y = \overline{\overline{AB}\cdot(C + D)}\). Rows: (1101) → \(\overline{0} = 1\); (0011) → \(\overline{1\cdot1} = 0\); (1010) → 0; (1111) → 1. That is table (A).

questions.q: Two masses \(m\) and 2 m are connected by a light string going over a pulley (disc) of mass 30 m with radius \(r = 0.1\) m. The pulley is mounted in a vertical plane and it is free to rotate about its axis. The 2 m mass is released from rest and its speed when it has descended through a height of 3.6 m is ____ m/s. (Assume string does not slip and g = 10 m/s²)
questions.sol: \(I = \tfrac12(30m)r^2 = 15mr^2\). Energy: \((2m - m)gh = \tfrac12(3m)v^2 + \tfrac12(15m)v^2 = 9mv^2 \Rightarrow v^2 = \dfrac{10\times3.6}{9} = 4\), \(v = 2\) m/s.

questions.q: An insulated cylinder of volume 60 cm³ is filled with a gas at 27°C and 2 atmospheric pressure. Then the gas is compressed making the final volume as 20 cm³ while allowing the temperature to rise to 77°C. The final pressure is ____ atmospheric pressure.
questions.sol: \(\dfrac{P_1V_1}{T_1} = \dfrac{P_2V_2}{T_2} \Rightarrow P_2 = 2\times\dfrac{60}{20}\times\dfrac{350}{300} = 7\) atm.

questions.q: A cylindrical conductor of length 2 m and area of cross-section 0.2 mm² carries an electric current of 1.6 A when its ends are connected to a 2 V battery. Mobility of electrons in the conductor is \(\alpha\times10^{-3}\) m²/V.s. The value of \(\alpha\) is : (electron concentration \(= 5\times10^{28}\)/m³ and electron charge \(= 1.6\times10^{-19}\) C )
questions.sol: \(v_d = \dfrac{I}{neA} = \dfrac{1.6}{5\times10^{28}\times1.6\times10^{-19}\times0.2\times10^{-6}} = 10^{-3}\) m/s; \(E = \dfrac22 = 1\) V/m. Mobility \(= \dfrac{v_d}{E} = 1\times10^{-3}\), so \(\alpha = 1\).

questions.q: A capacitor \(P\) with capacitance \(10\times10^{-6}\) F is fully charged with a potential difference of 6.0 V and disconnected from the battery. The charged capacitor \(P\) is connected across another capacitor \(Q\) with capacitance \(20\times10^{-6}\) F. The charge on capacitor \(Q\) when equilibrium is established will be \(\alpha\times10^{-5}C\) (assume capacitor \(Q\) does not have any charge initially), the value of \(\alpha\) is ____ .
questions.sol: Charge \(60\ \mu C\) is shared at a common voltage \(\dfrac{60}{30} = 2\) V. Q holds \(20\ \mu F\times2 = 40\ \mu C = 4\times10^{-5}\) C.

questions.q: A conducting circular loop is rotated about its diameter at a constant angular speed of 100 rad/s in a magnetic field of 0.5 T perpendicular to the axis of rotation. When the loop is rotated by 30° from the horizontal position, the induced EMF is 15.4 mV. The radius of the loop is ____ mm. \(\left(\text{Take } \pi = \frac{22}{7}\right)\)
questions.sol: \(\varepsilon = BA\omega\sin\theta\): \(15.4\times10^{-3} = 0.5\times\pi r^2\times100\times\tfrac12 \Rightarrow \pi r^2 = 6.16\times10^{-4}\), \(r^2 = 1.96\times10^{-4}\), \(r = 14\) mm.

questions.q:
Match the LIST-I with LIST-II
List-IList-II
A.Spring constantI.\(ML^2T^{-2}K^{-1}\)
B.Thermal conductivityII.\(ML^0T^{-2}\)
C.Boltzmann constantIII.\(ML^2T^{-3}A^{-2}\)
D.Inductive reactanceIV.\(MLT^{-3}K^{-1}\)
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.sol: Spring constant N/m = \([ML^0T^{-2}]\) (II); thermal conductivity W/(m K) = \([MLT^{-3}K^{-1}]\) (IV); Boltzmann constant J/K = \([ML^2T^{-2}K^{-1}]\) (I); reactance Ω = \([ML^2T^{-3}A^{-2}]\) (III).

questions.q: A projectile is thrown upward at an angle 60° with the horizontal. The speed of the projectile is 20 m/s when its direction of motion is 45° with the horizontal. The initial speed of the projectile is ____ m/s.
questions.sol: The horizontal velocity stays the same: \(u\cos60^\circ = 20\cos45^\circ \Rightarrow \dfrac u2 = 10\sqrt2 \Rightarrow u = 20\sqrt2\) m/s.

questions.q: A cylindrical tube \(AB\) of length \(l\), closed at both ends contains an ideal gas of 1 mol having molecular weight \(M\). The tube is rotated in a horizontal plane with constant angular velocity \(\omega\) about an axis perpendicular to \(AB\) and passing through the edge at end \(A\), as shown in the figure. If \(P_A\) and \(P_B\) are the pressures at \(A\) and \(B\) respectively, then (Consider the temperature is same at all points in the tube)
questions.sol: In the rotating frame \(\dfrac{dP}{dr} = \rho\omega^2r\) with \(\rho = \dfrac{PM}{RT}\): \(\ln\dfrac{P_B}{P_A} = \dfrac{M\omega^2l^2}{2RT}\), so \(P_B = P_Ae^{M\omega^2l^2/2RT}\).

questions.q: A solid sphere of mass 5 kg and radius 10 cm is kept in contact with another solid sphere of mass 10 kg and radius 20 cm. The moment of inertia of this pair of spheres about the tangent passing through the point of contact is ____ kg·m².
questions.sol: About a tangent through its surface each sphere has \(\tfrac25mr^2 + mr^2 = \tfrac75mr^2\). Total \(= \tfrac75(5\times0.01 + 10\times0.04) = 0.07 + 0.56 = 0.63\) kg m².

questions.q:
Given below are two statements :
Statement I : Pressure of a fluid is exerted only on a solid surface in contact as the fluid-pressure does not exist everywhere in a still fluid.
Statement II : Excess potential energy of the molecules on the surface of a liquid, when compared to interior, results in surface tension.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below
o: Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
questions.sol: Pressure exists at every point inside a fluid, not just on surfaces, so I is false. Surface molecules have extra potential energy, which is the origin of surface tension, so II is true.

questions.q: Rods \(x\) and \(y\) of equal dimensions but of different materials are joined as shown in figure. Temperatures of end points \(A\) and \(F\) are maintained at 100°C and 40°C respectively. Given the thermal conductivity of rod \(x\) is three times of that of rod \(y\), the temperature at junction points \(B\) and \(E\) are (close to):
questions.sol: Take the thermal resistance of a y rod as \(3r\) and of an x rod as \(r\). Between B and E: \(BCE = 6r\) in parallel with \(BDE = 2r\), giving \(1.5r\). Total \(= r + 1.5r + 3r = 5.5r\), \(H = \dfrac{60}{5.5r}\). \(T_B = 100 - Hr \approx 89\)°C, \(T_E = 40 + 3rH \approx 73\)°C.

questions.q: The volume of an ideal gas increases 8 times and temperature becomes \((1/4)^{\text{th}}\) of initial temperature during a reversible change. If there is no exchange of heat in this process (\(\Delta Q = 0\)) then identify the gas from the following options (Assuming the gases given in the options are ideal gases) :
questions.sol: Adiabatic: \(TV^{\gamma - 1}\) is constant, so \(\tfrac14\times8^{\gamma - 1} = 1 \Rightarrow 2^{3(\gamma - 1)} = 2^2 \Rightarrow \gamma = \tfrac53\): a monatomic gas, He.

questions.q: The escape velocity from a spherical planet \(A\) is 10 km/s. The escape velocity from another planet \(B\) whose density and radius are 10% of those of planet \(A\), is ____ m/s.
questions.sol: \(v_e = \sqrt{\dfrac{8\pi G\rho}{3}}\,R \propto R\sqrt\rho\). \(v_B = 10\times0.1\times\sqrt{0.1}\) km/s \(= \dfrac{1000}{\sqrt{10}} = 100\sqrt{10}\) m/s.

questions.q: Net gravitational force at the center of a square is found to be \(F_1\) when four particles having mass \(M, 2M, 3M\) and \(4M\) are placed at the four corners of the square as shown in figure and it is \(F_2\) when the positions of \(3M\) and \(4M\) are interchanged. The ratio \(\frac{F_1}{F_2}\) is \(\frac{\alpha}{\sqrt5}\). The value of \(\alpha\) is ____ .
questions.sol: Each mass pulls the centre towards itself along a diagonal. With 4M, 3M on top and M, 2M below: \(\vec F_1 \propto (0, 4)\), so \(F_1 \propto 4\). After swapping 3M and 4M: \(\vec F_2 \propto (2, 4)\), \(F_2 \propto 2\sqrt5\). \(\dfrac{F_1}{F_2} = \dfrac{2}{\sqrt5}\), so \(\alpha = 2\).

questions.q: Electric field in a region is given by \(\vec E = Ax\hat i + By\hat j\), where \(A = 10\) V/m² and \(B = 5\) V/m². If the electric potential at a point (10, 20) is 500 V, then the electric potential at origin is ____ V.

A simple pendulum has a bob with mass \(m\) and charge \(q\). The pendulum string has negligible mass. When a uniform and horizontal electric field \(\vec E\) is applied, the tension in the string changes. The final tension in the string, when pendulum attains an equilibrium position is ____ .
questions.sol: At equilibrium the string balances the resultant of gravity \(mg\) (down) and \(qE\) (sideways): \(T = \sqrt{m^2g^2 + q^2E^2}\).

questions.q: Six point charges are kept 60° apart from each other on the circumference of a circle of radius \(R\) as shown in figure. The net electric field at the center of the circle is ____ . (\(\epsilon_0\) is permittivity of free space)
questions.sol: The two charges on the y-axis cancel. Summing the remaining position vectors weighted by charge: \(\sum q\hat r = Q(\sqrt3, -1)\). The field at the centre points the opposite way: \(\vec E = -\dfrac{Q}{4\pi\epsilon_0R^2}(\sqrt3\hat i - \hat j)\).

questions.q: A meter bridge with two resistances \(R_1\) and \(R_2\) as shown in figure was balanced (null point) at 40 cm from the point \(P\). The null point changed to 50 cm from the point \(P\), when 16Ω resistance is connected in parallel to \(R_2\). The values of resistances \(R_1\) and \(R_2\) are ____ .
questions.sol: \(\dfrac{R_1}{R_2} = \dfrac{40}{60}\), and with 16Ω in parallel \(R_1 = \dfrac{16R_2}{R_2 + 16}\). So \(\dfrac23R_2 = \dfrac{16R_2}{R_2 + 16} \Rightarrow R_2 = 8\ \Omega\), \(R_1 = \dfrac{16}{3}\ \Omega\).

questions.q: \(XPQY\) is a vertical smooth long loop having a total resistance \(R\) where \(PX\) is parallel to \(QY\) and separation between them is \(l\). A constant magnetic field \(B\) perpendicular to the plane of the loop exists in the entire space. A rod \(CD\) of length \(L (L > l)\) and mass \(m\) is made to slide down from rest under the gravity as shown in figure. The terminal speed acquired by the rod is ____ m/s. (g = acceleration due to gravity)
questions.sol: Only the length \(l\) between the rails is in the circuit: emf \(Blv\), force \(\dfrac{B^2l^2v}{R}\). Terminal speed when this equals \(mg\): \(v = \dfrac{mgR}{B^2l^2}\).

questions.q: Three identical coils \(C_1, C_2\) and \(C_3\) are closely placed such that they share a common axis. \(C_2\) is exactly midway. \(C_1\) carries current \(I\) in anti-clockwise direction while \(C_3\) carries current \(I\) in clockwise direction. An induced current flows through \(C_2\) will be in clockwise direction when
o: \(C_1\) and \(C_3\) move with equal speeds away from \(C_2\)
\(C_1\) moves towards \(C_2\) and \(C_3\) moves away from \(C_2\)
\(C_1\) and \(C_3\) move with equal speeds towards \(C_2\)
\(C_1\) moves away from \(C_2\) and \(C_3\) moves towards \(C_2\)
questions.sol: \(C_1\) moving closer increases its (anticlockwise) flux through \(C_2\); \(C_3\) moving away reduces its (clockwise) flux. Both changes are opposed by a clockwise current in \(C_2\).

questions.q: A thin convex lens of focal length 5 cm and a thin concave lens of focal length 4 cm are combined together (without any gap) and this combination has magnification \(m_1\) when an object is placed 10 cm before the convex lens. Keeping the positions of convex lens and object undisturbed a gap of 1 cm is introduced between the lenses by moving the concave lens away, which lead to a change in magnification of total lens system to \(m_2\). The value of \(\left|\frac{m_1}{m_2}\right|\) is ____ .
questions.sol: In contact: \(\frac1f = \frac15 - \frac14 = -\frac{1}{20}\); with \(u = -10\), \(v = -\frac{20}{3}\), so \(m_1 = \frac23\). With a 1 cm gap: the convex lens gives \(v = 10\) cm (\(m = -1\)); this is a virtual object 9 cm beyond the concave lens: \(\frac1v = -\frac14 + \frac19 \Rightarrow v = -7.2\) cm, \(m = -0.8\). \(m_2 = 0.8\), so \(\left|\frac{m_1}{m_2}\right| = \frac56\).
questions.note: Bonus question: the correct value, \(\frac56\), is not one of the four options, so full marks are given to everyone.

questions.q: Consider an equilateral prism (refractive index \(\sqrt2\)). A ray of light is incident on its one surface at a certain angle \(i\). If the emergent ray is found to graze along the other surface then the angle of refraction at the incident surface is close to ____
questions.sol: Grazing emergence: \(r_2 = C = 45^\circ\) (since \(\sin C = \frac{1}{\sqrt2}\)). \(r_1 = A - r_2 = 60^\circ - 45^\circ = 15^\circ\).

questions.q: The minimum frequency of photon required to break a particle of mass 15.348 amu into \(4\alpha\) particles is ____ kHz. [mass of He nucleus = 4.002 amu, 1 amu \(= 1.66\times10^{-27}\) kg, \(h = 6.6\times10^{-34}\) J.s and \(c = 3\times10^8\) m/s ]

7.9 MeV α-particle scatters from a target material of atomic number 79. From the given data the estimated diameter of nuclei of the target material is (approximately) ____ m. [\(\frac{1}{4\pi\epsilon_0} = 9\times10^9\) Nm²/C² and electron charge \(= 1.6\times10^{-19}\) C]
questions.sol: Closest approach \(r = \dfrac{k(79e)(2e)}{K} = \dfrac{9\times10^9\times158\times1.6\times10^{-19}}{7.9\times10^6} \approx 2.88\times10^{-14}\) m; diameter \(\approx 5.76\times10^{-14}\) m.

questions.q: Find the correct combination of A, B, C and D inputs which can cause the LED to glow.
questions.sol: The NOR gates with joined inputs give \(\bar A\), \(\bar B\); the NAND then gives \(A + B\). The LED glows when the NAND side is high (\(A + B = 1\)) and the NOR output \(\overline{C + D}\) is low (C or D = 1). Only 1101 satisfies both.

questions.q: A circular disc has radius \(R_1\) and thickness \(T_1\). Another circular disc made of the same material has radius \(R_2\) and thickness \(T_2\). If the moment of inertia of both discs are same and \(\frac{R_1}{R_2} = 2\) then \(\frac{T_1}{T_2} = \frac1\alpha\). The value of \(\alpha\) is ____ .
questions.sol: \(I = \tfrac12MR^2\) with \(M = \rho\pi R^2T\), so \(I \propto R^4T\). Equal I: \(\dfrac{T_1}{T_2} = \left(\dfrac{R_2}{R_1}\right)^4 = \dfrac{1}{16}\), \(\alpha = 16\).

questions.q: Two loudspeakers (\(L_1\) and \(L_2\)) are placed with a separation of 10 m, as shown in figure. Both speakers are fed with an audio input signal of same frequency with constant volume. A voice recorder, initially at point \(A\), at equidistant to both loudspeakers, is moved by 25 m along the line \(AB\) while monitoring the audio signal. The measured signal was found to undergo 10 cycles of minima and maxima during the movement. The frequency of the input signal is ____ Hz (Speed of sound in air is 324 m/s and \(\sqrt5 = 2.23\))
questions.sol: Speakers at \((0, \pm5)\), A at (40, 0), B at (40, 25). At B the path difference is \(\sqrt{40^2 + 30^2} - \sqrt{40^2 + 20^2} = 50 - 44.6 = 5.4\) m. 10 cycles mean \(10\lambda = 5.4 \Rightarrow \lambda = 0.54\) m, \(f = \dfrac{324}{0.54} = 600\) Hz.

questions.q: Inductance of a coil with \(10^4\) turns is 10 mH and it is connected to a dc source of 10 V with internal resistance of 10Ω. The energy density in the inductor when the current reaches \(\left(\frac1e\right)\) of its maximum value is \(\alpha\pi\times\frac{1}{e^2}\) J/m³. The value of \(\alpha\) is ____ . (\(\mu_0 = 4\pi\times10^{-7}\) Tm/A).
questions.sol: Maximum current \(I_0 = \dfrac{10}{10} = 1\) A, so \(I = \dfrac1e\) A. Taking \(n = 10^4\) turns per metre: \(u = \dfrac{B^2}{2\mu_0} = \dfrac{\mu_0n^2I^2}{2} = \dfrac{4\pi\times10^{-7}\times10^8}{2e^2} = \dfrac{20\pi}{e^2}\), so \(\alpha = 20\).

questions.q: The electric field of a plane electromagnetic wave, travelling in an unknown nonmagnetic medium is given by, \(E_y = 20\sin(3\times10^6x - 4.5\times10^{14}t)\) V/m (where \(x\), t and other values have S.I. units). The dielectric constant of the medium is ____ (speed of light in free space is \(3\times10^8\) m/s)
questions.sol: \(v = \dfrac\omega k = \dfrac{4.5\times10^{14}}{3\times10^6} = 1.5\times10^8\) m/s, so \(n = 2\) and the dielectric constant \(n^2 = 4\).

questions.q: A parallel beam of light travelling in air (refractive index 1.0) is incident on a convex spherical glass surface of radius of curvature 50 cm. Refractive index of glass is 1.5. The rays converge to a point at a distance \(x\) cm from the centre of the curvature of the spherical surface. The value of \(x\) is ____ cm.
questions.sol: Single surface: \(\dfrac{1.5}{v} - \dfrac{1}{\infty} = \dfrac{0.5}{50} \Rightarrow v = 150\) cm from the surface; the centre is 50 cm from the surface, so \(x = 100\) cm.

questions.q: A spherical body of radius \(r\) and density \(\sigma\) falls freely through a viscous liquid having density \(\rho\) and viscosity \(\eta\) and attains a terminal velocity \(v_0\). Estimated maximum error in the quantity \(\eta\) is : (Ignore errors associated with \(\sigma\), \(\rho\) and \(g\), gravitational acceleration)
questions.sol: \(\eta = \dfrac{2r^2(\sigma - \rho)g}{9v_0}\), so the maximum relative error is \(\dfrac{\Delta\eta}{\eta} = \dfrac{2\Delta r}{r} + \dfrac{\Delta v_0}{v_0}\).

questions.q: Keeping the significant figures in view, the sum of the physical quantities 52.01 m, 153.2 m and 0.123 m is :
questions.sol: 52.01 + 153.2 + 0.123 = 205.333 m. In addition keep the fewest decimal places (one, from 153.2): 205.3 m.

questions.q: A river of width 200 m is flowing from west to east with a speed of 18 km/h. A boat, moving with speed of 36 km/h in still water, is made to travel one-round trip (bank to bank of the river). Minimum time taken by the boat for this journey and also the displacement along the river bank are ____ and ____ respectively.
questions.sol: Head straight across for minimum time: \(t = \dfrac{200}{10} = 20\) s each way, 40 s in all. The river (5 m/s) carries the boat \(5\times20 = 100\) m downstream on each crossing, both times the same way: 200 m.

questions.q: A large drum having radius \(R\) is spinning around its axis with angular velocity \(\omega\), as shown in figure. The minimum value of \(\omega\) so that a body of mass \(M\) remains stuck to the inner wall of the drum, taking the coefficient of friction between the drum surface and mass \(M\) as \(\mu\), is :
questions.sol: The wall's normal force \(M\omega^2R\) gives friction \(\mu M\omega^2R\), which must hold the weight: \(\mu\omega^2R \ge g \Rightarrow \omega_{min} = \sqrt{\dfrac{g}{\mu R}}\).

questions.q: A body of mass 2 kg is moving along \(x\)-direction such that its displacement as function of time is given by \(x(t) = \alpha t^2 + \beta t + \gamma\) m, where \(\alpha = 1\ m/s^2\), \(\beta = 1\ m/s\) and \(\gamma = 1\ m\). The work done on the body during the time interval \(t = 2s\) to \(t = 3s\), is ____ J.

Two cars A and B each of mass \(10^3\) kg are moving on parallel tracks separated by a distance of 10 m, in same direction with speeds 72 km/h and 36 km/h. The magnitude of angular momentum of car A with respect to car B is ____ J·s.
questions.sol: Relative speed \(= 20 - 10 = 10\) m/s, perpendicular distance 10 m. \(L = mv_{rel}d = 10^3\times10\times10 = 10^5\) J·s.

questions.q: The pulley shown in figure is made using a thin rim and two rods of length equal to diameter of the rim. The rim and each rod have a mass of M. Two blocks of mass of M and m are attached to two ends of a light string passing over the pulley, which is hinged to rotate freely in vertical plane about its center. The magnitudes of the acceleration experienced by the blocks is ____ (assume no slipping of string on pulley).
questions.sol: \(I = MR^2 + 2\times\dfrac{M(2R)^2}{12} = \dfrac53MR^2\). \(a = \dfrac{(M - m)g}{M + m + I/R^2} = \dfrac{(M - m)g}{\frac83M + m}\).

questions.q: Surface tension of two liquids (having same densities), \(T_1\) and \(T_2\), are measured using capillary rise method utilizing two tubes with inner radii of \(r_1\) and \(r_2\) where \(r_1 > r_2\). The measured liquid heights in these tubes are \(h_1\) and \(h_2\) respectively. [Ignore the weight of the liquid above the lowest point of miniscus]. The heights \(h_1\) and \(h_2\) and surface tensions \(T_1\) and \(T_2\) satisfy the relation :
questions.sol: \(h = \dfrac{2T\cos\theta}{r\rho g}\). The liquids have the same surface tension behaviour here (\(T_1 = T_2\)), so the narrower tube (\(r_2\)) gives the larger height: \(h_1 < h_2\).

questions.q: The r.m.s. speed of oxygen molecules at 47 °C is equal to that of the hydrogen molecules kept at ____ °C. (Mass of oxygen molecule/mass of hydrogen molecule = 32/2)
questions.sol: \(v_{rms} \propto \sqrt{T/M}\): \(\dfrac{320}{32} = \dfrac{T_H}{2} \Rightarrow T_H = 20\) K = −253 °C.

questions.q: The kinetic energy of a simple harmonic oscillator is oscillating with angular frequency of 176 rad/s. The frequency of this simple harmonic oscillator is ____ Hz. [ take \(\pi = \frac{22}{7}\) ]
questions.sol: Kinetic energy oscillates at twice the oscillator's frequency: \(\omega = 88\) rad/s, \(f = \dfrac{88}{2\pi} = \dfrac{88\times7}{44} = 14\) Hz.

questions.q: Consider two identical metallic spheres of radius \(R\) each having charge \(Q\) and mass \(m\). Their centers have an initial separation of \(4R\). Both the spheres are given an initial speed of \(u\) towards each other. The minimum value of \(u\), so that they can just touch each other is: (Take \(k = \frac{1}{4\pi\epsilon_0}\) and assume \(kQ^2 > Gm^2\) where \(G\) is the Gravitational constant)
questions.sol: They touch when the centres are \(2R\) apart. Energy: \(2\cdot\tfrac12mu^2 = (kQ^2 - Gm^2)\left(\dfrac{1}{2R} - \dfrac{1}{4R}\right) \Rightarrow u = \sqrt{\dfrac{kQ^2}{4mR}\left(1 - \dfrac{Gm^2}{kQ^2}\right)}\).

questions.q: Two known resistances of \(R\ \Omega\) and \(2R\ \Omega\) and one unknown resistance \(X\ \Omega\) are connected in a circuit as shown in the figure. If the equivalent resistance between points \(A\) and \(B\) in the circuit is \(X\ \Omega\), then the value of \(X\) is ____ Ω.
questions.sol: \((2R + X)\,\|\,R = X \Rightarrow R(2R + X) = X(3R + X) \Rightarrow X^2 + 2RX - 2R^2 = 0 \Rightarrow X = (\sqrt3 - 1)R\).

questions.q: The total length of potentiometer wire AB is 50 cm in the arrangement as shown in the figure. If \(P\) is the point where the galvanometer shows zero reading then the length AP is ____ cm.
questions.sol: Balanced bridge: \(\dfrac{AP}{PB} = \dfrac64 \Rightarrow AP = \dfrac35\times50 = 30\) cm.

questions.q: A battery with EMF \(E\) and internal resistance \(r\) is connected across a resistance \(R\). The power consumption in \(R\) will be maximum when:
questions.sol: Maximum power transfer theorem: power in \(R\) is greatest when \(R = r\).

questions.q: An infinitely long straight wire carrying current \(I\) is bent in a planar shape as shown in the diagram. The radius of the circular part is \(r\). The magnetic field at the centre \(O\) of the circular loop is :
questions.sol: The straight wire gives \(\dfrac{\mu_0I}{2\pi r}\) out of the page (\(+\hat i\)); the loop, traversed clockwise as seen, gives \(\dfrac{\mu_0I}{2r}\) into the page (\(-\hat i\)). Net \(= -\dfrac{\mu_0}{2\pi}\dfrac Ir(\pi - 1)\hat i\).

questions.q: A capacitor C is first charged fully with potential difference of \(V_0\) and disconnected from the battery. The charged capacitor is connected across an inductor having inductance L. In \(t\) s, 25% of the initial energy in the capacitor is transferred to the inductor. The value of \(t\) is ____ s.
questions.sol: Capacitor energy \(\propto q^2 = Q^2\cos^2\omega t\). 75% left: \(\cos^2\omega t = \tfrac34 \Rightarrow \omega t = \dfrac\pi6 \Rightarrow t = \dfrac{\pi\sqrt{LC}}{6}\).

questions.q:
Given below are two statements :
Statement I : In a Young's double slit experiment, the angular separation of fringes will increase as the screen is moved away from the plane of the slits
Statement II : In a Young's double slit experiment, the angular separation of fringes will increase when monochromatic source is replaced by another monochromatic source of higher wavelength
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
o: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
questions.sol: Angular fringe separation \(= \dfrac\lambda d\): it does not depend on the screen distance (I false) and increases with wavelength (II true).

questions.q: As shown in the diagram, when the incident ray is parallel to base of the prism, the emergent ray grazes along the second surface. If refractive index of the material of prism is \(\sqrt2\), the angle \(\theta\) of prism is.
questions.sol: At the first face \(i = 45^\circ\): \(\sin r_1 = \dfrac{\sin45^\circ}{\sqrt2} = \tfrac12 \Rightarrow r_1 = 30^\circ\). Grazing emergence: \(r_2 = C = 45^\circ\). Apex \(A = 75^\circ\), so \(\theta = 180^\circ - 45^\circ - 75^\circ = 60^\circ\).

questions.q: The energy of an electron in an orbit of the Bohr's atom is \(-0.04E_0\) eV where \(E_0\) is the ground state energy. If \(L\) is the angular momentum of the electron in this orbit and \(h\) is the Planck's constant, then \(\frac{2\pi L}{h}\) is ____ :
questions.sol: \(E_n = \dfrac{E_0}{n^2}\) and \(\dfrac{1}{n^2} = 0.04 \Rightarrow n = 5\). \(L = \dfrac{nh}{2\pi} \Rightarrow \dfrac{2\pi L}{h} = 5\).

questions.q: The charge stored by the capacitor C in the given circuit in the steady state is ____ μC.
questions.sol: In steady state no current flows in the capacitor branch, and only the forward-biased diode branch (4 Ω) conducts: \(I = \dfrac{2.5}{1 + 4} = 0.5\) A. The capacitor sees \(0.5\times4 = 2\) V: \(Q = 5\ \mu F\times2 = 10\ \mu C\).

questions.q: The terminal velocity of a metallic ball of radius 6 mm in a viscous fluid is 20 cm/s. The terminal velocity of another ball of same material and having radius 3 mm in the same fluid will be ____ cm/s.
questions.sol: \(v_t \propto r^2\): \(20\times\left(\tfrac36\right)^2 = 5\) cm/s.

questions.q: A diatomic gas (\(\gamma = 1.4\)) does 100 J of work when it is expanded isobarically. Then the heat given to the gas ____ J.
questions.sol: Isobaric: \(\dfrac{W}{Q} = \dfrac{nR\Delta T}{nC_p\Delta T} = \dfrac{\gamma - 1}{\gamma}\). \(Q = 100\times\dfrac{1.4}{0.4} = 350\) J.

questions.q: An electromagnetic wave of frequency 100 MHz propagates through a medium of conductivity, \(\sigma = 10\) mho/m. The ratio of maximum conduction current density to maximum displacement current density is ____ . [ Take \(\frac{1}{4\pi\epsilon_0} = 9\times10^9\) Nm²/C²]
questions.sol: \(\dfrac{J_c}{J_d} = \dfrac{\sigma}{\omega\epsilon_0} = \dfrac{10}{2\pi\times10^8\times8.85\times10^{-12}} \approx 1800\).

questions.q: In a Young's double slit experiment set up, the two slits are kept 0.4 mm apart and screen is placed at 1 m from slits. If a thin transparent sheet of thickness 20μ m is introduced in front of one of the slits then center bright fringe shifts by 20 mm on the screen. The refractive index of transparent sheet is given by \(\frac{\alpha}{10}\), where \(\alpha\) is ____ .
questions.sol: Shift \(= \dfrac{(\mu - 1)tD}{d} \Rightarrow 20\times10^{-3} = \dfrac{(\mu - 1)\times20\times10^{-6}\times1}{0.4\times10^{-3}} \Rightarrow \mu = 1.4 = \dfrac{14}{10}\).

questions.q: A particle having electric charge \(3\times10^{-19}\) C and mass \(6\times10^{-27}\) kg is accelerated by applying an electric potential of 1.21 V. Wavelength of the matter wave associated with the particle is \(\alpha\times10^{-12}\) m. The value of \(\alpha\) is ____ . (Take Planck's constant \(= 6.6\times10^{-34}\) J.s)
questions.sol: \(\lambda = \dfrac{h}{\sqrt{2mqV}} = \dfrac{6.6\times10^{-34}}{\sqrt{2\times6\times10^{-27}\times3\times10^{-19}\times1.21}} = \dfrac{6.6\times10^{-34}}{6.6\times10^{-23}} = 10\times10^{-12}\) m.

questions.q: In an experiment the values of two spring constants were measured as \(k_1 = (10 \pm 0.2)\) N/m and \(k_2 = (20 \pm 0.3)\) N/m. If these springs are connected in parallel, then the percentage error in equivalent spring constant is :
questions.sol: In parallel \(k = k_1 + k_2 = 30\) N/m with \(\Delta k = 0.2 + 0.3 = 0.5\). Percentage error \(= \dfrac{0.5}{30}\times100 = 1.67\%\).

questions.q: Consider a modified Bernoulli equation. \(\left(P + \dfrac{A}{Bt^2}\right) + \rho g(h + Bt) + \dfrac12\rho V^2 = \) constant. If \(t\) has the dimension of time then the dimensions of \(A\) and \(B\) are ____ , ____ respectively.
questions.sol: \(\rho gBt\) must have the dimensions of \(\rho gh\), so \(Bt\) is a length: \(B = [M^0LT^{-1}]\). \(\dfrac{A}{Bt^2}\) is a pressure: \(A = [ML^{-1}T^{-2}][LT^{-1}][T^2] = [ML^0T^{-1}]\).

questions.q: A 4 kg mass moves under the influence of a force \(\vec F = (4t^3\hat i - 3t\hat j)\) N where \(t\) is the time in second. If mass starts from origin at \(t = 0\), the velocity and position after \(t = 2\) s will be:
o: \(\vec v = 3\hat i + \frac32\hat j,\ \ \vec r = \frac65\hat i + \hat j\)
\(\vec v = 4\hat i - \frac32\hat j,\ \ \vec r = \frac65\hat i - \hat j\)
\(\vec v = 4\hat i - \frac32\hat j,\ \ \vec r = \frac85\hat i - \hat j\)
\(\vec v = 4\hat i + \frac52\hat j,\ \ \vec r = \frac85\hat i + 2\hat j\)
questions.sol: \(\vec a = \vec F/4 = t^3\hat i - \tfrac34t\hat j\). Integrating from rest: \(\vec v = \tfrac{t^4}{4}\hat i - \tfrac38t^2\hat j = 4\hat i - \tfrac32\hat j\) at 2 s; \(\vec r = \tfrac{t^5}{20}\hat i - \tfrac18t^3\hat j = \tfrac85\hat i - \hat j\).

questions.q: Potential energy (\(V\)) versus distance (\(x\)) is given by the graph. Rank various regions as per the magnitudes of the force (\(F\)) acting on a particle from high to low.
questions.sol: \(F = -\dfrac{dV}{dx}\), the slope of the graph. Slopes: BC = 3, AB = 1, DE = 0.5, CD = 0. So \(F_{BC} > F_{AB} > F_{DE} > F_{CD}\).

questions.q: A uniform rod of mass \(m\) and length \(l\) is suspended by means of two identical inextensible light strings as shown in figure. Tension in one string immediately after the other string is cut, is ____ . (\(g\) acceleration due to gravity)
questions.sol: Just after one string is cut, the rod pivots about the other end: \(mg\dfrac l2 = \dfrac{ml^2}{3}\alpha \Rightarrow \alpha = \dfrac{3g}{2l}\), \(a_{cm} = \dfrac{3g}{4}\). \(mg - T = m\dfrac{3g}{4} \Rightarrow T = \dfrac{mg}{4}\).

questions.q: Water flows through a horizontal tube as shown in the figure. The difference in height between the water columns in vertical tubes is 5 cm and the area of cross-sections at \(A\) and \(B\) are 6 cm² and 3 cm² respectively. The rate of flow will be ____ cm³/s. (take \(g = 10\ \text{m/s}^2\))
questions.sol: Bernoulli + continuity: \(Q = A_1A_2\sqrt{\dfrac{2gh}{A_1^2 - A_2^2}} = 18\sqrt{\dfrac{2\times1000\times5}{36 - 9}} = 18\times\dfrac{100}{\sqrt{27}} = 200\sqrt3\ \text{cm}^3/\text{s}\).

questions.q: An aluminium and steel rods having same lengths and cross-sections are joined to make total length of 120 cm at 30°C. The coefficient of linear expansion of aluminium and steel are \(24\times10^{-6}\)/°C and \(1.2\times10^{-5}\)/°C, respectively. The length of this composite rod when its temperature is raised to 100°C, is ____ cm.
questions.sol: Each rod is 60 cm. \(\Delta L = 60\times70\times(24 + 12)\times10^{-6} = 0.151\) cm, so the length becomes 120.15 cm.

questions.q: A gas based geyser heats water flowing at the rate of 5.0 litres per minute from 27°C to 87°C. The rate of consumption of the gas is ____ g/s. (Take heat of combustion of gas \(= 5.0\times10^4\) J/g, specific heat capacity of water = 4200 J/kg·°C)
questions.sol: Water: \(\dfrac{5000\ \text{g}}{60\ \text{s}} = 83.3\) g/s. Heat needed \(= 83.3\times4.2\times60 = 21000\) J/s. Gas \(= \dfrac{21000}{5\times10^4} = 0.42\) g/s.

questions.q: Two strings \((A, B)\) having linear densities \(\mu_A = 2\times10^{-4}\) kg/m and \(\mu_B = 4\times10^{-4}\) kg/m and lengths \(L_A = 2.5\) m and \(L_B = 1.5\) m respectively are joined. Free ends of \(A\) and \(B\) are tied to two rigid supports \(C\) and \(D\), respectively creating a tension of 500 N in the wire. Two identical pulses, sent from \(C\) and \(D\) ends, take time \(t_1\) and \(t_2\), respectively, to reach the joint. The ratio \(t_1/t_2\) is:

Initially a satellite of 100 kg is in a circular orbit of radius \(1.5R_E\). This satellite can be moved to a circular orbit of radius \(3R_E\) by supplying \(\alpha\times10^6\) J of energy. The value of \(\alpha\) is ____ . (Take Radius of Earth \(R_E = 6\times10^6\) m and \(g = 10\ \text{m/s}^2\))
questions.sol: Energy needed \(= \dfrac{GMm}{2}\left(\dfrac{1}{1.5R} - \dfrac{1}{3R}\right) = \dfrac{mgR}{6} = \dfrac{100\times10\times6\times10^6}{6} = 10^9\) J, so \(\alpha = 1000\).

questions.q: A point charge of \(10^{-8}\) C is placed at origin. The work done in moving a point charge 2 μC from point \(A(4, 4, 2)\) m to \(B(2, 2, 1)\) m is ____ J. (\(\frac{1}{4\pi\epsilon_0} = 9\times10^9\) in SI units)
questions.sol: \(r_A = 6\) m, \(r_B = 3\) m. \(W = q(V_B - V_A) = 2\times10^{-6}\times9\times10^9\times10^{-8}\left(\tfrac13 - \tfrac16\right) = 30\times10^{-6}\) J.

questions.q: A parallel plate capacitor has capacitance \(C\), when there is vacuum within the parallel plates. A sheet having thickness \(\left(\frac13\right)^{\text{rd}}\) of the separation between the plates and relative permittivity \(K\) is introduced between the plates. The new capacitance of the system is :
questions.sol: \(C' = \dfrac{\epsilon_0A}{d - t + t/K}\) with \(t = d/3\): \(C' = \dfrac{\epsilon_0A}{d\left(\frac23 + \frac{1}{3K}\right)} = \dfrac{3KC}{2K+1}\).

questions.q: A current carrying solenoid is placed vertically and a particle of mass \(m\) with charge \(Q\) is released from rest. The particle moves along the axis of solenoid. If \(g\) is acceleration due to gravity then the acceleration (a) of the charged particle will satisfy :
questions.sol: On the axis the field is along the motion, so \(\vec v\times\vec B = 0\): no magnetic force. Only gravity acts: \(a = g\).

questions.q: A conducting circular loop of area 1.0 m² is placed perpendicular to a magnetic field which varies as \(B = \sin(100t)\) Tesla. If the resistance of the loop is 100Ω, then the average thermal energy dissipated in the loop in one period is ____ J.
questions.sol: \(\varepsilon = 100\cos(100t)\) V. Average power \(= \dfrac{\varepsilon_0^2}{2R} = \dfrac{10^4}{200} = 50\) W. One period \(= \dfrac{2\pi}{100}\) s, so energy \(= \pi\) J.

questions.q: A 1 m long metal rod AB completes the circuit as shown in figure. The area of circuit is perpendicular to the magnetic field of 0.10 T. If the resistance of the total circuit is 2Ω then the force needed to move the rod towards right with constant speed (\(v\)) of 1.5 m/s is ____ N.
questions.sol: \(F = \dfrac{B^2l^2v}{R} = \dfrac{0.01\times1\times1.5}{2} = 7.5\times10^{-3}\) N.

questions.q: The electric field in a plane electromagnetic wave is given by : \(E_y = 69\sin[0.6\times10^3x - 1.8\times10^{11}t]\) V/m. The expression for magnetic field associated with this electromagnetic wave is ____ T.
questions.sol: \(B_0 = \dfrac{69}{3\times10^8} = 2.3\times10^{-7}\) T, same phase. The wave travels along \(+x\) and \(\vec E\) is along \(y\), so \(\vec B\) is along \(z\) (\(\hat y\times\hat z = \hat x\)).

questions.q: In a double slit experiment the distance between the slits is 0.1 cm and the screen is placed at 50 cm from the slits plane. When one slit is covered with a transparent sheet having thickness \(t\) and refractive index \(n (= 1.5)\), the central fringe shifts by 0.2 cm. The value of \(t\) is ____ cm.
questions.sol: Shift \(= \dfrac{(n-1)tD}{d} \Rightarrow 0.2 = \dfrac{0.5\,t\times50}{0.1} \Rightarrow t = 8\times10^{-4}\) cm.

questions.q: If an alpha particle with energy 7.7 MeV is bombarded on a thin gold foil, the closest distance from nucleus it can reach is ____ m. (Atomic number of gold = 79 and \(\frac{1}{4\pi\epsilon_0} = 9\times10^9\) in SI units)
questions.sol: \(r_0 = \dfrac{k(Ze)(2e)}{E} = \dfrac{9\times10^9\times79\times2\times(1.6\times10^{-19})^2}{7.7\times1.6\times10^{-13}} \approx 2.95\times10^{-14}\) m.

questions.q: A light wave described by \(E = 60[\sin(3\times10^{15})t + \sin(12\times10^{15})t]\) (in SI units) falls on a metal surface of work function 2.8 eV. The maximum kinetic energy of ejected photoelectron is (approximately) ____ eV. (\(h = 6.6\times10^{-34}\) J.s. and \(e = 1.6\times10^{-19}\) C)
questions.sol: Highest frequency \(\omega = 12\times10^{15}\) rad/s: \(E = \dfrac{h\omega}{2\pi} = 1.26\times10^{-18}\) J \(\approx 7.9\) eV. \(K_{max} = 7.9 - 2.8 \approx 5.1\) eV.

questions.q: The given circuit works as :
questions.sol: The first two NOR gates (inputs joined) give \(\bar A\) and \(\bar B\). Their NOR is \(\overline{\bar A + \bar B} = AB\), and the last NOR (inputs joined) inverts it: \(\overline{AB}\), a NAND gate.

questions.q: Two identical thin rods of mass \(M\) kg and length \(L\) m are connected as shown in figure. Moment of inertia of the combined rod system about an axis passing through point \(P\) and perpendicular to the plane of the rods is \(\frac{x}{12}ML^2\) kg m². The value of \(x\) is ____ .
questions.sol: Vertical rod about its end P: \(\dfrac{ML^2}{3}\). Horizontal rod: \(\dfrac{ML^2}{12} + ML^2 = \dfrac{13}{12}ML^2\). Total \(= \dfrac{17}{12}ML^2\), so \(x = 17\).

questions.q: 10 mole of oxygen is heated at constant volume from 30°C to 40°C. The change in the internal energy of the gas is ____ cal. (The molecular specific heat of oxygen at constant pressure, \(C_P = 7\) cal/mol·°C and R = 2 cal/mol·°C.)
questions.sol: \(C_V = C_P - R = 5\) cal/mol·°C. \(\Delta U = nC_V\Delta T = 10\times5\times10 = 500\) cal.

questions.q: The heat generated in 1 minute between points \(A\) and \(B\) in the given circuit, when a battery of 9 V with internal resistance of 1Ω is connected across these points is ____ J.
questions.sol: \(\dfrac12 = \dfrac24\): the bridge is balanced, so the middle 1Ω carries no current. \(R_{AB} = 3\,\|\,6 = 2\ \Omega\). \(I = \dfrac{9}{2+1} = 3\) A. Heat \(= I^2Rt = 9\times2\times60 = 1080\) J.

questions.q: In a microscope the objective is having focal length \(f_o = 2\) cm and eye-piece is having focal length \(f_e = 4\) cm. The tube length is 32 cm. The magnification produced by this microscope for normal adjustment is ____ .
questions.sol: Normal adjustment: \(M = \dfrac{L}{f_o}\cdot\dfrac{D}{f_e} = \dfrac{32}{2}\times\dfrac{25}{4} = 100\).

questions.q: A collimated beam of light of diameter 2 mm is propagating along \(x\)-axis. The beam is required to be expanded in a collimated beam of diameter 14 mm using a system of two convex lenses. If first lens has focal length 40 mm, then the focal length of second lens is ____ mm.
questions.sol: A beam expander: \(\dfrac{f_2}{f_1} = \dfrac{14}{2} = 7 \Rightarrow f_2 = 280\) mm.

questions.q: A quantity Q is formulated as \(X^{-2}Y^{+\frac32}Z^{-\frac25}\). X, Y, and Z are independent parameters which have fractional errors of 0.1, 0.2, and 0.5, respectively in measurement. The maximum fractional error of Q is

Two balls with same mass and initial velocity, are projected at different angles in such a way that maximum height reached by first ball is 8 times higher than that of the second ball. \(T_1\) and \(T_2\) are the total flying times of first and second ball, respectively, then the ratio of \(T_1\) and \(T_2\) is
questions.sol: \(H \propto \sin^2\theta\): \(\dfrac{\sin\theta_1}{\sin\theta_2} = \sqrt8 = 2\sqrt2\). \(T \propto \sin\theta\), so \(T_1 : T_2 = 2\sqrt2 : 1\).

questions.q: A body of mass 2 kg moving with velocity of \(\vec v_{in} = 3\hat i + 4\hat j\) m s\(^{-1}\) enters into a constant force field of 6 N directed along positive \(z\)-axis. If the body remains in the field for a period of \(\frac53\) seconds, then velocity of the body when it emerges from force field is.
questions.sol: \(a = \dfrac62 = 3\) m/s² along \(z\). After \(\dfrac53\) s, \(v_z = 5\) m/s: \(\vec v = 3\hat i + 4\hat j + 5\hat k\).

questions.q: A block of mass 2 kg is attached to one end of a massless spring whose other end is fixed at a wall. The spring-mass system moves on a frictionless horizontal table. The spring's natural length is 2 m and spring constant is 200 N/m. The block is pushed such that the length of the spring becomes 1 m and then released. At distance \(x\) m (\(x < 2\)) from the wall, the speed of the block will be
questions.sol: SHM about \(x = 2\) m with amplitude 1 m and \(\omega = \sqrt{200/2} = 10\) rad/s. \(v = \omega\sqrt{A^2 - (2 - x)^2} = 10[1 - (2 - x)^2]^{1/2}\) m/s.

questions.q: A rod of linear mass density '\(\lambda\)' and length '\(L\)' is bent to form a ring of radius '\(R\)'. Moment of inertia of ring about any of its diameter is.
questions.sol: \(M = \lambda L\), \(R = \dfrac{L}{2\pi}\). About a diameter \(I = \dfrac{MR^2}{2} = \dfrac{\lambda L^3}{8\pi^2}\).

questions.q: A 3 m long wire of radius 3 mm shows an extension of 0.1 mm when loaded vertically by a mass of 50 kg in an experiment to determine Young's modulus. The value of Young's modulus of the wire as per this experiment is \(P\times10^{11}\) N m\(^{-2}\), where the value of \(P\) is: (Take \(g = 3\pi\) m/s²)
questions.sol: \(Y = \dfrac{FL}{A\Delta L} = \dfrac{50\times3\pi\times3}{\pi\times9\times10^{-6}\times10^{-4}} = 5\times10^{11}\) N/m².

questions.q: Water falls from a height of 200 m into a pool. Calculate the rise in temperature of the water assuming no heat dissipation from the water in the pool. (Take \(g\) = 10 m/s², specific heat of water = 4200 J/(kg K))
questions.sol: \(mgh = mc\Delta T \Rightarrow \Delta T = \dfrac{10\times200}{4200} \approx 0.48\) K.

questions.q: A monoatomic gas having \(\gamma = \frac53\) is stored in a thermally insulated container and the gas is suddenly compressed to \(\left(\frac18\right)^{th}\) of its initial volume. The ratio of final pressure and initial pressure is: (\(\gamma\) is the ratio of specific heats of the gas at constant pressure and at constant volume)
questions.sol: \(\dfrac{P_2}{P_1} = \left(\dfrac{V_1}{V_2}\right)^\gamma = 8^{5/3} = 32\).

questions.q: The amplitude and phase of a wave that is formed by the superposition of two harmonic travelling waves, \(y_1(x, t) = 4\sin(kx - \omega t)\) and \(y_2(x, t) = 2\sin\left(kx - \omega t + \frac{2\pi}{3}\right)\), are: (Take the angular frequency of initial waves same as \(\omega\))
questions.sol: \(A = \sqrt{16 + 4 + 2\cdot4\cdot2\cos120^\circ} = \sqrt{12} = 2\sqrt3\). \(\tan\phi = \dfrac{2\sin120^\circ}{4 + 2\cos120^\circ} = \dfrac{\sqrt3}{3} \Rightarrow \phi = \dfrac\pi6\).

questions.q: Two strings with circular cross section and made of same material, are stretched to have same amount of tension. A transverse wave is then made to pass through both the strings. The velocity of the wave in the first string having the radius of cross section \(R\) is \(v_1\), and that in the other string having radius of cross section \(R/2\) is \(v_2\). Then \(\frac{v_2}{v_1}\) =
questions.sol: \(v = \sqrt{T/\mu}\) with \(\mu \propto r^2\), so \(v \propto \dfrac1r\): \(\dfrac{v_2}{v_1} = 2\).

questions.q: Two metal spheres of radius \(R\) and \(3R\) have same surface charge density \(\sigma\). If they are brought in contact and then separated, the surface charge density on smaller and bigger sphere becomes \(\sigma_1\) and \(\sigma_2\), respectively. The ratio \(\frac{\sigma_1}{\sigma_2}\) is
questions.sol: Total charge \(= \sigma(4\pi R^2 + 36\pi R^2) = 40\pi\sigma R^2\). Equal potentials share it in the ratio of radii 1 : 3: \(10\pi\sigma R^2\) and \(30\pi\sigma R^2\). \(\sigma_1 = 2.5\sigma\), \(\sigma_2 = \dfrac56\sigma\), ratio 3.

questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R
Assertion A : Work done in moving a test charge between two points inside a uniformly charged spherical shell is zero, no matter which path is chosen.
Reason R : Electrostatic potential inside a uniformly charged spherical shell is constant and is same as that on the surface of the shell.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below.
o: A is true but R is false
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is false but R is true
questions.sol: Inside the shell the potential is constant and equal to the surface value, so the potential difference, and hence the work, is zero along any path. R explains A.

questions.q:
Electric charge is transferred to an irregular metallic disk as shown in the figure. If \(\sigma_1, \sigma_2, \sigma_3\) and \(\sigma_4\) are charge densities at given points then, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
A. \(\sigma_1 > \sigma_3;\ \sigma_2 = \sigma_4\)
B. \(\sigma_1 > \sigma_2;\ \sigma_3 > \sigma_4\)
C. \(\sigma_1 > \sigma_3 > \sigma_2 = \sigma_4\)
D. \(\sigma_1 < \sigma_3 < \sigma_2 = \sigma_4\)
E. \(\sigma_1 = \sigma_2 = \sigma_3 = \sigma_4\)
questions.sol: Charge density is largest where the surface is most sharply curved: the point at 1 most, then 3; points 2 and 4 are alike. So A, B and C hold.

questions.q: An infinitely long wire has uniform linear charge density \(\lambda\) = 2 nC/m. The net flux through a Gaussian cube of side length \(\sqrt3\) cm, if the wire passes through any two corners of the cube, that are maximally displaced from each other, would be \(x\) N m² C\(^{-1}\), where \(x\) is: [Neglect any edge effects and use \(\frac{1}{4\pi\epsilon_0} = 9\times10^9\) SI units]
questions.sol: The wire runs along the body diagonal, inside length \(\sqrt3\times\sqrt3 = 3\) cm. \(\phi = \dfrac{\lambda l}{\epsilon_0} = 2\times10^{-9}\times0.03\times4\pi\times9\times10^9 = 2.16\pi\).

questions.q: Figure shows a current carrying square loop ABCD of edge length '\(a\)' lying in a plane. If the resistance of the ABC part is \(r\) and that of ADC part is \(2r\), then the magnitude of the resultant magnetic field at centre of the square loop is
questions.sol: Currents split 2 : 1: \(\dfrac{2I}{3}\) through ABC and \(\dfrac I3\) through ADC. Each side contributes \(\dfrac{\sqrt2\mu_0i}{2\pi a}\); the two halves oppose: \(B = 2\times\dfrac{\sqrt2\mu_0}{2\pi a}\left(\dfrac{2I}{3} - \dfrac I3\right) = \dfrac{\sqrt2\mu_0I}{3\pi a}\).

questions.q: In a Young's double slit experiment, the source is white light. One of the slits is covered by red filter and another by a green filter. In this case:
o: there shall be alternate interference fringes of red and green.
there shall be an interference pattern for red distinct from that for green.
there shall be an interference pattern, where each fringe's pattern center is green and outer edges is red.
there shall be no interference fringes.
questions.sol: Red and green light from the two slits have different frequencies, so they are not coherent: no interference fringes.

questions.q: A convex lens of focal length 30 cm is placed in contact with a concave lens of focal length 20 cm. An object is placed at 20 cm to the left of this lens system. The distance of the image from the lens in cm is ____ .
questions.sol: \(\dfrac1F = \dfrac1{30} - \dfrac1{20} = -\dfrac1{60}\). \(\dfrac1v = -\dfrac1{60} - \dfrac1{20} \Rightarrow v = -15\) cm.

questions.q: A concave-convex lens of refractive index 1.5 and the radii of curvature of its surfaces are 30 cm and 20 cm, respectively. The concave surface is upwards and is filled with a liquid of refractive index 1.3. The focal length of the liquid-glass combination will be
questions.sol: Glass meniscus: \(0.5\left(\dfrac1{20} - \dfrac1{30}\right) = \dfrac1{120}\). Liquid lens (plano-convex, \(R = 30\) cm): \(\dfrac{0.3}{30} = \dfrac1{100}\). Total \(= \dfrac{11}{600}\), \(f = \dfrac{600}{11}\) cm.

questions.q: For a nucleus of mass number \(A\) and radius \(R\), the mass density of nucleus can be represented as
questions.sol: \(\rho \propto \dfrac{A}{R^3} = \dfrac{A}{R_0^3A}\): independent of \(A\).

questions.q: The output voltage in the following circuit is (Consider ideal diode case)
questions.sol: \(D_2\) (anode at the output node, cathode to ground) is forward biased, so the output is held at 0 V; \(D_1\) is then reverse biased.

questions.q: A thin solid disk of 1 kg is rotating along its diameter axis at the speed of 1800 rpm. By applying an external torque of \(25\pi\) N m for 40 s, the speed increases to 2100 rpm. The diameter of the disk is ____ m.
questions.sol: \(\Delta\omega = 300\times\dfrac{2\pi}{60} = 10\pi\) rad/s. \(25\pi\times40 = I\times10\pi \Rightarrow I = 100 = \dfrac{MR^2}{4} \Rightarrow R = 20\) m, diameter 40 m.

questions.q: A sample of a liquid is kept at 1 atm. It is compressed to 5 atm which leads to a change of volume of 0.8 cm³. If the bulk modulus of the liquid is 2 GPa, the initial volume of the liquid was ____ litre. (Take 1 atm = \(10^5\) Pa)
questions.sol: \(V = \dfrac{B\Delta V}{\Delta P} = \dfrac{2\times10^9\times0.8\times10^{-6}}{4\times10^5} = 4\times10^{-3}\) m³ = 4 L.

questions.q: A cube having a side of 10 cm with unknown mass and 200 gm mass were hung at two ends of a uniform rigid rod of 27 cm long. The rod along with masses was placed on a wedge keeping the distance between wedge point and 200 gm weight as 25 cm. Initially the masses were not at balance. A beaker is placed beneath the unknown mass and water is added slowly to it. At given point the masses were in balance and half volume of the unknown mass was inside the water. (Take the density of unknown mass is more than that of the water, the mass did not absorb water and water density is 1 gm/cm³.) The unknown mass is ____ kg.
questions.sol: Wedge is 2 cm from the cube. \((M - 500)\times2 = 200\times25\) (buoyancy of half of 1000 cm³ = 500 g). \(M = 3000\) g = 3 kg.

questions.q: Space between the plates of a parallel plate capacitor of plate area 4 cm² and separation of 1.77 mm, is filled with uniform dielectric materials with dielectric constants (3 and 5) as shown in figure. Another capacitor of capacitance 7.5 pF is connected in parallel with it. The effective capacitance of this combination is ____ pF. (Given \(\epsilon_0 = 8.85\times10^{-12}\) F/m)
questions.sol: Two layers of \(d/2\) in series: \(C = \dfrac{2\epsilon_0A}{d}\cdot\dfrac{3\times5}{3 + 5} = 4\ \text{pF}\times\dfrac{15}{8} = 7.5\) pF. With 7.5 pF in parallel: 15 pF.

questions.q: An electron is released from rest near an infinite non-conducting sheet of uniform charge density '\(-\sigma\)'. The rate of change of de-Broglie wave length associated with the electron varies inversely as \(n^{th}\) power of time. The numerical value of \(n\) is ____ .
questions.sol: Constant field: \(p = eEt\), \(\lambda = \dfrac{h}{eEt}\), so \(\dfrac{d\lambda}{dt} \propto \dfrac1{t^2}\): \(n = 2\).

questions.q: The dimension of \(\sqrt{\frac{\mu_0}{\epsilon_0}}\) is equal to that of: (\(\mu_0\) = Vacuum permeability and \(\epsilon_0\) = Vacuum permittivity)
questions.sol: \(\sqrt{\mu_0/\epsilon_0} \approx 377\ \Omega\), the impedance of free space: the dimension of resistance.

questions.q:
Match List - I with List - II.

(A) Mass density(I) \([ML^2T^{-3}]\)
(B) Impulse(II) \([MLT^{-1}]\)
(C) Power(III) \([ML^2T^0]\)
(D) Moment of inertia(IV) \([ML^{-3}T^0]\)
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.sol: Density \([ML^{-3}]\) (IV); impulse \([MLT^{-1}]\) (II); power \([ML^2T^{-3}]\) (I); moment of inertia \([ML^2]\) (III).

questions.q: A helicopter flying horizontally with a speed of 360 km/h at an altitude of 2 km, drops an object at an instant. The object hits the ground at a point O, 20 s after it is dropped. Displacement of 'O' from the position of helicopter where the object was released is : (use acceleration due to gravity \(g\) = 10 m/s² and neglect air resistance)
questions.sol: Horizontal \(= 100\times20 = 2\) km; it falls 2 km. Displacement \(= 2\sqrt2\) km.

questions.q: An object with mass 500 g moves along \(x\)-axis with speed \(v = 4\sqrt x\) m/s. The force acting on the object is :
questions.sol: \(a = v\dfrac{dv}{dx} = 4\sqrt x\cdot\dfrac{2}{\sqrt x} = 8\) m/s². \(F = 0.5\times8 = 4\) N.

questions.q: Which one of the following forces cannot be expressed in terms of potential energy?
questions.sol: Friction is non-conservative (its work depends on the path), so it has no potential energy.

questions.q: A capillary tube of radius 0.1 mm is partly dipped in water (surface tension 70 dyn/cm and glass water contact angle ≈ 0°) with 30° inclined with the vertical. The length of water risen in the capillary is ____ cm. (Take \(g\) = 9.8 m/s²)
questions.sol: Vertical rise \(h = \dfrac{2T}{\rho gr} = \dfrac{2\times0.07}{1000\times9.8\times10^{-4}} = 14.3\) cm. Along the tube: \(\dfrac{h}{\cos30^\circ} \approx 16.5\) cm \(\approx \dfrac{82}{5}\) cm.

questions.q:
Match List - I with List - II.
List-IList-II
(A) Isothermal(I) \(\Delta W\) (work done) = 0
(B) Adiabatic(II) \(\Delta Q\) (supplied heat) = 0
(C) Isobaric(III) \(\Delta U\) (change in internal energy) \(\ne\) 0
(D) Isochoric(IV) \(\Delta U\) = 0
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.sol: Isothermal \(\Delta U = 0\); adiabatic \(\Delta Q = 0\); isobaric \(\Delta U \ne 0\); isochoric \(\Delta W = 0\).

questions.q: The helium and argon are put in the flask at the same room temperature (300 K). The ratio of average kinetic energies (per molecule) of helium and argon is: (Give: Molar mass of helium = 4 g/mol, Molar mass of argon = 40 g/mol)
questions.sol: Average kinetic energy per molecule is \(\dfrac32kT\), independent of mass: 1 : 1.

questions.q: The equation of a wave travelling on a string is \(y = \sin[20\pi x + 10\pi t]\), where \(x\) and \(t\) are distance and time in SI units. The minimum distance between two points having the same oscillating speed is :
questions.sol: \(\lambda = \dfrac{2\pi}{20\pi} = 0.1\) m. Points half a wavelength apart oscillate with equal (opposite) velocities: 5 cm.

questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).
Assertion (A) : The radius vector from the Sun to a planet sweeps out equal areas in equal intervals of time and thus areal velocity of planet is constant.
Reason (R) : For a central force field the angular momentum is a constant.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
o: (A) is not correct but (R) is correct
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
questions.sol: Gravity is a central force, so \(L\) is constant; areal velocity \(= \dfrac{L}{2m}\) is then constant. R explains A.

questions.q: A dipole with two electric charges of 2 μC magnitude each, with separation distance 0.5 μm, is placed between the plates of a capacitor such that its axis is parallel to an electric field established between the plates when a potential difference of 5 V is applied. Separation between the plates is 0.5 mm. If the dipole is rotated by 30° from the axis, it tends to realign in the direction due to a torque. The value of torque is:

Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).
Assertion (A) : The outer body of an aircraft is made of metal which protects persons sitting inside from lightning strikes.
Reason (R) : The electric field inside the cavity enclosed by a conductor is zero.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
o: Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.sol: The metal body acts as a closed conductor; the field inside its cavity is zero, which protects the people inside.

questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).
Assertion (A) : Magnetic monopoles do not exist.
Reason (R) : Magnetic field lines are continuous and form closed loops.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
o: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
questions.sol: Closed, continuous field lines mean there are no sources or sinks of B, i.e. no monopoles.

questions.q: The unit of \(\sqrt{\frac{2I}{\epsilon_0c}}\) is : (\(I\) = intensity of an electromagnetic wave, \(c\) = speed of light)
questions.sol: \(I = \tfrac12c\epsilon_0E_0^2 \Rightarrow \sqrt{\dfrac{2I}{\epsilon_0c}} = E_0\), measured in N/C.

questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).
Assertion (A) : Refractive index of glass is higher than that of air.
Reason (R) : Optical density of a medium is directly proportionate to its mass density which results in a proportionate refractive index.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
o: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
questions.sol: Glass does have a higher refractive index than air, but optical density is not proportional to mass density.

questions.q: A mirror is used to produce an image with magnification of \(\frac14\). If the distance between object and its image is 40 cm, then the focal length of the mirror is ____ .
questions.sol: An erect \(\frac14\) image means a convex mirror: \(u = -32\) cm, \(v = +8\) cm (distance 40 cm). \(\dfrac1f = \dfrac18 - \dfrac1{32} = \dfrac3{32} \Rightarrow f \approx 10.7\) cm.

questions.q: A transparent block A having refractive index \(\mu\) = 1.25 is surrounded by another medium of refractive index \(\mu\) = 1.0 as shown in the figure. A light ray is incident on the flat face of the block with incident angle \(\theta\) as shown in the figure. What is the maximum value of \(\theta\) for which light suffers total internal reflection at the top surface of the block?
questions.sol: TIR at the top needs \(\sin(90^\circ - r) \ge \dfrac1{1.25} = 0.8 \Rightarrow \sin r \le 0.6\). Then \(\sin\theta = 1.25\sin r \le 0.75\): \(\theta_{max} = \sin^{-1}\dfrac34\).

questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).
Assertion (A) : The density of the copper (\({}^{64}_{29}\text{Cu}\)) nucleus is greater than that of the carbon (\({}^{12}_6\text{C}\)) nucleus.
Reason (R) : The nucleus of mass number \(A\) has a radius proportional to \(A^{1/3}\).
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
o: (A) is correct but (R) is not correct
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.sol: \(R \propto A^{1/3}\) makes nuclear density the same for all nuclei: A is wrong, R is right.

questions.q: A photoemissive substance is illuminated with a radiation of wavelength \(\lambda_i\) so that it releases electrons with de-Broglie wavelength \(\lambda_e\). The longest wavelength of radiation that can emit photoelectron is \(\lambda_o\). Expression for de-Broglie wavelength is given by: (\(m\): mass of the electron, \(h\): Planck's constant and \(c\): speed of light)
questions.sol: \(\dfrac{p^2}{2m} = hc\left(\dfrac1{\lambda_i} - \dfrac1{\lambda_o}\right)\), so \(\lambda_e = \dfrac hp = \sqrt{\dfrac{h}{2mc\left(\frac1{\lambda_i} - \frac1{\lambda_o}\right)}}\).

questions.q: Consider the following logic circuit. The output is \(Y = 0\) when :

Let \(M\) and \(R\) be the mass and radius of a disc. A small disc of radius \(R/3\) is removed from the bigger disc as shown in figure. The moment of inertia of remaining part of bigger disc about an axis AB passing through the centre O and perpendicular to the plane of disc is \(\frac4xMR^2\). The value of \(x\) is ____ .
questions.sol: Removed disc: mass \(\dfrac M9\), centre \(\dfrac{2R}{3}\) from O. Its \(I = \dfrac M9\left(\dfrac{R^2}{18} + \dfrac{4R^2}{9}\right) = \dfrac{MR^2}{18}\). Remainder \(= \dfrac{MR^2}{2} - \dfrac{MR^2}{18} = \dfrac49MR^2\), so \(x = 9\).

questions.q: Two cylindrical rods A and B made of different materials, are joined in a straight line. The ratios of lengths, radii and thermal conductivities of these rods are: \(\frac{L_A}{L_B} = \frac12\), \(\frac{r_A}{r_B} = 2\) and \(\frac{K_A}{K_B} = \frac12\). The free ends of rods A and B are maintained at 400 K, 200 K, respectively. The temperature of rods interface is ____ K, when equilibrium is established.
questions.sol: Thermal resistance \(\propto \dfrac{L}{Kr^2}\): \(\dfrac{R_A}{R_B} = \dfrac{1/2}{(1/2)(4)} = \dfrac14\). The 200 K drop splits 1 : 4, so the interface is at \(400 - 40 = 360\) K.

questions.q: The electric field in a region is given by \(\vec E = (2\hat i + 4\hat j + 6\hat k)\times10^3\) N/C. The flux of the field through a rectangular surface parallel to \(x - z\) plane is 6.0 N m² C\(^{-1}\). The area of the surface is ____ cm².
questions.sol: Normal along \(\hat j\): \(\phi = 4\times10^3A = 6 \Rightarrow A = 1.5\times10^{-3}\) m² = 15 cm².

questions.q: A parallel plate capacitor has charge \(5\times10^{-6}\) C. A dielectric slab is inserted between the plates and almost fills the space between the plates. If the induced charge on one face of the slab is \(4\times10^{-6}\) C then the dielectric constant of the slab is ____ .
questions.sol: \(q_{ind} = q\left(1 - \dfrac1K\right) \Rightarrow 4 = 5\left(1 - \dfrac1K\right) \Rightarrow K = 5\).

questions.q: An inductor of reactance 100 Ω, a capacitor of reactance 50 Ω, and a resistor of resistance 50 Ω are connected in series with an AC source of 10 V, 50 Hz. Average power dissipated by the circuit is ____ W.

Two projectiles are fired from ground with same initial speeds from same point at angles \((45^\circ + \alpha)\) and \((45^\circ - \alpha)\) with horizontal direction. The ratio of their times of flights is
questions.sol: \(T \propto \sin\theta\): \(\dfrac{\sin(45^\circ + \alpha)}{\sin(45^\circ - \alpha)} = \dfrac{\cos\alpha + \sin\alpha}{\cos\alpha - \sin\alpha} = \dfrac{1 + \tan\alpha}{1 - \tan\alpha}\).

questions.q: A cubic block of mass \(m\) is sliding down on an inclined plane at 60° with an acceleration of \(\frac g2\), the value of coefficient of kinetic friction is
questions.sol: \(a = g(\sin60^\circ - \mu\cos60^\circ) = \dfrac g2 \Rightarrow \dfrac{\sqrt3}{2} - \dfrac\mu2 = \dfrac12 \Rightarrow \mu = \sqrt3 - 1\).

questions.q: An object of mass 1000 g experiences a time dependent force \(\vec F = (2t\hat i + 3t^2\hat j)\) N. The power generated by the force at time \(t\) is:
questions.sol: \(m = 1\) kg, so \(\vec v = \int\vec F\,dt = t^2\hat i + t^3\hat j\). \(P = \vec F\cdot\vec v = 2t^3 + 3t^5\) W.

questions.q: A rod of length 5 L is bent right angle keeping one side length as 2 L. The position of the centre of mass of the system : (Consider L = 10 cm)
questions.sol: Vertical part: \(\frac35\) of the mass at \((0, 15)\) cm. Horizontal part: \(\frac25\) at \((10, 0)\) cm. Centre of mass \(= (4, 9)\) cm.

questions.q: Two wires A and B are made of same material having ratio of lengths \(\frac{L_A}{L_B} = \frac13\) and their diameters ratio \(\frac{d_A}{d_B} = 2\). If both the wires are stretched using same force, what would be the ratio of their respective elongations?
questions.sol: \(\Delta L = \dfrac{FL}{AY} \propto \dfrac{L}{d^2}\): \(\dfrac{\Delta L_A}{\Delta L_B} = \dfrac13\times\dfrac14 = \dfrac1{12}\).

(B)Diatomic non-rigid gas(II)\(\frac{C_p}{C_v} = \frac75\)
