(D)Diatomic rigid gas(IV)\(\frac{C_p}{C_v} = \frac97\)
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.sol: Triatomic rigid: \(f = 6\), \(\gamma = \dfrac43\) (III). Diatomic non-rigid: \(f = 7\), \(\gamma = \dfrac97\) (IV). Monoatomic: \(\dfrac53\) (I). Diatomic rigid: \(\dfrac75\) (II).

questions.q: Two harmonic waves moving in the same direction superimpose to form a wave \(x = a\cos(1.5t)\cos(50.5t)\) where \(t\) is in seconds. Find the period with which they beat. (close to nearest integer)
questions.sol: \(\cos(1.5t)\cos(50.5t)\) comes from frequencies \(52\) and \(49\) rad/s. Beat \(\omega = 3\) rad/s, period \(\dfrac{2\pi}{3} \approx 2\) s.

questions.q: Two charges \(q_1\) and \(q_2\) are separated by a distance of 30 cm. A third charge \(q_3\) initially at 'C' as shown in the figure, is moved along the circular path of radius 40 cm from C to D. If the difference in potential energy due to movement of \(q_3\) from C to D is given by \(\frac{q_3K}{4\pi\epsilon_0}\), the value of \(K\) is :
questions.sol: The distance to \(q_1\) stays 40 cm. To \(q_2\): 50 cm at C and 10 cm at D. \(\Delta U = \dfrac{q_3q_2}{4\pi\epsilon_0}\left(\dfrac1{0.1} - \dfrac1{0.5}\right) = \dfrac{q_3}{4\pi\epsilon_0}(8q_2)\).

questions.q: A wire of resistance \(R\) is bent into a triangular pyramid as shown in figure with each segment having same length. The resistance between points A and B is \(R/n\). The value of \(n\) is :
questions.sol: Six equal edges of \(\dfrac R6\). Between two vertices of a tetrahedron the resistance is half an edge: \(\dfrac{R}{12}\), so \(n = 12\).

questions.q: A particle of charge \(q\), mass \(m\) and kinetic energy \(E\) enters in magnetic field perpendicular to its velocity and undergoes a circular arc of radius (\(r\)). Which of the following curves represents the variation of \(r\) with \(E\) ?
questions.sol: \(r = \dfrac{\sqrt{2mE}}{qB} \propto \sqrt E\): a curve rising from the origin and bending over, graph (A).

questions.q: Uniform magnetic fields of different strengths (\(B_1\) and \(B_2\)), both normal to the plane of the paper exist as shown in the figure. A charged particle of mass \(m\) and charge \(q\), at the interface at an instant, moves into the region 2 with velocity \(v\) and returns to the interface. It continues to move into region 1 and finally reaches the interface. What is the displacement of the particle during this movement along the interface? (Consider the velocity of the particle to be normal to the magnetic field and \(B_2 > B_1\))
questions.sol: It makes a semicircle of diameter \(\dfrac{2mv}{qB_2}\) in region 2, then one of \(\dfrac{2mv}{qB_1}\) in region 1, the other way along the interface. Net displacement \(= \dfrac{2mv}{qB_1}\left(1 - \dfrac{B_1}{B_2}\right)\).

questions.q: The percentage increase in magnetic field (B) when space within a current carrying solenoid is filled with magnesium (magnetic susceptibility \(\chi_{Mg} = 1.2\times10^{-5}\)) is :
questions.sol: \(B\) increases by the factor \((1 + \chi)\): \(1.2\times10^{-5}\times100\% = 1.2\times10^{-3}\% = \dfrac65\times10^{-3}\%\).

questions.q: An ac current is represented as \(i = 5\sqrt2 + 10\cos\left(650\pi t + \frac\pi6\right)\) Amp. The r.m.s value of the current is

If \(\epsilon_0\) denotes the permittivity of free space and \(\Phi_E\) is the flux of the electric field through the area bounded by the closed surface, then dimensions of \(\left(\epsilon_0\frac{d\phi_E}{dt}\right)\) are that of :
questions.sol: \(\epsilon_0\dfrac{d\phi_E}{dt}\) is the displacement current, so it has the dimensions of current.

questions.q: Two plane polarized light waves combine at a certain point whose electric field components are \(E_1 = E_0\sin\omega t\) and \(E_2 = E_0\sin\left(\omega t + \frac\pi3\right)\). Find the amplitude of the resultant wave.
questions.sol: \(A = 2E_0\cos\dfrac\pi6 = \sqrt3E_0 \approx 1.7E_0\).

questions.q: Two thin convex lenses of focal lengths 30 cm and 10 cm are placed coaxially, 10 cm apart. The power of this combination is:
questions.sol: \(\dfrac1F = \dfrac1{30} + \dfrac1{10} - \dfrac{10}{300} = \dfrac1{10}\) per cm, so \(P = 10\) D.

questions.q: A lens having refractive index 1.6 has focal length of 12 cm, when it is in air. Find the focal length of the lens when it is placed in water. (Take refractive index of water as 1.28)
In a hydrogen like ion, the energy difference between the 2\(^{nd}\) excitation energy state and ground is 108.8 eV. The atomic number of the ion is:
questions.sol: The second excited state is \(n = 3\): \(13.6Z^2\left(1 - \dfrac19\right) = 12.09Z^2 = 108.8 \Rightarrow Z = 3\).

questions.q: For a hydrogen atom, the ratio of the largest wavelength of Lyman series to that of the Balmer series is
questions.sol: Longest Lyman: \(\dfrac1\lambda \propto \dfrac34\); longest Balmer: \(\dfrac{5}{36}\). Ratio \(= \dfrac{5/36}{3/4} = \dfrac{5}{27}\).

questions.q: In the following circuit, the reading of the ammeter will be (Take Zener breakdown voltage = 4 V)
questions.sol: The Zener holds 4 V across the 400 Ω branch: \(I = \dfrac{4}{400} = 10\) mA.

questions.q: A, B and C are disc, solid sphere and spherical shell respectively with same radii and masses. These masses are placed as shown in figure. The moment of inertia of the given system about PQ axis is \(\frac{x}{15}I\), where \(I\) is the moment of inertia of the disc about its diameter. The value of \(x\) is ____ .
questions.sol: With \(I = \dfrac{MR^2}{4}\) (disc about its diameter, through PQ): sphere B, its centre \(R\) from PQ, gives \(\dfrac75MR^2 = \dfrac{28}{5}I\); shell C gives \(\dfrac53MR^2 = \dfrac{20}{3}I\). Total \(= \left(1 + \dfrac{28}{5} + \dfrac{20}{3}\right)I = \dfrac{199}{15}I\).

questions.q: A wire of length 10 cm and diameter 0.5 mm is used in a bulb. The temperature of the wire is 1727°C and power radiated by the wire is 94.2 W. Its emissivity is \(\frac x8\) where \(x\) = ____ . (Given \(\sigma = 6.0\times10^{-8}\) W m\(^{-2}\) K\(^{-4}\), \(\pi\) = 3.14 and assume that the emissivity of wire material is same at all wavelength.)
An ideal gas has undergone through the cyclic process as shown in the figure. Work done by the gas in the entire cycle is ____ \(\times10^{-1}\) J. (Take \(\pi\) = 3.14)
questions.sol: Work = area of the circle \(= \pi\times(100\times10^3\text{ Pa})\times(100\times10^{-6}\text{ m}^3) = 31.4\) J \(= 314\times10^{-1}\) J.

questions.q: For ac circuit shown in figure, \(R = 100\) kΩ and \(C = 100\) pF and the phase difference between \(V_{in}\) and \((V_B - V_A)\) is 90°. The input signal frequency is \(10^x\) rad/sec, where '\(x\)' is ____ .
questions.sol: \(V_B - V_A\) is at 90° to \(V_{in}\) when \(\omega RC = 1\): \(\omega = \dfrac{1}{10^5\times10^{-10}} = 10^5\) rad/s, so \(x = 5\).

questions.q: A container contains a liquid with refractive index of 1.2 up to a height of 60 cm and another liquid having refractive index 1.6 is added to height \(H\) above first liquid. If viewed from above, the apparent shift in the position of bottom of container is 40 cm. The value of \(H\) is ____ cm. (Consider liquids are immisible)
questions.sol: Shift \(= 60\left(1 - \dfrac1{1.2}\right) + H\left(1 - \dfrac1{1.6}\right) = 10 + 0.375H = 40 \Rightarrow H = 80\) cm.

questions.q: In an electromagnetic system, a quantity defined as the ratio of electric dipole moment and magnetic dipole moment has dimension of \([M^PL^QT^RA^S]\). The value of \(P\) and \(Q\) are :
questions.sol: \(\dfrac{p_e}{m} = \dfrac{(\text{C m})}{(\text{A m}^2)} = \dfrac{\text{A s m}}{\text{A m}^2} = [L^{-1}T]\): \(P = 0\), \(Q = -1\).

questions.q: For the determination of refractive index of glass slab, a travelling microscope is used whose main scale contains 300 equal divisions equals to 15 cm. The vernier scale attached to the microscope has 25 divisions equals to 24 divisions of main scale. The least count (LC) of the travelling microscope is (in cm) :

The displacement \(x\) versus time graph is shown below.
(A) The average velocity during 0 to 3 s is 10 m/s
(B) The average velocity during 3 to 5 s is 0 m/s
(C) The instantaneous velocity at \(t\) = 2 s is 5 m/s
(D) The average velocity during 5 to 7 s and instantaneous velocity at \(t\) = 6.5 s are equal
(E) The average velocity from \(t\) = 0 to \(t\) = 9 s is zero
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.sol: From the graph: 3–5 s flat, so 0 m/s (B); the slope from 1 s to 3 s is \(\dfrac{10}{2} = 5\) m/s, so at 2 s, 5 m/s (C); \(x = 0\) at both 0 s and 9 s, so the average is 0 (E). The average 0–3 s is \(\dfrac53\) m/s, and 5–7 s gives \(-2.5\) m/s against \(-10\) m/s at 6.5 s.

questions.q: A block of mass 25 kg is pulled along a horizontal surface by a force at an angle 45° with the horizontal. The friction coefficient between the block and the surface is 0.25. The block travels at a uniform velocity. The work done by the applied force during a displacement of 5 m of the block is :
questions.sol: \(F\cos45^\circ = \mu(mg - F\sin45^\circ) \Rightarrow \dfrac{F}{\sqrt2}(1.25) = 0.25\times245 \Rightarrow \dfrac{F}{\sqrt2} = 49\) N. \(W = \dfrac{F}{\sqrt2}\times5 = 245\) J.

questions.q: A wheel is rolling on a plane surface. The speed of a particle on the highest point of the rim is 8 m/s. The speed of the particle on the rim of the wheel at the same level as the centre of wheel, will be :
questions.sol: Top: \(2v = 8 \Rightarrow v = 4\) m/s. At centre height the velocity is \(v\) forward and \(v\) vertical: \(4\sqrt2\) m/s.

questions.q: A cylindrical rod of length 1 m and radius 4 cm is mounted vertically. It is subjected to a shear force of \(10^5\) N at the top. Considering infinitesimally small displacement in the upper edge, the angular displacement \(\theta\) of the rod axis from its original position would be : (shear moduli, \(G = 10^{10}\) N/m²)

Consider a rectangular sheet of solid material of length \(l\) = 9 cm and width \(d\) = 4 cm. The coefficient of linear expansion is \(\alpha = 3.1\times10^{-5}\) K\(^{-1}\) at room temperature and one atmospheric pressure. The mass of sheet \(m\) = 0.1 kg and the specific heat capacity \(C_v\) = 900 J kg\(^{-1}\) K\(^{-1}\). If the amount of heat supplied to the material is \(8.1\times10^2\) J then change in area of the rectangular sheet is :
questions.sol: \(\Delta T = \dfrac{810}{0.1\times900} = 9\) K. \(\Delta A = 2\alpha A\Delta T = 2\times3.1\times10^{-5}\times36\times10^{-4}\times9 \approx 2.0\times10^{-6}\) m².

questions.q:
Match List - I with List - II.
List-IList-II
(A)Isobaric(I)\(\Delta Q = \Delta W\)
(B)Isochoric(II)\(\Delta Q = \Delta U\)
(C)Adiabatic(III)\(\Delta Q\) = zero
(D)Isothermal(IV)\(\Delta Q = \Delta U + P\Delta V\)
\(\Delta Q\) = Heat supplied, \(\Delta W\) = Work done by the system, \(\Delta U\) = Change in internal energy, \(P\) = Pressure of the system, \(\Delta V\) = Change in volume of the system.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.sol: Isobaric: \(\Delta Q = \Delta U + P\Delta V\); isochoric: \(\Delta Q = \Delta U\); adiabatic: \(\Delta Q = 0\); isothermal: \(\Delta Q = \Delta W\).

questions.q: There are two vessels filled with an ideal gas where volume of one is double the volume of other. The large vessel contains the gas at 8 kPa at 1000 K while the smaller vessel contains the gas at 7 kPa at 500 K. If the vessels are connected to each other by a thin tube allowing the gas to flow and the temperature of both vessels is maintained at 600 K, at steady state the pressure in the vessels will be (in kPa).
questions.sol: Moles \(\propto \dfrac{PV}{T}\): \(\dfrac{8\times2V}{1000} + \dfrac{7\times V}{500} = 0.03V = \dfrac{P\times3V}{600} \Rightarrow P = 6\) kPa.

questions.q: Displacement of a wave is expressed as \(x(t) = 5\cos\left(628t + \frac\pi2\right)\) m. The wavelength of the wave when its velocity is 300 m/s is : (\(\pi\) = 3.14)

An object is kept at rest at a distance of \(3R\) above the earth's surface where \(R\) is earth's radius. The minimum speed with which it must be projected so that it does not return to earth is : (Assume \(M\) = mass of earth, \(G\) = Universal gravitational constant)
questions.sol: At \(r = 4R\), escape speed \(= \sqrt{\dfrac{2GM}{4R}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{GM}{2R}}\).

questions.q: A metallic ring is uniformly charged as shown in figure. AC and BD are two mutually perpendicular diameters. Electric field due to arc AB at '\(O\)' is '\(E\)' in magnitude. What would be the magnitude of electric field at '\(O\)' due to arc ABC ?
questions.sol: Arc ABC is arcs AB and BC; their fields at O are each \(E\) and at right angles: \(\sqrt2E\).

questions.q: There are '\(n\)' number of identical electric bulbs, each is designed to draw a power \(p\) independently from the mains supply. They are now joined in series across the mains supply. The total power drawn by the combination is :
questions.sol: Each bulb has \(R = \dfrac{V^2}{p}\). In series \(P = \dfrac{V^2}{nR} = \dfrac pn\).

questions.q: From the combination of resistors with resistances values \(R_1 = R_2 = R_3 = 5\ \Omega\) and \(R_4 = 10\ \Omega\), which of the following combination is the best circuit to get an equivalent resistance of 6 Ω ?

Three parallel plate capacitors \(C_1\), \(C_2\) and \(C_3\) each of capacitance 5 μF are connected as shown in figure. The effective capacitance between points A and B, when the space between the parallel plates of \(C_1\) capacitor is filled with a dielectric medium having dielectric constant of 4, is :
questions.sol: \(C_1 = 20\ \mu\)F with the dielectric; in series with \(C_2\): \(\dfrac{20\times5}{25} = 4\ \mu\)F; parallel with \(C_3\): \(4 + 5 = 9\ \mu\)F.

questions.q: Two polarisers \(P_1\) and \(P_2\) are placed in such a way that the intensity of the transmitted light will be zero. A third polariser \(P_3\) is inserted in between \(P_1\) and \(P_2\), at particular angle between \(P_2\) and \(P_3\). The transmitted intensity of the light passing through all three polarisers is maximum. The angle between the polarisers \(P_2\) and \(P_3\) is :
questions.sol: \(I = \dfrac{I_0}{2}\cos^2\theta\sin^2\theta = \dfrac{I_0}{8}\sin^22\theta\), largest at \(\theta = 45^\circ = \dfrac\pi4\).

questions.q: A finite size object is placed normal to the principal axis at a distance of 30 cm from a convex mirror of focal length 30 cm. A plane mirror is now placed in such a way that the image produced by both the mirrors coincide with each other. The distance between the two mirrors is :
questions.sol: Convex mirror: \(\dfrac1v = \dfrac1{30} + \dfrac1{30} \Rightarrow v = 15\) cm behind it, i.e. 45 cm from the object. The plane mirror must be 22.5 cm from the object, which is \(30 - 22.5 = 7.5\) cm from the convex mirror.

questions.q: A radioactive material P first decays into Q and then Q decays to non-radioactive material R. Which of the following figure represents time dependent mass of P, Q and R ?
questions.sol: P decays exponentially; Q rises, peaks, then falls as it decays; R rises steadily towards the total mass: figure (B).

questions.q:
Given below are two statements :
Statement (I) : The dimensions of Planck's constant and angular momentum are same.
Statement (II) : In Bohr's model electron revolve around the nucleus only in those orbits for which angular momentum is integral multiple of Planck's constant.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
o: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.sol: \(h\) and angular momentum are both J s (I correct). Bohr's rule is \(L = \dfrac{nh}{2\pi}\), not an integral multiple of \(h\) (II incorrect).

questions.q:
Consider a n-type semiconductor in which \(n_e\) and \(n_h\) are number of electrons and holes, respectively.
(A) Holes are minority carriers
(B) The dopant is a pentavalent atom
(C) \(n_en_h \ne n_i^2\) (where \(n_i\) is number of electrons or holes in semiconductor when it is intrinsic form)
(D) \(n_en_h \geqslant n_i^2\)
(E) The holes are not generated due to the donors
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.sol: n-type: holes are minority carriers, the dopant is pentavalent, and donors give electrons, not holes. \(n_en_h = n_i^2\) still holds, so (C) and (D) are wrong.

questions.q: A solid sphere with uniform density and radius \(R\) is rotating initially with constant angular velocity (\(\omega_1\)) about its diameter. After some time during the rotation it starts losing mass at a uniform rate, with no change in its shape. The angular velocity of the sphere when its radius become \(R/2\) is \(x\omega_1\). The value of \(x\) is ____ .
questions.sol: \(L = I\omega\) is conserved. With uniform density, \(M \propto R^3\) and \(I \propto MR^2 \propto R^5\). Halving \(R\) divides \(I\) by 32, so \(\omega = 32\omega_1\).

questions.q: A particle of charge 1.6 μC and mass 16 μg is present in a strong magnetic field of 6.28 T. The particle is then fired perpendicular to magnetic field. The time required for the particle to return to original location for the first time is ____ s. (\(\pi\) = 3.14)
questions.sol: \(T = \dfrac{2\pi m}{qB} = \dfrac{6.28\times16\times10^{-9}}{1.6\times10^{-6}\times6.28} = 0.01\) s.
questions.note: The time works out to 0.01 s; the answer key gives 0 (the value rounded to an integer). Both are accepted here.

questions.q: An inductor of self inductance 1 H is connected in series with a resistor of \(100\pi\) ohm and an ac supply of \(100\pi\) volt, 50 Hz. Maximum current flowing in the circuit is ____ A.
questions.sol: \(X_L = 2\pi\times50\times1 = 100\pi\ \Omega\), \(Z = 100\pi\sqrt2\ \Omega\). \(I_{max} = \dfrac{100\pi\sqrt2}{100\pi\sqrt2} = 1\) A.

questions.q: If an optical medium possesses a relative permeability of \(\frac{10}{\pi}\) and relative permittivity of \(\frac{1}{0.0885}\), then the velocity of light is greater in vacuum than that in this medium by ____ times. (\(\mu_0 = 4\pi\times10^{-7}\) H/m, \(\epsilon_0 = 8.85\times10^{-12}\) F/m, \(c = 3\times10^8\) m/s)
questions.sol: \(\dfrac cv = \sqrt{\mu_r\epsilon_r} = \sqrt{\dfrac{10}{\pi}\times\dfrac{1}{0.0885}} \approx 6\).

questions.q: In a Young's double slit experiment, two slits are located 1.5 mm apart. The distance of screen from slits is 2 m and the wavelength of the source is 400 nm. If the 20 maxima of the double slit pattern are contained within the central maximum of the single slit diffraction pattern, then the width of each slit is \(x\times10^{-3}\) cm, where \(x\)-value is ____ .
questions.sol: Central diffraction maximum width \(\dfrac{2\lambda D}{a}\) holds 20 fringes of width \(\dfrac{\lambda D}{d}\): \(a = \dfrac{d}{10} = 0.15\) mm \(= 15\times10^{-3}\) cm.

questions.q: In an electromagnetic system, the quantity representing the ratio of electric flux and magnetic flux has dimension of \(M^PL^QT^RA^S\), where value of '\(Q\)' and '\(R\)' are
questions.sol: \(\dfrac{\phi_E}{\phi_B} = \dfrac{EA}{BA} = \dfrac EB\), a speed: \([LT^{-1}]\), so \(Q = 1\), \(R = -1\).

questions.q: A body of mass \(m\) is suspended by two strings making angles \(\theta_1\) and \(\theta_2\) with the horizontal ceiling with tensions \(T_1\) and \(T_2\) simultaneously. \(T_1\) and \(T_2\) are related by \(T_1 = \sqrt3T_2\), the angles \(\theta_1\) and \(\theta_2\) are
questions.sol: Horizontal: \(\sqrt3T_2\cos\theta_1 = T_2\cos\theta_2\), satisfied by \(\theta_1 = 60^\circ\), \(\theta_2 = 30^\circ\). Vertical: \(\sqrt3T_2\cdot\dfrac{\sqrt3}{2} + \dfrac{T_2}{2} = mg \Rightarrow T_2 = \dfrac{mg}{2}\).

questions.q:
Which of the following are correct expression for torque acting on a body?
A. \(\vec\tau = \vec r\times\vec L\)
B. \(\vec\tau = \frac{d}{dt}(\vec r\times\vec p)\)
C. \(\vec\tau = \vec r\times\frac{d\vec p}{dt}\)
D. \(\vec\tau = I\vec\alpha\)
E. \(\vec\tau = \vec r\times\vec F\)
(\(\vec r\) = position vector; \(\vec p\) = linear momentum; \(\vec L\) = angular momentum; \(\vec\alpha\) = angular acceleration; \(I\) = moment of inertia; \(\vec F\) = force; \(t\) = time)
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
o: A, B, D and E Only
B, C, D and E Only
questions.sol: \(\vec\tau = \dfrac{d\vec L}{dt} = \dfrac{d}{dt}(\vec r\times\vec p) = \vec r\times\dfrac{d\vec p}{dt} = \vec r\times\vec F\), and \(I\vec\alpha\) about a fixed axis. \(\vec r\times\vec L\) is not a torque.

questions.q: If \(\vec L\) and \(\vec P\) represent the angular momentum and linear momentum respectively of a particle of mass '\(m\)' having position vector as \(\vec r = a(\hat i\cos\omega t + \hat j\sin\omega t)\). The direction of force is
o: Opposite to the direction of \(\vec L\)
Opposite to the direction of \(\vec L\times\vec P\)
Opposite to the direction of \(\vec r\)
Opposite to the direction of \(\vec P\)
questions.sol: The particle moves uniformly on a circle, so the force is centripetal: opposite to \(\vec r\).

questions.q: Two liquids A and B have \(\theta_A\) and \(\theta_B\) as contact angles in a capillary tube. If \(K = \cos\theta_A/\cos\theta_B\), then identify the correct statement:
o: K is negative, then liquid A and liquid B have convex meniscus.
K is negative, then liquid A and liquid B have concave meniscus.
K is zero, then liquid A has convex meniscus and liquid B has concave meniscus.
K is negative, then liquid A has concave meniscus and liquid B has convex meniscus.
questions.sol: \(\cos\theta > 0\) gives a concave meniscus and \(\cos\theta < 0\) a convex one. \(K < 0\) means opposite signs, e.g. A concave and B convex.

questions.q: The mean free path and the average speed of oxygen molecules at 300 K and 1 atm are \(3\times10^{-7}\) m and 600 m/s, respectively. Find the frequency of its collisions.
questions.sol: \(f = \dfrac{\bar v}{\lambda} = \dfrac{600}{3\times10^{-7}} = 2\times10^9\) per second.

questions.q: Two simple pendulums having lengths \(l_1\) and \(l_2\) with negligible string mass undergo angular displacements \(\theta_1\) and \(\theta_2\), from their mean positions, respectively. If the angular accelerations of both pendulums are same, then which expression is correct?
questions.sol: Angular acceleration \(= \dfrac gl\theta\). Equal values: \(\dfrac{\theta_1}{l_1} = \dfrac{\theta_2}{l_2} \Rightarrow \theta_1l_2 = \theta_2l_1\).

questions.q: Consider the sound wave travelling in ideal gases of He, CH\(_4\), and CO\(_2\). All the gases have the same ratio \(\frac P\rho\), where \(P\) is the pressure and \(\rho\) is the density. The ratio of the speed of sound through the gases \(V_{He} : V_{CH_4} : V_{CO_2}\) is given by
questions.sol: \(v = \sqrt{\gamma P/\rho}\): with \(\gamma = \dfrac53\) (He), \(\dfrac43\) (CH\(_4\)) and \(\dfrac75\) (linear CO\(_2\)), \(v_{He} : v_{CH_4} : v_{CO_2} = \sqrt{\dfrac53} : \sqrt{\dfrac43} : \sqrt{\dfrac75}\).

questions.q: In an experiment with a closed organ pipe, it is filled with water by \(\left(\frac15\right)\)th of its volume. The frequency of the fundamental note will change by
questions.sol: The air column becomes \(\dfrac45\) as long, so \(f \propto \dfrac1L\) rises by a factor \(\dfrac54\): +25%.

questions.q:
Given below are two statements : one is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R
Assertion A : The kinetic energy needed to project a body of mass \(m\) from earth surface to infinity is \(\frac12mgR\), where \(R\) is the radius of earth.
Reason R : The maximum potential energy of a body is zero when it is projected to infinity from earth surface.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below
o: A is false but R is true
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
questions.sol: Escape needs \(\dfrac{GMm}{R} = mgR\), not \(\dfrac12mgR\): A is false. The potential energy rises to its maximum value, zero, at infinity: R is true.

questions.q: Two infinite identical charged sheets and a charged spherical body of charge density '\(\rho\)' are arranged as shown in figure. Then the correct relation between the electrical fields at A, B, C and D points is:
questions.sol: The two sheets' fields cancel between them and add outside, so A and B differ (the sphere's field falls with distance; A is closer). Outside, at C and D, the sheets' fields point in opposite directions, so \(\vec E_C \ne \vec E_D\).

questions.q: Two small spherical balls of mass 10 g each with charges \(-2\ \mu\)C and \(2\ \mu\)C, are attached to two ends of very light rigid rod of length 20 cm. The arrangement is now placed near an infinite nonconducting charge sheet with uniform charge density of 100 μC/m² such that length of rod makes an angle of 30° with electric field generated by charge sheet. Net torque acting on the rod is: (Take \(\epsilon_0\) : \(8.85\times10^{-12}\) C²/N m²)
questions.sol: \(E = \dfrac{\sigma}{2\epsilon_0} = \dfrac{10^{-4}}{1.77\times10^{-11}} \approx 5.65\times10^6\) N/C. \(\tau = pE\sin30^\circ = (2\times10^{-6}\times0.2)\times5.65\times10^6\times0.5 \approx 1.13\) N m.

questions.q: Current passing through a wire as function of time is given as \(I(t) = 0.02t + 0.01\) A. The charge that will flow through the wire from \(t\) = 1 s to \(t\) = 2 s is
An alternating current is represented by the equation, \(i = 100\sqrt2\sin(100\pi t)\) ampere. The RMS value of current and the frequency of the given alternating current are
questions.sol: \(I_{rms} = \dfrac{100\sqrt2}{\sqrt2} = 100\) A; \(f = \dfrac{100\pi}{2\pi} = 50\) Hz.

questions.q: In a Young's double slit experiment, the slits are separated by 0.2 mm. If the slits separation is increased to 0.4 mm, the percentage change of the fringe width is :
questions.sol: \(\beta \propto \dfrac1d\): doubling \(d\) halves the fringe width, a 50% change.

questions.q: When an object is placed 40 cm away from a spherical mirror an image of magnification \(\frac12\) is produced. To obtain an image with magnification of \(\frac13\), the object is to be moved :
questions.sol: An erect, smaller image means a convex mirror: \(m = \dfrac{f}{f + |u|}\). \(\dfrac12 = \dfrac{f}{f + 40} \Rightarrow f = 40\) cm. \(\dfrac13 = \dfrac{40}{40 + |u|} \Rightarrow |u| = 80\) cm: move 40 cm farther away.

questions.q: Considering the Bohr model of hydrogen like atoms, the ratio of the radius of 5\(^{th}\) orbit of the electron in Li\(^{2+}\) and He\(^+\) is
questions.sol: \(r \propto \dfrac{n^2}{Z}\): same \(n\), so \(\dfrac{r_{Li}}{r_{He}} = \dfrac23\).

questions.q: A small mirror of mass \(m\) is suspended by a massless thread of length \(l\). Then the small angle through which the thread will be deflected when a short pulse of laser of energy \(E\) falls normal on the mirror (\(c\) = speed of light in vacuum and \(g\) = acceleration due to gravity)
questions.sol: On reflection the momentum given is \(\dfrac{2E}{c}\), so \(v = \dfrac{2E}{mc}\). For a pendulum \(v = \theta\sqrt{gl}\) at small angles: \(\theta = \dfrac{2E}{mc\sqrt{gl}}\).

questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R
Assertion A : In photoelectric effect, on increasing the intensity of incident light the stopping potential increases.
Reason R : Increase in intensity of light increases the rate of photoelectrons emitted, provided the frequency of incident light is greater than threshold frequency.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
A is false but R is true
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
questions.sol: The stopping potential depends on frequency, not intensity: A is false. More intensity means more photoelectrons per second: R is true.

questions.q:
The Boolean expression \(Y = A\bar BC + \bar A\bar C\) can be realised with which of the following gate configurations.
A. One 3-input AND gate, 3 NOT gates and one 2-input OR gate, one 2-input AND gate
B. One 3-input AND gate, 1 NOT gate, One 2-input NOR gate and one 2-input OR gate
C. 3-input OR gate, 3 NOT gates and one 2-input AND gate
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.sol: \(A\bar BC\): a 3-input AND with one NOT. \(\bar A\bar C\): either two NOTs and a 2-input AND (config A) or a single NOR (config B). Then OR them. Config C cannot produce Y.

questions.q: A circular ring and a solid sphere having same radius roll down on an inclined plane from rest without slipping. The ratio of their velocities when reached at the bottom of the plane is \(\sqrt{\frac x5}\) where \(x\) = ____ .
questions.sol: Ring: \(v^2 = gh\). Solid sphere: \(v^2 = \dfrac{10}{7}gh\). Ratio \(= \sqrt{\dfrac{7}{10}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{3.5}{5}}\), so \(x = 3.5\).
questions.note: The ratio works out to \(\sqrt{7/10} = \sqrt{3.5/5}\), so \(x = 3.5\); the answer key accepts both 3.5 and 4.

questions.q: Two slabs with square cross section of different materials (1, 2) with equal sides (\(l\)) and thickness \(d_1\) and \(d_2\) such that \(d_2 = 2d_1\) and \(l > d_2\). Considering lower edges of these slabs are fixed to the floor, we apply equal shearing force on the narrow faces. The angle of deformation is \(\theta_2 = 2\theta_1\). If the shear moduli of material 1 is \(4\times10^9\) N/m², then shear moduli of material 2 is \(x\times10^9\) N/m², where value of \(x\) is ____ .
questions.sol: \(\theta = \dfrac{F}{GA}\) with \(A = ld\). \(\dfrac{G_2}{G_1} = \dfrac{d_1\theta_1}{d_2\theta_2} = \dfrac14\), so \(G_2 = 1\times10^9\) N/m².

questions.q: Four capacitors each of capacitance 16 μF are connected as shown in the figure. The capacitance between points A and B is : ____ (in μF).
questions.sol: Tracing the wires, each capacitor has one plate on the A-side wire and the other on the B-side wire: all four are in parallel, \(4\times16 = 64\ \mu\)F.

questions.q: Conductor wire ABCDE with each arm 10 cm in length is placed in magnetic field of \(\frac{1}{\sqrt2}\) Tesla, perpendicular to its plane. When conductor is pulled towards right with constant velocity of 10 cm/s, induced emf between points A and E is ____ mV.
questions.sol: Only the length perpendicular to the motion counts: A to E spans \(2\times10\sin45^\circ = 10\sqrt2\) cm vertically. \(\varepsilon = Bvl = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt2}\times0.1\times0.1\sqrt2 = 0.01\) V = 10 mV.

questions.q: Distance between object and its image (magnified by \(-\frac13\)) is 30 cm. The focal length of the mirror used is \(\left(\frac x4\right)\) cm, where magnitude of value of \(x\) is ____ .
questions.sol: Real, inverted image: \(v = \dfrac u3\) and \(|u| - |v| = 30\), so \(u = -45\) cm, \(v = -15\) cm. \(\dfrac1f = -\dfrac1{15} - \dfrac1{45} \Rightarrow f = -\dfrac{45}{4}\) cm, \(x = 45\).

questions.q:
Match the LIST-I with LIST-II
LIST-ILIST-II
A.Boltzmann constantI.\(ML^2T^{-1}\)
B.Coefficient of viscosityII.\(MLT^{-3}K^{-1}\)
C.Planck's constantIII.\(ML^2T^{-2}K^{-1}\)
D.Thermal conductivityIV.\(ML^{-1}T^{-1}\)
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
o: A - III, B - IV, C - I, D - II
A - III, B - IV, C - II, D - I
A - III, B - II, C - I, D - IV
A - II, B - III, C - IV, D - I
questions.sol: Boltzmann constant (J/K) \(ML^2T^{-2}K^{-1}\) (III); viscosity \(ML^{-1}T^{-1}\) (IV); Planck's constant (J s) \(ML^2T^{-1}\) (I); thermal conductivity \(MLT^{-3}K^{-1}\) (II).

questions.q: A particle moves along the \(x\)-axis and has its displacement \(x\) varying with time \(t\) according to the equation: \(x = c_0(t^2 - 2) + c(t - 2)^2\) where \(c_0\) and \(c\) are constants of appropriate dimensions. Then, which of the following statements is correct?
o: the acceleration of the particle is \(2(c + c_0)\)
the acceleration of the particle is \(2c_0\)
the acceleration of the particle is \(2c\)
the initial velocity of the particle is \(4c\)
questions.sol: \(x = (c_0 + c)t^2 - 4ct + (4c - 2c_0)\), so \(a = 2(c + c_0)\). The initial velocity is \(-4c\), not \(4c\).

questions.q: A particle is projected with velocity \(u\) so that its horizontal range is three times the maximum height attained by it. The horizontal range of the projectile is given as \(\frac{nu^2}{25g}\), where value of \(n\) is: (Given, '\(g\)' is the acceleration due to gravity.)
questions.sol: \(R = 3H \Rightarrow 4\cot\theta = 3 \Rightarrow \tan\theta = \dfrac43\). \(R = \dfrac{u^2\cdot2\sin\theta\cos\theta}{g} = \dfrac{u^2\cdot2\cdot\frac45\cdot\frac35}{g} = \dfrac{24u^2}{25g}\).

questions.q: A block of mass 1 kg, moving along \(x\) with speed \(v_i\) = 10 m/s enters a rough region ranging from \(x\) = 0.1 m to \(x\) = 1.9 m. The retarding force acting on the block in this range is \(F_r = -kx\) N, with \(k\) = 10 N/m. Then the final speed of the block as it crosses rough region is.

Consider two blocks A and B of masses \(m_1\) = 10 kg and \(m_2\) = 5 kg that are placed on a frictionless table. The block A moves with a constant speed \(v\) = 3 m/s towards the block B kept at rest. A spring with spring constant \(k\) = 3000 N/m is attached with the block B as shown in the figure. After the collision, suppose that the blocks A and B, along with the spring in constant compression state, move together, then the compression in the spring is, (Neglect the mass of the spring)
questions.sol: Common velocity \(= \dfrac{30}{15} = 2\) m/s. KE lost \(= 45 - 30 = 15\) J \(= \tfrac12kx^2 \Rightarrow x^2 = 0.01\), \(x = 0.1\) m.

questions.q: Two cylindrical vessels of equal cross sectional area of 2 m² contain water upto heights 10 m and 6 m, respectively. If the vessels are connected at their bottom then the work done by the force of gravity is (Density of water is \(10^3\) kg/m³ and \(g\) = 10 m/s²)
questions.sol: Levels settle at 8 m. Water moved: \(2\times2 = 4\) m³ = 4000 kg, whose centre drops from 9 m to 7 m. \(W = 4000\times10\times2 = 8\times10^4\) J.

questions.q: A solid steel ball of diameter 3.6 mm acquired terminal velocity \(2.45\times10^{-2}\) m/s while falling under gravity through an oil of density 925 kg m\(^{-3}\). Take density of steel as 7825 kg m\(^{-3}\) and \(g\) as 9.8 m/s². The viscosity of the oil in SI unit is
questions.sol: \(\eta = \dfrac{2r^2(\rho - \sigma)g}{9v} = \dfrac{2(1.8\times10^{-3})^2\times6900\times9.8}{9\times2.45\times10^{-2}} \approx 1.99\) Pa s.

questions.q: An ideal gas exists in a state with pressure \(P_0\), volume \(V_0\). It is isothermally expanded to 4 times of its initial volume (\(V_0\)), then isobarically compressed to its original volume. Finally the system is heated isochorically to bring it to its initial state. The amount of heat exchanged in this process is
questions.sol: Isothermal: \(W = P_0V_0\ln4 = 2\ln2\,P_0V_0\). Isobaric at \(\frac{P_0}{4}\) from \(4V_0\) to \(V_0\): \(W = -\frac34P_0V_0\). Isochoric: \(W = 0\). For a cycle \(Q = W = P_0V_0(2\ln2 - 0.75)\).

questions.q: Pressure of an ideal gas, contained in a closed vessel, is increased by 0.4% when heated by 1°C. Its initial temperature must be:
questions.sol: At constant volume \(\dfrac{\Delta P}{P} = \dfrac{\Delta T}{T} \Rightarrow T = \dfrac{1}{0.004} = 250\) K.

questions.q: In the resonance experiment, two air columns (closed at one end) of 100 cm and 120 cm long, give 15 beats per second when each one is sounding in the respective fundamental modes. The velocity of sound in the air column is:
questions.sol: \(\dfrac v4\left(\dfrac{1}{1.0} - \dfrac{1}{1.2}\right) = 15 \Rightarrow \dfrac{v}{24} = 15 \Rightarrow v = 360\) m/s.

questions.q: A motor operating on 100 V draws a current of 1 A. If the efficiency of the motor is 91.6%, then the loss of power in units of cal/s is

Using a battery, a 100 pF capacitor is charged to 60 V and then the battery is removed. After that, a second uncharged capacitor is connected to the first capacitor in parallel. If the final voltage across the second capacitor is 20 V, its capacitance is: (in pF)
questions.sol: Charge \(= 100\times60 = 6000\) pC is shared: \(C_{total} = \dfrac{6000}{20} = 300\) pF, so the second capacitor is 200 pF.

questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R
Assertion A : If Oxygen ion (O\(^{-2}\)) and Hydrogen ion (H\(^+\)) enter normal to the magnetic field with equal momentum, then the path of O\(^{-2}\) ion has a smaller curvature than that of H\(^+\).
Reason R : A proton with same linear momentum as an electron will form a path of smaller radius of curvature on entering a uniform magnetic field perpendicularly.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below
o: Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is false but R is true
A is true but R is false
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
questions.sol: \(r = \dfrac{p}{qB}\): with equal momentum the O\(^{2-}\) ion (charge \(2e\)) has half the radius of H\(^+\), as the key reads A. A proton and an electron with the same momentum have the same charge magnitude, so the same radius: R is false.
questions.note: The key takes 'smaller curvature' in Assertion A to mean a smaller radius of curvature: the O²⁻ ion (twice the charge, same momentum) moves on a circle of half the radius.

questions.q: A magnetic dipole experiences a torque of \(80\sqrt3\) N m when placed in uniform magnetic field in such a way that dipole moment makes angle of 60° with magnetic field. The potential energy of the dipole is :
questions.sol: \(mB\sin60^\circ = 80\sqrt3 \Rightarrow mB = 160\). \(U = -mB\cos60^\circ = -80\) J.

questions.q: An electric bulb rated as 100 W − 220 V is connected to an ac source of rms voltage 220 V. The peak value of current through the bulb is :
Two monochromatic light beams have intensities in the ratio 1 : 9. An interference pattern is obtained by these beams. The ratio of the intensities of maximum to minimum is
questions.sol: Amplitudes 1 : 3. \(\dfrac{I_{max}}{I_{min}} = \dfrac{(1 + 3)^2}{(3 - 1)^2} = 4\).

questions.q: Width of one of the two slits in a Young's double slit interference experiment is half of the other slit. The ratio of the maximum to the minimum intensity in the interference pattern is :
questions.sol: Intensity \(\propto\) slit width, so amplitudes are \(1 : \sqrt2\). \(\dfrac{(\sqrt2 + 1)^2}{(\sqrt2 - 1)^2} = \dfrac{3 + 2\sqrt2}{3 - 2\sqrt2}\).

questions.q: A monochromatic light of frequency \(5\times10^{14}\) Hz travelling through air, is incident on a medium of refractive index '2'. Wavelength of the refracted light will be :
questions.sol: In air \(\lambda = \dfrac{3\times10^8}{5\times10^{14}} = 600\) nm; in the medium \(\dfrac{600}{2} = 300\) nm.

questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R
Assertion A : The Bohr model is applicable to hydrogen and hydrogen-like atoms only.
Reason R : The formulation of Bohr model does not include repulsive force between electrons.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below
o: A is true but R is false
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
A is false but R is true
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
questions.sol: Bohr's model treats a single electron with no electron–electron repulsion, which is why it works only for hydrogen-like atoms: A and R are true and R explains A.

questions.q: The truth table corresponding to the circuit given below is:
questions.sol: \(C = A\cdot(A + B) = A\): table (A).

questions.q: A physical quantity \(C\) is related to four other quantities \(p, q, r\) and \(s\) as follows \(C = \frac{pq^2}{r^3\sqrt s}\). The percentage errors in the measurement of \(p, q, r\) and \(s\) are 1%, 2%, 3% and 2%, respectively. The percentage error in the measurement of \(C\) will be ____ %
questions.sol: \(\dfrac{\Delta C}{C} = 1 + 2\times2 + 3\times3 + \tfrac12\times2 = 15\%\).

questions.q: The excess pressure inside a soap bubble A in air is half the excess pressure inside another soap bubble B in air. If the volume of the bubble A is \(n\) times the volume of the bubble B, then, the value of \(n\) is ____ .
questions.sol: \(\Delta P \propto \dfrac1r\): \(r_A = 2r_B\), so \(V_A = 8V_B\).

questions.q: Two cells of emfs 1 V and 2 V and internal resistances 2 Ω and 1 Ω, respectively, are connected in series with an external resistance of 6 Ω. The total current in the circuit is \(I_1\). Now the same two cells in parallel configuration are connected to same external resistance. In this case, the total current drawn is \(I_2\). The value of \(\frac{I_1}{I_2}\) is \(\frac x3\). The value of \(x\) is ____ .
questions.sol: Series: \(I_1 = \dfrac{3}{2 + 1 + 6} = \dfrac13\) A. Parallel: \(E = \dfrac{1/2 + 2/1}{1/2 + 1} = \dfrac53\) V, \(r = \dfrac23\ \Omega\), \(I_2 = \dfrac{5/3}{20/3} = \dfrac14\) A. \(\dfrac{I_1}{I_2} = \dfrac43\), so \(x = 4\).

questions.q: Light from a point source in air falls on a spherical glass surface (refractive index, \(\mu\) = 1.5 and radius of curvature = 50 cm). The image is formed at a distance of 200 cm from the glass surface inside the glass. The magnitude of distance of the light source from the glass surface is ____ m.
questions.sol: \(\dfrac{1.5}{200} - \dfrac1u = \dfrac{0.5}{50} \Rightarrow \dfrac1u = 0.0075 - 0.01 \Rightarrow u = -400\) cm. The source is 4 m away.

questions.q: An electron in the hydrogen atom initially in the fourth excited state makes a transition to \(n^{th}\) energy state by emitting a photon of energy 2.86 eV. The integer value of \(n\) will be ____ .

A person measures mass of 3 different particles as 435.42 g, 226.3 g and 0.125 g. According to the rules for arithmetic operations with significant figures, the addition of the masses of 3 particles will be.
questions.sol: Sum \(= 661.845\) g. The least precise term (226.3 g) has one decimal place, so the result is 661.8 g.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

Which of the following curves possibly represent one-dimensional motion of a particle?
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.sol: Phase grows linearly with time (A); \(v\)–\(x\) of SHM is a closed curve (B); total distance never decreases (D). A velocity–time circle (C) gives two velocities at one instant, which is impossible.

questions.q: The angle of projection of a particle is measured from the vertical axis as \(\phi\) and the maximum height reached by the particle is \(h_m\). Here \(h_m\) as function of \(\phi\) can be presented as
questions.sol: With \(\phi\) from the vertical, \(h_m = \dfrac{u^2\cos^2\phi}{2g}\): largest at \(\phi = 0\) and falling to zero at \(90^\circ\).

questions.q: A particle is released from height \(S\) above the surface of the earth. At certain height its kinetic energy is three times its potential energy. The height from the surface of the earth and the speed of the particle at that instant are respectively.
questions.sol: \(K = 3U\) and \(K + U = mgS\), so \(mgh = \dfrac{mgS}{4}\), \(h = \dfrac S4\). \(v^2 = 2g\left(S - \dfrac S4\right) = \dfrac{3gS}{2}\).

questions.q: A force of 49 N acts tangentially at the highest point of a sphere (solid) of mass 20 kg, kept on a rough horizontal plane. If the sphere rolls without slipping, then the acceleration of the center of the sphere is
questions.sol: \(F + f = ma\) and \((F - f)R = \dfrac25mR^2\dfrac aR\). Adding: \(2F = 1.4ma\), \(a = \dfrac{98}{28} = 3.5\) m/s².

questions.q: Consider a completely full cylindrical water tank of height 1.6 m and of cross-sectional area 0.5 m². It has a small hole in its side at a height 90 cm from the bottom. Assume, the cross-sectional area of the hole to be negligibly small as compared to that of the water tank. If a load 50 kg is applied at the top surface of the water in the tank then the velocity of the water coming out at the instant when the hole is opened is: (g = 10 m/s²)
questions.sol: The load adds \(\dfrac{500}{0.5} = 1000\) Pa, equal to 0.1 m of water. Effective head \(= 0.7 + 0.1 = 0.8\) m. \(v = \sqrt{2\times10\times0.8} = 4\) m/s.

questions.q: A gas is kept in a container having walls which are thermally non-conducting. Initially the gas has a volume of 800 cm³ and temperature 27°C. The change in temperature when the gas is adiabatically compressed to 200 cm³ is: (Take \(\gamma = 1.5\); \(\gamma\) is the ratio of specific heats at constant pressure and at constant volume)
questions.sol: \(TV^{\gamma - 1}\) is constant: \(T_2 = 300\times\left(\dfrac{800}{200}\right)^{0.5} = 600\) K. The change is 300 K.

questions.q: During the melting of a slab of ice at 273 K at atmospheric pressure :
o: Internal energy of ice-water system remains unchanged.
Positive work is done by the ice-water system on the atmosphere.
Positive work is done on the ice-water system by the atmosphere.
Internal energy of the ice-water system decreases.
questions.sol: Ice contracts on melting, so the atmosphere does positive work on the system; the internal energy increases because heat is absorbed.

questions.q: A piston of mass \(M\) is hung from a massless spring whose restoring force law goes as \(F = -kx^3\), where \(k\) is the spring constant of appropriate dimension. The piston separates the vertical chamber into two parts, where the bottom part is filled with '\(n\)' moles of an ideal gas. An external work is done on the gas isothermally (at a constant temperature \(T\)) with the help of a heating filament (with negligible volume) mounted in lower part of the chamber, so that the piston goes up from a height \(L_0\) to \(L_1\), the total energy delivered by the filament is: (Assume spring to be in its natural length before heating)
questions.sol: Energy supplied = isothermal work on the gas \(nRT\ln\dfrac{L_1}{L_0}\) + rise in the piston's potential energy \(Mg(L_1 - L_0)\) + energy stored in the spring, \(\int kx^3dx = \dfrac k4x^4\). This matches (B).

questions.q:
Two blocks of masses \(m\) and \(M\), (\(M > m\)), are placed on a frictionless table as shown in figure. A massless spring with spring constant \(k\) is attached with the lower block. If the system is slightly displaced and released, then (\(\mu\) = coefficient of friction between the two blocks)
A. The time period of small oscillation of the two blocks is \(T = 2\pi\sqrt{\frac{(m + M)}{k}}\)
B. The acceleration of the blocks is \(a = -\frac{kx}{M + m}\) (\(x\) = displacement of the blocks from the mean position)
C. The magnitude of the frictional force on the upper block is \(\frac{m\mu|x|}{M + m}\)
D. The maximum amplitude of the upper block, if it does not slip, is \(\frac{\mu(M + m)g}{k}\)
E. Maximum frictional force can be \(\mu(M + m)g\).
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.sol: Together they oscillate with \(\omega^2 = \dfrac{k}{M + m}\): A and B are true. Friction on the upper block \(= m|a| = \dfrac{mk|x|}{M + m}\), not with \(\mu\) (C false). No slipping needs \(\dfrac{mkA}{M + m} \le \mu mg\), so \(A_{max} = \dfrac{\mu(M + m)g}{k}\) (D true). The maximum friction is \(\mu mg\) (E false).

questions.q: The electrostatic potential on the surface of uniformly charged spherical shell of radius \(R\) = 10 cm is 120 V. The potential at the centre of shell, at a distance \(r\) = 5 cm from centre, and at a distance \(r\) = 15 cm from the centre of the shell respectively, are:
questions.sol: Inside the shell the potential equals the surface value, 120 V (at the centre and at 5 cm). Outside: \(120\times\dfrac{10}{15} = 80\) V.

questions.q: A wire of length 25 m and cross-sectional area 5 mm² having resistivity of \(2\times10^{-6}\ \Omega\) m is bent into a complete circle. The resistance between diametrically opposite points will be
questions.sol: \(R = \dfrac{\rho L}{A} = \dfrac{2\times10^{-6}\times25}{5\times10^{-6}} = 10\ \Omega\). Two halves of 5 Ω in parallel: 2.5 Ω.

questions.q: A parallel plate capacitor is filled equally (half) with two dielectrics of dielectric constants \(\epsilon_1\) and \(\epsilon_2\), as shown in figures (first configuration on the left, second on the right). The distance between the plates is \(d\) and area of each plate is \(A\). If capacitance in first configuration and second configuration are \(C_1\) and \(C_2\) respectively, then \(\frac{C_1}{C_2}\) is:
questions.sol: First (layers in series): \(C_1 = \dfrac{2\epsilon_0A}{d}\dfrac{\epsilon_1\epsilon_2}{\epsilon_1 + \epsilon_2}\). Second (side by side): \(C_2 = \dfrac{\epsilon_0A}{2d}(\epsilon_1 + \epsilon_2)\). \(\dfrac{C_1}{C_2} = \dfrac{4\epsilon_1\epsilon_2}{(\epsilon_1 + \epsilon_2)^2}\).

questions.q:
Consider following statements for refraction of light through prism, when angle of deviation is minimum.
A. The refracted ray inside prism becomes parallel to the base.
B. Larger angle prisms provide smaller angle of minimum deviation.
C. Angle of incidence and angle of emergence becomes equal.
D. There are always two sets of angle of incidence for which deviation will be same except at minimum deviation setting.
E. Angle of refraction becomes double of prism angle.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.sol: At minimum deviation the ray inside is parallel to the base (A) and \(i = e\) (C). Every other deviation occurs for two angles of incidence (D). Larger prism angles give larger deviation, and \(A = 2r\), not \(r = 2A\).

questions.q: The radii of curvature for a thin convex lens are 10 cm and 15 cm respectively. The focal length of the lens is 12 cm. The refractive index of the lens material is
questions.sol: \(\dfrac1{12} = (\mu - 1)\left(\dfrac1{10} + \dfrac1{15}\right) = \dfrac{\mu - 1}{6} \Rightarrow \mu = 1.5\).

questions.q:
Match the LIST-I with LIST-II

A.\({}^1_0n + {}^{235}_{92}\text{U} \to {}^{140}_{54}\text{Xe} + {}^{94}_{38}\text{Sr} + 2\,{}^1_0n\)I.Chemical reaction
B.\(2\text{H}_2 + \text{O}_2 \to 2\text{H}_2\text{O}\)II.Fusion with +ve Q value
C.\({}^2_1\text{H} + {}^2_1\text{H} \to {}^3_2\text{He} + {}^1_0n\)III.Fission
D.\({}^1_1\text{H} + {}^3_1\text{H} \to {}^2_1\text{H} + {}^2_1\text{H}\)IV.Fusion with -ve Q value
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.sol: A is fission (III), B is a chemical reaction (I), C is fusion releasing energy (II), and D, H-1 + H-3 → two H-2, needs energy: fusion with negative Q (IV).

questions.q: The work function of a metal is 3 eV. The color of the visible light that is required to cause emission of photoelectrons is
questions.sol: \(\lambda_{max} = \dfrac{1240}{3} \approx 413\) nm, so light of shorter wavelength than this is needed: blue.

questions.q: The radiation pressure exerted by a 450 W light source on a perfectly reflecting surface placed at 2 m away from it, is
questions.sol: \(I = \dfrac{450}{4\pi\times2^2} \approx 8.95\) W/m². For a perfect reflector \(P = \dfrac{2I}{c} \approx 6\times10^{-8}\) Pa.

ABY

111
questions.sol: The table gives \(Y = A\). Circuit (A): \(Y = A\cdot(A + B) = A\).

questions.q: Three identical spheres of mass \(m\), are placed at the vertices of an equilateral triangle of length \(a\). When released, they interact only through gravitational force and collide after a time \(T\) = 4 seconds. If the sides of the triangle are increased to length \(2a\) and also the masses of the spheres are made \(2m\), then they will collide after ____ seconds.
questions.sol: Collision time \(\propto\sqrt{\dfrac{a^3}{Gm}}\). Doubling \(a\) multiplies it by \(\sqrt8\); doubling \(m\) divides it by \(\sqrt2\). Net factor 2: 8 s.

questions.q: In the figure shown below, a resistance of 150.4 Ω is connected in series to an ammeter A of resistance 240 Ω. A shunt resistance of 10 Ω is connected in parallel with the ammeter. The reading of the ammeter is ____ mA.
questions.sol: Ammeter with shunt: \(\dfrac{240\times10}{250} = 9.6\ \Omega\). Total \(= 160\ \Omega\), current \(= \dfrac{20}{160} = 125\) mA. Through the ammeter: \(125\times\dfrac{10}{250} = 5\) mA.

questions.q: A loop ABCDA, carrying current \(I\) = 12 A, is placed in a plane, consists of two semi-circular segments of radius \(R_1 = 6\pi\) m and \(R_2 = 4\pi\) m. The magnitude of the resultant magnetic field at center O is \(k\times10^{-7}\) T. The value of \(k\) is ____ . (Given \(\mu_0 = 4\pi\times10^{-7}\) T m A\(^{-1}\))
questions.sol: Each semicircle gives \(\dfrac{\mu_0I}{4R}\): \(\dfrac{4\pi\times10^{-7}\times12}{4\times6\pi} = 2\times10^{-7}\) T and \(\dfrac{4\pi\times10^{-7}\times12}{4\times4\pi} = 3\times10^{-7}\) T, in opposite directions. Net \(= 1\times10^{-7}\) T.

questions.q: A 4.0 cm long straight wire carrying a current of 8 A is placed perpendicular to a uniform magnetic field of strength 0.15 T. The magnetic force on the wire is ____ mN.

Two coherent monochromatic light beams of intensities \(4I\) and \(9I\) are superimposed. The difference between the maximum and minimum intensities in the resulting interference pattern is \(xI\). The value of \(x\) is ____ .
If \(\mu_0\) and \(\epsilon_0\) are the permeability and permittivity of free space, respectively, then the dimension of \(\left(\frac{1}{\mu_0\epsilon_0}\right)\) is :
questions.sol: \(\dfrac{1}{\mu_0\epsilon_0} = c^2\), so the dimension is \(L^2/T^2\).

questions.q: Given a charge \(q\), current \(I\) and permeability of vacuum \(\mu_0\). Which of the following quantity has the dimension of momentum ?
A sportsman runs around a circular track of radius \(r\) such that he traverses the path \(ABAB\). The distance travelled and displacement, respectively, are
questions.sol: \(ABAB\) is three half-circles: distance \(3\pi r\). It ends at B, a diameter away from A: displacement \(2r\).

questions.q: A body of mass 1 kg is suspended with the help of two strings making angles as shown in figure. Magnitudes of tensions \(T_1\) and \(T_2\), respectively, are (in N) : (Take acceleration due to gravity 10 m/s²)
questions.sol: Horizontal: \(T_1\cos60^\circ = T_2\cos30^\circ \Rightarrow T_1 = \sqrt3T_2\). Vertical: \(T_1\sin60^\circ + T_2\sin30^\circ = 10 \Rightarrow 2T_2 = 10\). So \(T_2 = 5\) N and \(T_1 = 5\sqrt3\) N.

questions.q: The moment of inertia of a circular ring of mass \(M\) and diameter \(r\) about a tangential axis lying in the plane of the ring is :
questions.sol: Radius \(= \dfrac r2\). About a diameter \(\dfrac{MR^2}{2}\); tangent in the plane \(= \dfrac32MR^2 = \dfrac38Mr^2\).

questions.q: Two water drops each of radius '\(r\)' coalesce to form a bigger drop. If '\(T\)' is the surface tension, the surface energy released in this process is :
questions.sol: Volume conserved: \(R = 2^{1/3}r\). Energy released \(= T(2\cdot4\pi r^2 - 4\pi R^2) = 4\pi r^2T(2 - 2^{2/3})\).

Match List - I with List - II.

(C)Latent heat(III)J kg\(^{-1}\) K\(^{-1}\)
(D)Thermal conductivity(IV)J m\(^{-1}\) K\(^{-1}\) s\(^{-1}\)

questions.sol: Heat capacity J K\(^{-1}\) (II); specific heat J kg\(^{-1}\) K\(^{-1}\) (III); latent heat J kg\(^{-1}\) (I); thermal conductivity J m\(^{-1}\) K\(^{-1}\) s\(^{-1}\) (IV).

questions.q:
Identify the characteristics of an adiabatic process in a monoatomic gas.
(A) Internal energy is constant.
(B) Work done in the process is equal to the change in internal energy.
(C) The product of temperature and volume is a constant.
(D) The product of pressure and volume is a constant.
(E) The work done to change the temperature from \(T_1\) to \(T_2\) is proportional to \((T_2 - T_1)\).
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.sol: With \(Q = 0\): \(|W| = |\Delta U| = nC_v|T_2 - T_1|\), so (B) and (E) hold. In an adiabatic process \(TV^{\gamma - 1}\) and \(PV^\gamma\) are constant, not \(TV\) or \(PV\), and \(U\) changes.

questions.q: A sinusoidal wave of wavelength 7.5 cm travels a distance of 1.2 cm along the \(x\)-direction in 0.3 sec. The crest P is at \(x = 0\) at \(t = 0\) sec and maximum displacement of the wave is 2 cm. Which equation correctly represents this wave?

Given below are two statements : one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).
Assertion (A) : Net dipole moment of a polar linear isotropic dielectric substance is not zero even in the absence of an external electric field.
Reason (R) : In absence of an external electric field, the different permanent dipoles of a polar dielectric substance are oriented in random directions.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
o: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
questions.sol: Without an external field the permanent dipoles point randomly, so the net dipole moment is zero: (A) is wrong, (R) is right.

questions.q: Two large plane parallel conducting plates are kept 10 cm apart as shown in figure. The potential difference between them is \(V\). The potential difference between the points A and B (shown in the figure) is :
questions.sol: \(AC = 3\) cm and \(AB = 5\) cm, so \(CB = 4\) cm along the field. \(E = \dfrac{V}{0.1}\); \(V_A - V_B = E\times0.04 = \dfrac25V\).

questions.q: Consider a circular loop that is uniformly charged and has a radius \(a\sqrt2\). Find the position along the positive \(z\)-axis of the cartesian coordinate system where the electric field is maximum if the ring was assumed to be placed in \(xy\) plane at the origin :
questions.sol: On the axis of a ring, \(E\) is maximum at \(z = \dfrac{R}{\sqrt2} = \dfrac{a\sqrt2}{\sqrt2} = a\).

questions.q:
In a moving coil galvanometer, two moving coils \(M_1\) and \(M_2\) have the following particulars :
\(R_1 = 5\ \Omega,\ N_1 = 15,\ A_1 = 3.6\times10^{-3}\) m², \(B_1 = 0.25\) T
\(R_2 = 7\ \Omega,\ N_2 = 21,\ A_2 = 1.8\times10^{-3}\) m², \(B_2 = 0.50\) T
Assuming that torsional constant of the springs are same for both coils, what will be the ratio of voltage sensitivity of \(M_1\) and \(M_2\) ?
questions.sol: Voltage sensitivity \(= \dfrac{NAB}{kR}\). \(M_1\): \(\dfrac{15\times3.6\times10^{-3}\times0.25}{5} = 2.7\times10^{-3}\); \(M_2\): \(\dfrac{21\times1.8\times10^{-3}\times0.5}{7} = 2.7\times10^{-3}\). Ratio 1 : 1.

questions.q: A solenoid having area \(A\) and length '\(l\)' is filled with a material having relative permeability 2. The magnetic energy stored in the solenoid is :
questions.sol: Energy density \(= \dfrac{B^2}{2\mu}\) with \(\mu = 2\mu_0\): \(U = \dfrac{B^2}{4\mu_0}Al\).

questions.q: Two identical objects are placed in front of convex mirror and concave mirror having same radii of curvature of 12 cm, at same distance of 18 cm from the respective mirrors. The ratio of sizes of the images formed by convex mirror and by concave mirror is :

A bi-convex lens has radius of curvature of both the surfaces same as 1/6 cm. If this lens is required to be replaced by another convex lens having different radii of curvatures on both sides (\(R_1 \ne R_2\)), without any change in lens power then possible combination of \(R_1\) and \(R_2\) is :
questions.sol: Same power needs \(\dfrac1{R_1} + \dfrac1{R_2} = 6 + 6 = 12\) cm\(^{-1}\). \(\dfrac15\) and \(\dfrac17\) cm give \(5 + 7 = 12\).

questions.q: Energy released when two deuterons (\({}_1\text{H}^2\)) fuse to form a helium nucleus (\({}_2\text{He}^4\)) is : (Given : Binding energy per nucleon of \({}_1\text{H}^2\) = 1.1 MeV and binding energy per nucleon of \({}_2\text{He}^4\) = 7.0 MeV)

Assuming the validity of Bohr's atomic model for hydrogen like ions the radius of Li\(^{++}\) ion in its ground state is given by \(\frac1Xa_0\), where \(X\) = ____ (Where \(a_0\) is the first Bohr's radius.)

An electron with mass '\(m\)' with an initial velocity (\(t = 0\)), \(\vec v = v_0\hat i\) (\(v_0 > 0\)) enters a magnetic field \(\vec B = B_0\hat j\). If the initial de-Broglie wavelength at \(t = 0\) is \(\lambda_0\) then its value after time '\(t\)' would be :
questions.sol: The magnetic force is perpendicular to the velocity, so the speed (and momentum magnitude) stays the same: \(\lambda = \lambda_0\).

questions.q: In the digital circuit shown in the figure, for the given inputs the \(P\) and \(Q\) values are :
questions.sol: With both inputs 1: the NAND gives \(X = 0\); the OR of the two inverted inputs gives \(Y = 0\). \(P = X\cdot Y = 0\); \(Q = \overline{\bar X + Y} = \overline{1 + 0} = 0\).

questions.q: A wheel of radius 0.2 m rotates freely about its center when a string that is wrapped over its rim is pulled by force of 10 N as shown in figure. The established torque produces an angular acceleration of 2 rad/s². Moment of intertia of the wheel is ____ kg m². (Acceleration due to gravity = 10 m/s²)
questions.sol: \(\tau = 10\times0.2 = 2\) N m \(= I\alpha \Rightarrow I = 1\) kg m².

questions.q: The length of a light string is 1.4 m when the tension on it is 5 N. If the tension increases to 7 N, the length of the string is 1.56 m. The original length of the string is ____ m.
questions.sol: \(L = L_0 + \dfrac Tk\): \(1.56 - 1.4 = \dfrac2k \Rightarrow \dfrac1k = 0.08\). \(L_0 = 1.4 - 5\times0.08 = 1.0\) m.

questions.q: The internal energy of air in 4 m × 4 m × 3 m sized room at 1 atmospheric pressure will be ____ \(\times10^6\) J (Consider air as diatomic molecule)
questions.sol: \(U = \dfrac52PV = 2.5\times10^5\times48 \approx 12\times10^6\) J.

questions.q: A satellite of mass 1000 kg is launched to revolve around the earth in an orbit at a height of 270 km from the earth's surface. Kinetic energy of the satellite in this orbit is ____ \(\times10^{10}\) J. (Mass of earth = \(6\times10^{24}\) kg, Radius of earth = \(6.4\times10^6\) m, Gravitational constant = \(6.67\times10^{-11}\) N m² kg\(^{-2}\))
questions.sol: \(r = 6.4\times10^6 + 0.27\times10^6 = 6.67\times10^6\) m. \(K = \dfrac{GMm}{2r} = \dfrac{6.67\times10^{-11}\times6\times10^{24}\times1000}{2\times6.67\times10^6} = 3\times10^{10}\) J.

questions.q: A ray of light suffers minimum deviation when incident on a prism having angle of the prism equal to 60°. The refractive index of the prism material is \(\sqrt2\). The angle of incidence (in degrees) is ____
questions.sol: \(\sqrt2 = \dfrac{\sin\frac{A + \delta}{2}}{\sin30^\circ} \Rightarrow \sin\dfrac{A + \delta}{2} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt2}\). At minimum deviation \(i = \dfrac{A + \delta}{2} = 45^\circ\).

questions.q: The equation for real gas is given by \(\left(P + \frac{a}{V^2}\right)(V - b) = RT\), where \(P, V, T\) and \(R\) are the pressure, volume, temperature and gas constant, respectively. The dimension of \(ab^{-2}\) is equivalent to that of :
questions.sol: \(\dfrac{a}{V^2}\) is a pressure, so \(a = PV^2\); \(b\) is a volume. \(ab^{-2} = P\), which has the dimensions of energy density.

questions.q: A river is flowing from west to east direction with speed of 9 km h\(^{-1}\). If a boat capable of moving at a maximum speed of 27 km h\(^{-1}\) in still water, crosses the river in half a minute, while moving with maximum speed at an angle of 150° to direction of river flow, then the width of the river is :
questions.sol: Velocity across the river \(= 27\sin150^\circ = 13.5\) km/h \(= 3.75\) m/s. Width \(= 3.75\times30 = 112.5\) m.

questions.q: Moment of inertia of a rod of mass '\(M\)' and length '\(L\)' about an axis passing through its center and normal to its length is '\(\alpha\)'. Now the rod is cut into two equal parts and these parts are joined symmetrically to form a cross shape. Moment of inertia of cross about an axis passing through its center and normal to plane containing cross is :
questions.sol: \(\alpha = \dfrac{ML^2}{12}\). Each half (mass \(\frac M2\), length \(\frac L2\)) about its centre: \(\dfrac{(M/2)(L/2)^2}{12} = \dfrac{ML^2}{96}\). Two halves: \(\dfrac{ML^2}{48} = \dfrac\alpha4\).

questions.q: A square Lamina \(OABC\) of length 10 cm is pivoted at '\(O\)'. Forces act at Lamina as shown in figure. If Lamina remains stationary, then the magnitude of \(F\) is :
questions.sol: Torques about O (side 0.1 m): at B the up and right forces cancel; at A the 10 N down force gives \(10\times0.1\) clockwise; at C, \(F\) to the left gives \(F\times0.1\) anticlockwise. Balance: \(F = 10\) N.

questions.q: A cord of negligible mass is wound around the rim of a wheel supported by spokes with negligible mass. The mass of wheel is 10 kg and radius is 10 cm and it can freely rotate without any friction. Initially the wheel is at rest. If a steady pull of 20 N is applied on the cord, the angular velocity of the wheel, after the cord is unwound by 1 m, would be:
questions.sol: Work done \(= 20\times1 = 20\) J \(= \tfrac12I\omega^2\) with \(I = MR^2 = 0.1\) kg m² (all mass on the rim). \(\omega^2 = 400\), \(\omega = 20\) rad/s.

questions.q: In an adiabatic process, which of the following statements is true?
o: The internal energy of the gas decreases as the temperature increases
The molar heat capacity is zero
Work done by the gas equals the increase in internal energy
The molar heat capacity is infinite
questions.sol: No heat is exchanged (\(Q = 0\)) although the temperature changes, so \(C = \dfrac{Q}{n\Delta T} = 0\).

questions.q: A particle is subjected to two simple harmonic motions as: \(x_1 = \sqrt7\sin5t\) cm and \(x_2 = 2\sqrt7\sin\left(5t + \frac\pi3\right)\) cm where \(x\) is displacement and \(t\) is time in seconds. The maximum acceleration of the particle is \(x\times10^{-2}\) m s\(^{-2}\). The value of \(x\) is :
questions.sol: Resultant amplitude: \(A^2 = 7 + 28 + 2\sqrt7\cdot2\sqrt7\cos60^\circ = 49\), \(A = 7\) cm. \(a_{max} = \omega^2A = 25\times7 = 175\) cm/s² \(= 175\times10^{-2}\) m/s².

questions.q: Consider two infinitely large plane parallel conducting plates as shown below. The plates are uniformly charged with a surface charge density \(+\sigma\) and \(-2\sigma\). The force experienced by a point charge \(+q\) placed at the mid point between two plates will be:
questions.sol: Between the plates the fields add: \(E = \dfrac{\sigma}{2\epsilon_0} + \dfrac{2\sigma}{2\epsilon_0} = \dfrac{3\sigma}{2\epsilon_0}\). \(F = \dfrac{3\sigma q}{2\epsilon_0}\).

questions.q: A point charge \(+q\) is placed at the origin. A second point charge \(+9q\) is placed at \((d, 0, 0)\) in Cartesian coordinate system. The point in between them where the electric field vanishes is:
questions.sol: \(\dfrac{q}{x^2} = \dfrac{9q}{(d - x)^2} \Rightarrow d - x = 3x \Rightarrow x = \dfrac d4\).

questions.q: A small bob of mass 100 mg and charge \(+10\ \mu\)C is connected to an insulating string of length 1 m. It is brought near to an infinitely long non-conducting sheet of charge density '\(\sigma\)' as shown in figure. If string subtends an angle of 45° with the sheet at equilibrium the charge density of sheet will be. (Given, \(\epsilon_0 = 8.85\times10^{-12}\) F/m and acceleration due to gravity, \(g = 10\) m/s²)
questions.sol: \(\tan45^\circ = \dfrac{qE}{mg} \Rightarrow \dfrac{q\sigma}{2\epsilon_0} = mg = 10^{-3}\) N. \(\sigma = \dfrac{2\times8.85\times10^{-12}\times10^{-3}}{10^{-5}} = 1.77\times10^{-9}\) C/m².

questions.q: The battery of a mobile phone is rated as 4.2 V, 5800 mAh. How much energy is stored in it when fully charged?
questions.sol: \(E = VQ = 4.2\times5.8\times3600 \approx 87.7\times10^3\) J.

questions.q: Let \(B_1\) be the magnitude of magnetic field at center of a circular coil of radius \(R\) carrying current \(I\). Let \(B_2\) be the magnitude of magnetic field at an axial distance '\(x\)' from the center. For \(x : R = 3 : 4\), \(\frac{B_2}{B_1}\) is :

The relationship between the magnetic susceptibility (\(\chi\)) and the magnetic permeability (\(\mu\)) is given by : (\(\mu_0\) is the permeability of free space and \(\mu_r\) is relative permeability)
questions.sol: \(\mu = \mu_0(1 + \chi) \Rightarrow \chi = \dfrac{\mu}{\mu_0} - 1\).

questions.q: A light wave is propagating with plane wave fronts of the type \(x + y + z\) = constant. The angle made by the direction of wave propagation with the \(x\)-axis is :
questions.sol: The wave travels along the normal \((1, 1, 1)\): \(\cos\theta = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt3}\).

questions.q: A spherical surface separates two media of refractive indices 1 and 1.5 as shown in figure. Distance of the image of an object '\(O\)', is : (\(C\) is the center of curvature of the spherical surface and \(R\) is the radius of curvature)
o: 0.24 m left to the spherical surface
0.24 m right to the spherical surface
0.4 m left to the spherical surface
0.4 m right to the spherical surface
questions.sol: \(\dfrac{1.5}{v} - \dfrac{1}{-0.2} = \dfrac{1.5 - 1}{0.4} \Rightarrow \dfrac{1.5}{v} = 1.25 - 5 \Rightarrow v = -0.4\) m: 0.4 m to the left (virtual).

questions.q: A slanted object \(AB\) is placed on one side of convex lens as shown in the diagram. The image is formed on the opposite side. Angle made by the image with principal axis is :
questions.sol: A (\(u = -30\)): \(v = 60\) cm. B (\(u = -29\) cm, 2 cm high): \(v = \dfrac{20\times29}{9} \approx 64.4\) cm, image height \(= -2\times\dfrac{64.4}{29} \approx -4.4\) cm. The image rises 4.4 cm downward over 4.4 cm along the axis: \(-45^\circ\).

Considering Bohr's atomic model for hydrogen atom :
(A) the energy of H atom in ground state is same as energy of He\(^+\) ion in its first excited state.
(B) the energy of H atom in ground state is same as that for Li\(^{++}\) ion in its second excited state.
(C) the energy of H atom in its ground state is same as that of He\(^+\) ion for its ground state.
(D) the energy of He\(^+\) ion in its first excited state is same as that for Li\(^{++}\) ion in its ground state.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :

A monochromatic light is incident on a metallic plate having work function \(\phi\). An electron, emitted normally to the plate from a point A with maximum kinetic energy, enters a constant magnetic field, perpendicular to the initial velocity of electron. The electron passes through a curve and hits back the plate at a point B. The distance between A and B is : (Given : The magnitude of charge of an electron is \(e\) and mass is \(m\), \(h\) is Planck's constant and \(c\) is velocity of light. Take the magnetic field exists throughout the path of electron)
questions.sol: \(K = \dfrac{hc}{\lambda} - \phi\), \(r = \dfrac{mv}{eB} = \dfrac{\sqrt{2mK}}{eB}\). It lands after a semicircle: \(AB = 2r = \dfrac{\sqrt{8m(hc/\lambda - \phi)}}{eB}\).

questions.q: A zener diode with 5 V zener voltage is used to regulate an unregulated dc voltage input of 25 V. For a 400 Ω resistor connected in series, the zener current is found to be 4 times load current. The load current (\(I_L\)) and load resistance (\(R_L\)) are :
questions.sol: Series current \(= \dfrac{25 - 5}{400} = 50\) mA \(= I_Z + I_L = 5I_L\), so \(I_L = 10\) mA and \(R_L = \dfrac{5}{0.01} = 500\ \Omega\).

questions.q: A person travelling on a straight line moves with a uniform velocity \(v_1\) for a distance \(x\) and with a uniform velocity \(v_2\) for the next \(\frac32x\) distance. The average velocity in this motion is \(\frac{50}{7}\) m/s. If \(v_1\) is 5 m/s then \(v_2\) = ____ m/s.
questions.sol: Total distance \(\dfrac52x\), time \(\dfrac x5 + \dfrac{3x}{2v_2}\). \(\dfrac{5/2}{1/5 + 3/(2v_2)} = \dfrac{50}{7} \Rightarrow \dfrac15 + \dfrac{3}{2v_2} = \dfrac{7}{20} \Rightarrow v_2 = 10\) m/s.

questions.q: A steel wire of length 2 m and Young's modulus \(2.0\times10^{11}\) N m\(^{-2}\) is stretched by a force. If Poisson ratio and transverse strain for the wire are 0.2 and \(10^{-3}\) respectively, then the elastic potential energy density of the wire is ____ \(\times10^5\) (in SI units).
questions.sol: Longitudinal strain \(= \dfrac{10^{-3}}{0.2} = 5\times10^{-3}\). Energy density \(= \tfrac12Y\varepsilon^2 = \tfrac12\times2\times10^{11}\times25\times10^{-6} = 25\times10^5\) J/m³.

questions.q: A vessel with square cross-section and height of 6 m is vertically partitioned. A small window of 100 cm² with hinged door is fitted at a depth of 3 m in the partition wall. One part of the vessel is filled completely with water and the other side is filled with the liquid having density \(1.5\times10^3\) kg/m³. What force (in N) one needs to apply on the hinged door so that it does not get opened? (Acceleration due to gravity = 10 m/s²)
questions.sol: Pressure difference at 3 m depth \(= (1500 - 1000)\times10\times3 = 1.5\times10^4\) Pa. \(F = 1.5\times10^4\times10^{-2} = 150\) N.

questions.q: \(\gamma_A\) is the specific heat ratio of monoatomic gas A having 3 translational degrees of freedom. \(\gamma_B\) is the specific heat ratio of polyatomic gas B having 3 translational, 3 rotational degrees of freedom and 1 vibrational mode. If \(\frac{\gamma_A}{\gamma_B} = \left(1 + \frac1n\right)\), then the value of \(n\) is ____ .
questions.sol: \(\gamma_A = \dfrac53\). Gas B: \(f = 3 + 3 + 2 = 8\), \(\gamma_B = 1 + \dfrac28 = \dfrac54\). \(\dfrac{\gamma_A}{\gamma_B} = \dfrac43 = 1 + \dfrac13\), so \(n = 3\).

questions.q: If the measured angular separation between the second minimum to the left of the central maximum and the third minimum to the right of the central maximum is 30° in a single slit diffraction pattern recorded using 628 nm light, then the width of the slit is ____ μm.
questions.sol: Minima at \(a\sin\theta = n\lambda\); from \(n = -2\) to \(n = +3\) the separation is \(\dfrac{5\lambda}{a} = \dfrac\pi6\). \(a = \dfrac{6\times5\times628\times10^{-9}}{3.14} = 6\times10^{-6}\) m = 6 μm.
